full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J : In this rule nisi the petitioner called in question the legality of the judgment and decree dated 17-2-2004 (decree signed on 23-2- 2004, Annexure-D and E to the writ petition respectively) passed by the learned Judge of the Arrha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka in Altha Rin Suit No. 371 of 2003. The petitioner also challenged the initiation of the proceeding of Artha Jari Case No. 214 of 2007 without drawing up final decree as well as Order No.4 dated 29-11-2007 for issuance of sale proclamation without passing order of sale as required under Order XXI, rule 64 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the successive orders passed in the execution case.

2. The petitioner's case, in short, areas follows:

The petitioner is a director of Messrs Romana Industries Limited (thereinafter referred to as the Company). Respondent No.3 Md Altaf Uddin is the full brother of the petitioner and Managing Director of the Company. Respondent No.3 by misleading the petitioner managed to mortgage her properties fully described in the schedule of the plaint of Title Suit No. 45 of 2003. The Company obtained loan from respondent No.2. Rupali Bank Limited, Ibrahim Mansion Corporate Branch, 11 Purana Paltan, Dhaka (hereinafter stated as the Bank). The Bank instituted Title Suit No. 45 of 2003 on 21-4-2003 before the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 51,46,23 1.10 against the petitioner, the Company and its directors. After the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into operation, the said suit was renumbered as ArthaRin Suit No. 371 of 2003 before the Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka (the Adalat, in short). The petitioner had executed a deed of mortgage as well as a power of attorney in favour of the Bank as security of loan of Taka 20,000 only. In the deed of mortgage as well as the power of attorney address of the petitioner has been correctly described as under:

“মোসাম্মাৎ আফিফা সুলতানা, স্বামী- মোঃ লিয়াকত আলী খান, সাং- ১৮নং ইসদাইর রোড, থানা- ফতুল্লা, জেলা- নারয়ণগঞ্জ।”

3. The Bank fraudulently by giving false address of the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 45 of 2003 (renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No. 371 of 2003) and the summon of the suit was not served upon the petitioner. Therefore, the petitioner was not aware about the institution of the suit. However, the suit was decreed on contest against the Company  and other defendants and ex parte against the defendant-petitioner by judgment and decree dated 17-2-2004 (decree signed on 23-2-2004). The Bank there- after filed Artha Jari Case No. 214 Of 2007 on the basis of the preliminary decree signed on 23-2-2004 before the Adalat prior to drawing up of the final decree and the learned Judge of the Adalat directed to publish the auction sale notice by order dated 29- 11-2007 in the daily newspaper under section 33(1) of the Ain but no one participated in the auction. Eventually, on an application filed by the Bank for issuance of title under section 33(7) of the Ain, the learned Judge of the Adalat issued certificate of title by order dated 25-6-2009. The petitioner came to know about the suit and the proceeding of the execution case in the first week of March, 2010 from respondent No.3 (brother of the petitioner) and filed this writ petition.

4. Respondent No.2, the Bank contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying the material averments made in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that at the time of availing the loan, the petitioner signed and executed all necessary documents as director of the Company. The petitioner admitted that the loanee-company and other directors appeared and contested the Artha Rin Suit. It is hardly believable that she was not aware about the said suit as all other directors of the Company contested the suit. Summons were duly served upon the defendant-petitioner in accordance with law. Certificate of title has also been issued in favour of the Bank under section 33(7) of the Ain in accordance with law. The writ petition is misconceived, not maintainable and the rule is liable to be discharged.

5. The petitioner filed a supplementary affidavit stating that the deed of mortgage was executed and registered on 22-10-1994 between the petitioner as first party and respondent No.2 as second party providing additional security for a term loan amounting to Taka 20,000 and the petitioner mortgaged the property as additional security for an amount of Taka 20,000 and if, respondent Nos. 3 and 4 have not repaid the said term loan in the meantime, the petitioner is ready to pay the said amount of Taka 20,000 with interest in favour of the Bank.

6. The Bank filed an affidavit-in-reply that on prayer of the Company, the Bank, as a financial institution allowed term loan, cash credit (hypo), cash credit (pledge), L/C limit in favour of the Company. The petitioner is a director of the said Messrs Romana Industries Limited (the Company) and as security for repayment of the said loan; the petitioner mortgaged her property by executing registered deed of mortgage and power of attorney in favour of the Bank. The petitioner also created further charge for rest amount of the loan liabilities of the Company and created equitable mortgage by depositing relevant documents of her title with the Bank and signed and executed memorandum of deposit of Title Deeds. The Bank filed Title Suit No. 45 of 2003 before the Adalat against Messrs Romana Industries Limited and its directors for recovery of outstanding loan liabilities. Three addresses of the petitioner were mentioned in the cause title of the plaint, one is 16/1 Abul Hasnat Road, Satrowja, Police Station-Kotwali, Dhaka which is the registered address of Messrs Romana Industries Limited, another address is 171, Bhagalpur, Savar, Dhaka which is factory address of Messrs Romana Industries Limited and last one is 20/1, Abul Hasnat Road, Dhaka which has been given in the Memorandum and Articles of Association of Messrs Romana Industries Limited by the petitioner as her address. The summons of the Artha Rin Suit was duly served upon the defendants of Artha Rin Suit and three defendants including the Company, its Managing Director and others appeared in the suit. The suit was decreed on contest against the said defendants by judgment and decree dated 17-2-2004 (decree signed on 23-2-2004). After completion of all legal formalities the Bank filed Artha Jari Case No. 331 of 2004. Eventually, a certificate was issued in favour of the Bank under section 33(5) of the Ain. Subsequently, the Bank filed a second execution case being Artha Jari Case No. 214 of 2007 on 21-7-2009 and in the second execution case on prayer of the Bank certificate of title was issued in its favour under section 33(7) of the Ain which has already been registered with the office of sub-registrar. Narayangonj. The summons and the notices were duly served upon the petitioner in accordance with law and, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged.

7. Mr Md Asadullah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that on perusal of the plaint it is evident that the residential address of the defendant-petitioner was not given in the plaint of the suit as required under Order VII, rule 1(c) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code. in short), He next submits that the Bank intentionally avoided to mention the residential address of the petitioner which has been given in the deed of mortgage as well as in the power of attorney and the Bank obtained the Judgment and decree by fraudulent means. He further submits that the execution case filed after the preliminary decree and before the final decree illegally and therefore the execution proceeding is liable to be struck down. He next submits that direction for publishing auction sale notice of the mortgage property without passing any order of sale as required under Order XXI, rule 64 of the Code is illegal and it is liable to be struck down. He lastly submits that the petitioner is liable to pay Taka 20,000 with interest as per the terms of mortgage deed and she is willing to pay the same to save her property and necessary order may be passed accordingly.

8. In reply. Mr Md Imam Hasan, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 2 Bank has taken us through the plaint of the suit, deed of mortgage. power of attorney as well as the Memorandum and Articles of Association of Messrs Romana Industries Limited (shortly, the Memorandum) and contends that in the plaint three addresses of the petitioner were given and all those are correct addresses of the defendant-petitioner. He next con- tends that in the deed of mortgage number of holding was mentioned but in the power of attorney the number of holding was not given by the petitioner and therefore, to avoid confusion the Bank used the address of the petitioner as was given by her in the Memorandum of the Company. He further contends that the allegations that the Bank obtained decree by committing fraud upon the Adalat by using false address is not true and all the addresses given by the Bank in the plaint are correct addresses of the petitioner. He also contends that it has already been settled in a good number of cases by this Division that in an Artha Rin Suit an execution case may be filed after preliminary decree and after selling of the mortgage property the preliminary decree shall be made final. He next contends that writ petition against judgment and decree passed by Artha Rin Adalat is not maintainable as alternative forum of appeal is available under section 41 of the Ain. He further contends that admittedly two full brothers of the petitioner contested the suit and so, it is hardly believable that the petitioner was not aware about the suit and execution cases. He lastly contends that the proceeding of the Artha Jari Case No. 214 of 2007 is lawful and the rule is liable to be discharged.

9. We have examined the writ petition, supplementary affidavit, affidavit-in-opposition, affidavit-in-reply and the connected materials on record.

10. It is admitted proposition that the petitioner is a director of the Company, namely, Messrs Romana Industries Limited and her full brother respondent No.3 Md Altaf Uddin is the Managing Director of Messrs Romana Industries Limited. It is further admitted that the petitioner executed a deed of mortgage as well as a power of attorney in favour of the Bank empowering the Bank to sell the mortgage property as security of some loan obtained by Messrs Romana Industries Limited. Further that the Company and its directors as well as mortgagors having failed to repay the loan, the Bank filed Title Suit No. 45 of2003 on 21-4-2003 and subsequently, the said suit was renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No. 371 of 2003 before the Adalat. Admittedly out of four defendants three defendants including two full brothers of the petitioner contested the suit and only the petitioner did not contest the suit.

11. It has been alleged by the petitioner that she was not aware about the suit as a result of which she could not contest the suit. It has been further alleged that the other defendants did not inform the petitioner about the suit and the summon was not served upon her.

12. It has been stated in paragraph 7 of the writ petition that the plaintiff-Bank fraudulently by giving false address of the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 45 of 2003 renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No. 371 of 2003 as petitioner's address given in the deed of mortgage as well as a power of attorney was not used in the plaint of the suit.

13. The Bank categorically denied those allegations and stated that 16/1 Abul Hasnat Road. Satrowja, Police Station Kotwali. Dhaka is registered address of Messrs Romana Industries Limited and the second address 171 Bhagalpur, Savar, Dhaka is the factory address of Messrs Romana Industries Limited of which the petitioner is a director. The petitioner did not convert the said facts that the above addresses of the petitioner are the office address and factory address of Messrs Romana Industries Limited. Moreover those addresses were also used in the plaint as the address of other director-defendants who had contested the suit.

14. On careful scrutiny of the plaint of the suit (Annexure-A to the writ petition) it appears that the petitioner was defendant No.3 of the suit and her name and addresses in the plaint were given by the Bank as under:

“৩। মিসেস আফিফা সুলতানা, পিতা মৃত মহিউদ্দিন আহম্মদ, পরিচালক, মেসার্স রোমানা ইন্ড্রাষ্টিজলি:, ১৬/১ আবুল হাসনাত রোড, সাতরওজা, থানা- কোতয়ালী, জেলা- ঢাকা।

ও

১৭১, ভাগলপুর, সাভার, ঢাকা।

ও

২০/১ আবুল হাসনাত রোড, ঢাকা।”

15. The last address of the petitioner as given in the plaint by the Bank is 20/1, Abul Hasnat Road, Dhaka.

16. We have carefully examined the Memorandum of Messrs Romana Industries Limited (Annexure-2 to the affidavit- in-reply tiled by the Bank). It transpires that the registered address of the Company has not been used in the Memorandum of the Company. In this Memorandum the address of the petitioner is shown as 20/1 Abul Hasnat Road, Dhaka. Therefore, it transpires that the petitioner herself used this address to be her address in the Memorandum of Messrs Romana Industries Limited of which she is admittedly a director. As this address of the petitioner is not the official or factory address of the Company, it is possibly her residential address as she herself used this address.

17. In this case, the Bank used three correct addresses of the petitioner and the petitioner herself used her address as 20/1 Abul Hasnat Road, Dhaka in the Memorandum. It is true that the Bank could have also used the address of the petitioner which has been stated in the deed of mortgage as well as the power of attorney. But in the power of attorney holding number is absent in the place of address. We have already seen that the Bank used three addresses of the petitioner and, as such, we find no substance in the allegations that the Bank used false address of the petitioner in the plaint and obtained judgment and decree by fraudulent means. Rather, the petitioner made untrue statements in paragraph 7 of the writ petition about use of false address and has not come with clean hands to avail equitable relief in writ jurisdiction. Moreover, in writ jurisdiction it cannot be ascertained whether summons were duly upon the petitioner or not as the Bank claims that summons were served upon the petitioner. The question whether 20/1 Abul Hasnat Road, Dhaka is the residential address of the petitioner or whether 18, lshdhair Road, Fatullah, Narayangonj is the residential address of the petitioner or whether the petitioner is Hable for Taka 20,000 with interest are all disputed questions of facts which cannot be decided in the writ jurisdiction without proper evidence.

18. It has been decided in the cases of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank LId reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, Gazi M Towfiq vs Agrani Bank, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6, Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation vs Artha Rin Adalat, reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6 and Edruk Limited vs Secretary. Ministry of Industries, reported in 14 BLC 102 and in a good number of cases by the Appellate Division as well as High Court Division that a writ petition is not maintainable against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat as alternative forum of appeal is available under section 41 of the Ain.

19. By now it is a settled principle of law that a judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot be challenged in writ jurisdiction except coramnon-judice or fraud committed upon Adalat in obtaining the judgment and the decree.

20. In this case it is not disputed that the learned Judge of the Adalat had lawful jurisdiction to pass the impugned judgment and decree. The question as to whether the judgment and decree has been obtained by practicing fraud upon the Adalat is a disputed question of fact which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. Moreover, the petitioner failed to prove any apparent fraud committed by the Bank in obtaining the judgment and decree. Therefore challenging of the judgment and decree in writ jurisdiction is not maintainable.

21. The next question is whether the execution case may be tiled after preliminary decree.

22. It has been decided by this Division by judgment dated 29-8-2007 passed in Writ Petition No. 3672 of 2004 in consideration of the provisions of section 5(3)(4) of the Ain that in a suit for recovery of loan by sell of mortgage property, the decree shall be deemed to be a final decree only when the property mortgaged in favour of the plaintiff is sold in auction in accordance with the decree and filing of an execution case after the preliminary decree is lawful.

23. Thus, we find no substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that filing of the execution case after preliminary decree is unlawful.

<u>24. The last question is whether auction sale notice may be published before passing an order of sale under Order XXI, rule 64 of the Code. The Ain is a special law providing special procedure for auction sale of the mortgaged property under section 33 of the Ain. Therefore, under section 33(1) of the Ain, the Adalat is empowered to pass an order for publishing auction sale notice of the mortgage property directly and the provision of Order XXI, rule 64 of the Code is not applicable relating to auction sale in Artha Ain Execution Cases.</u>

25. Therefore, the impugned order dated 29- 11-2007 and the subsequent orders passed by the learned Judge of the Adalat in Artha Jari Case No. 214 of 2007 cannot be said to be without lawful authority.

26. At the end of the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is now willing to file application before the Bank to settle the matter with the Bank.

27. Amicable settlement out of the executing Adalat is possible during pendency of an execution case under section 38 of the Ain.

28. Be that as it may, for filing any application before the Bank no permission is required from this Court.

29. In view of discussions made in the forgoing paragraphs vis-a-vis the law, we find no merit in this rule. Accordingly, the rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

The order of stay granted earlier by the Court stands vacated.

Communicate the judgment to respondent No. 1 at once.

End.

lawyer:
Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate, instructed by SR Khoshnabish, 
Advocate-on-Record------  For the Appellant.
 Ex parte------ Respondents
parties:
Abdur Rashid Mollah ------ Appellant
vs.
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Works and Urban Development and another ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 25th May 2000 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 50 of 1996).
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: This appeal by leave at the instance of the writ petitioner is directed against the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.50 of 1996 affirming those of the respondent No. 2 i.e. the Court of Settlement, in Case No. 11 of 1989 in respect of House No. 24/10, Block-C, Tajmahal Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka.

2. The case of the appellant is that the case property previously belonged to Abdul Hafiz who got the same from the Government of the then East Pakistan by registered deed of lease dated 15-1-69 and constructed a tin shed house and lived there. The said Abdul Hafiz entered into an agreement on 20-12-71 with the appellant to sell the same to the appellant on receipt of Taka 13,500 as advance out of total consideration .money of Taka 15,000 and delivered possession of the same to the appellant on the same day as part performance of the agreement for sale Before the execution of the deed. Abdul Hafiz died in January 1972 leaving behind three legal heirs and successors namely, wife Hazera Khatun, daughter Baby Tabasun (minor) and son Md Kalim (minor). A succession certificate was issued in Succession Certificate Case No. 620 of 1978 by Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in support of aforesaid heirs and successors of deceased Abdul Hafiz. On 9-11-78 wife of deceased, Abdul Hafiz namely, Hazera Khatun, affirmed an affidavit before Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka declaring that she was a permanent resident of Bangladesh and also declared her intention to live in Bangladesh along with her entire family members for the remaining period of her life. On being refused by the successors of the deceased Abdul Hafiz on 20-11-78 to execute and register the deed of sale in respect of the suit property the appellant filed Title Suit No. 596 of 1978 before learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for specific performance of contract in which respondent No: 2 Government of Bangladesh was. a party. The suit was decreed ex parte on 8-11-79 against which respondent No.2 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 187 of 1979 for setting aside the said, ex parte decree before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka who after hearing, by order dated 26-12-80 dismissed the case. Thereafter, the appellant filed Title Execution Case No.1 of 1981 before learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for execution of the said ex parte decree who after hearing by order dated 13-4-81 allowed the said execution case and executed and registered the deed of sale being No. 9921 dated 13- 4-81 in favour of the appellant. The appellant thereafter prayed for mutation of the property in his name to the Assistant Commissioner, Settlement Directorate of Housing and Urban Development. On 30-11-83, a high-powered survey team of the Ministry of Public Works after survey of the house made a report with the remark that the property might not be treated as an abandoned property. Thereafter, the Administrative Officer, Mohammadpur Housing Estate sent a report dated 10-10-84 to the Assistant Commissioner, Settlement admitting the facts as stated with an observation that the appellant was in possession of the property by way of lawful purchase. Thereafter, the respondent No. 2 again filed Miscellaneous Case No. 183 of 1986 before learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for setting aside the aforesaid ex parte decree, which was dismissed for default on 7-2-89. The appellant claimed to have been in continuous peaceful possession of the suit property since 20-12-71 and was never dispossessed therefrom. The Government was never in possession of the property and the same was not leased out to anybody treating the same as an abandoned property at any point of time since 28-2-72. The appellant was surprised to know that the property was included in the "Ka" list as abandoned property by notification in the official Gazette on 28-11-85 under section 5 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985. The appellant filed an application under said Ordinance to exclude the property from "Ka" list of abandoned properties before the Court of Settlement which after hearing the case dismissed the application with the findings that the whereabouts of the owner was not known, that he had been residing in a country which was at war with Bangladesh and that' the owner ceased to occupy, supervise or manage the property.

3. The appellant, being aggrieved by the judgment, filed the writ petition before the High Court Division which discharged the Rule upon finding, inter alia; that the appellant had filed only the photo copy of the lease deed of Abdul Hafiz and no other basic documents. The certified copy of the original deed was obtained on 22-8-78. He also did not file the deed of agreement for sale and simply said that he lost the agreement while returning from the Assistant Commissioner's Office on 25-10-84 after showing him all the documents. The Court of Settlement did not believe this story that he informed the police about it by filling an entry in the police diary. He produced a photo copy of the GDE which the Court of Settlement held was not proved by calling for Original from the police station. The record of the case was called from the Assistant Commissioner's Office where he filed all the photocopies except bainapatra and he did not complain about losing the bainapatra in the office of Housing and Settlement. With regard to the suit for specific performance of contract and execution of the registered, sale deed, the High Court Division referred to the case reported in 47 DLR (AD) 71 where it was held that in a suit for specific performance of contract the dispute between the vendor and the vendee is decided, and it does not exclude the property from being an abandoned property. Further, the appellant could not produce the sheet anchor of his claim i.e. the bainapatra, and "it is a mystery how the original succession certificate came to the hand of the petitioner where his claim was resisted by Abdul Hafiz". The High Court Division therefore, discharged the Rule.

4. Leave was granted to consider the point raised by the learned Counsel for the appellants that from the admitted position, apart from the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 596 of 1978 that the petitioner is in possession of the property since 1978 and the possession having not been taken over by the Government, the listing of the property in "Ka" list is contrary to section 5 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (LIV of 1985) and is illegal. The High Court Division failed to appreciate that the inclusion of the property in "Ka" list without any notice as contemplated under President's Order 16 of 1972 read with section 5 of the Ordinance LIV of 1985 was without lawful authority. It was further submitted that the case property 'being enlisted in the "Ka" list of the Gazette, although the petitioner had been on the property since 1971 on the strength of bainapatra and subsequent decree, and no notice having been given to the petitioner before enlisting of the properties in the Gazette, the inclusion of the case property in the list was without lawful authority and, in support, a decision of this Division in the case of Bangladesh vs Amena Khatun and others reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55 has been referred.

5. Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that from the admitted position that the appellant is in possession of the property since 17-12-1971 which he got from the admitted owner MA Hafiz, apart from the decree for specific performance of contract in Title Suit No. 596 of 1978 in which he obtained the registered deed executed and registered through Court, the possession not having been taken over by the Government, the listing of the property in 'Ka' schedule is contrary to the provision of section 5(1)(Ka) of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 (No. LIV of 1985). The learned Counsel has further submitted that after appropriate proceeding under Articles 7 and 15 of President's Order No.16 of 1972 and under section 5 of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985, the inclusion of the building in 'Ka' list without any notice as contemplated therein is illegal and is without any lawful authority: The learned Counsel has referred to the above decision in the case of Bangladesh vs Amena Khatun and others reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55.

6. Article 7 of President's Order No.16 of 1972 provides that the Deputy Commissioner shall take possession of the property where any abandoned property is not in possession of the owner by service of notice asking him to surrender the possession to the Deputy Commissioner or his agent within 7 days of the service of the order, and where he fails to surrender the Deputy Commissioner shall serve the notice on him in a prescribed form requiring him to surrender the property within 7 days of the notice and to show cause against such surrender within such period, if he fails to do so the Deputy Commissioner shall take possession of the same.

7. Article 15 provides that any person claiming any right or interest may within 3 months of the announcing of the order claiming any interest or right therein treated by the Government as abandoned property may make an application stating that this property is not an abandoned property and his interest has not been affected by the provision of the said order. Admittedly, in the instant case no notice under Article 7 was served so as to entitle the appellant from challenging the order treating the property as abandoned.

8. Rule 5 of Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 as well provides that the property of which possession has already been taken by the Government as abandoned property could only be listed in the 'Ka' schedule under section 5(1)(a) of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985, but in the instant case admittedly, the possession has been lying althrough with the appellant. The High Court. Division has not at all adverted its attention to the fact that according to clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 5 of the Abandoned Property (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance 1985, abandoned property in possession of the Government could only be included in the "Ka" list of abandoned building in respect of which possession has been taken by issuance of notice under Article 7 of President's Order No.16 of 1972.

<u>9. Although the appellant could not produce the bainapatra in original which the appellant is alleged to have lost and in support thereof had filed a GD. Entry but the said bainapatra was the subject-matter of Title Suit No. 596 of 1978 which was decreed ex parte and the appellant obtained document executed and registered through Court and the respondent No. 2 as well filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.183 of 1986 before the Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Dhaka for setting aside the aforesaid decree which was dismissed for default on 7-2-1989. Admittedly, the appellant has been claiming to be in continuous peaceful possession of the suit property since 20-12-1971 and was never dispossessed and he was also never issued with any notice to surrender. It further appears that the Government-respondents did not take any step to take over the possession of the same till publication of the Gazette notification on 23-9-1985. It further appears that even after publication of the Gazette notification the Government was aware of the decree in respect of the property in favour of the appellant and filed Miscellaneous Case No. 183 of 1986 before the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Dhaka for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 8-11-1979 in respect of the case building. Since there was no notice contemplated under Article 7 and there was non-compliance of the provision of section 5 of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 as no notice under section 5(1)(a) of the Ordinance was ever served and, as such, the property was wrongly included in the 'Ka' list of the abandoned buildings and the listing, as such, undoubtedly has been done illegally and without any lawful authority. This view finds support in the case referred to by the learned Counsel for the appellant in the case of Bangladesh vs Amena Khatun reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55.</u>

The appeal is accordingly, allowed without any order as to costs.

End.

lawyer: ASM Abdur Razzaque, Advocate----- For the Appellant.
parties:
Uttara Bank Ltd ----- Plaintiff-appellant
Vs.
Gazi Nazim Uddin and others ----- Defendant-respondents
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: This appeal at the instance of Appellant, Uttara Bank Ltd. is directed against the judgment and decree dated 16-8-1998 (decree signed on 23-8-1998) passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka so far it relates to Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 decreeing the suit in-part.

2. The material facts of the case as necessary for disposal of this appeal are that appellant, Uttara Bank as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 before the sub-Judge & 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka for recovery of Taka 3,40,21,750 against the defendants including interest and changes on 9-11- 1992. The facts of the case in brief are that at the request of defendant No.2, Gazi Nazimuddin, proprietor of M/S Gazi Nazimuddin (borrower), Uttara Bank Limited opened a Letter of credit being L/C No. UBL/WES/BF/86/159 on 2-10-1986 for US $ 10,87,500 equivalent to Taka 3,61,05,000 with 10% Margin for importing 1,500 MT Powder; that the plaintiff, Uttara Bank upon receipt of the shipping documents under the L/C on 9-10-1986, made payment of Taka 3,28,80,162 to the negotiating bank and requested to defendant No.2, to release the shipping documents upon payment of the same, but the defendants failed to release the documents: that the defendant No. 2 vide letter dated 20-10-1986 requested the plaintiff-Bank to send the original shipping documents of C&F Agent for assessment of the goods. In this backdrop, Uttara Bank received letter dated 14-12-1986 from the C&F Agent that the goods will be sold in auction unless the same are release from the port and the defendant No.2 vide letter dated 6-1-1987 requested the Bank to allow him to release of the goods and storing the same in his Godown and to adjust the loan liabilities by February 15, 1987. Thereafter, the plaintiff Bank sanctioned LlM facilities of Taka 3,35,95,703 in favour of the defendant Nos. 1-2 (borrowers) by creating LlM Account No. 7 on 9-2-1987 and goods were ultimately released from the port and stored in the Godown of the defendant Nos. 1-2; that plaintiff Bank vide letter dated 3-5-1987 requested the defendant No.2 to take delivery of entire goods from the Godown and pay the dues to Uttara Bank; that a burglary was committed in the Godown and approximately 120/150 bags of milk powder were lifted from the Godown and the same has been informed to the defendants on 8-4-1987 and then imported Milk powders were seized by the Double Mooring Police on 18-4-1987 and the same were ultimately returned on 3-5-1987 since milk powers have been found suitable for human consumption. The defendant-borrower vide letter dated 4-5-1987 requested to the plaintiff, Uttara Bank for sanction of further TR Facility which was not ultimately granted by Uttara Bank and thereupon, the defendant Nos. 1-2 vide letter dated 13-9-1987 admitted taking delivery of 30,000 bags of milk powder without obtaining delivery order from the plaintiff, Uttara Bank Limited; that the plaintiff-Uttara Bank vide its letter dated 10-10-1987 requested the defendants to adjust its loan liability, but the defendants did not come forward to adjust the same. Under this circumstances the plaintiff-Bank under legal obligation served Legal Notice dated 3-5-1992 through its lawyer requesting the borrowers/mortgagor/guarantor to pay the loan liability in the LIM account No. 7 and also other accounts the defendant-respondents did not turn to adjust the loan facility. Hence the suit.

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing joint written statements denying most of the allegations of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that due to the intentional fault of the plaintiff-Bank the defendants failed to run their business and thereby they could not adjust the entire amount against the credit facility. It is also contended in the amended written statements that the representative of defendant-company, Monsur Khan in collusion with Bank officials misappropriated the pledged goods.

4. At the trial both the parties led evidence to prove their respective cases. The plaintiff-Bank examined 2 (two) witnesses namely, PW 1 and PW 2 and the defendant side also examined 2 (two) witnesses namely, DW 1 and DW 2 and both the parties produced documents in support of their respective claims.

5. The learned judge of the Artha Rin Adalat upon hearing the parties and on considering the materials on record by a single judgment dated 16- 8-1998 decided 3 (three) suits namely, Title Suit No. 128 of 1992, Title Suit No. 129 of 1992 and Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 in which decreed the instant Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 in part in deducting the claim of the bank including the claim of interest pendente lite.

6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 16-8-1998, the plaintiff-Bank as appellant preferred the instant First Appeal so far it relates to judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 but no appeal has been filed on behalf of the defendant-respondents (judgments debtors).

7. Mr ASM Abdur Razzaque, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellant-Bank submits that the Artha Rin Adalat committed gross illegality in deducting the claim of the bank including the claim of interest pendente lite, that is, from the data of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the decree. He next in the course of his argument upon placing the impugned judgment and decree, deposition of witnesses and statement of accounts, plaint, written statement and other materials on record submits that the judge of the Adalat in its judgment dated 16-8-1998 observed that admittedly, the Bank received Taka 50,00,00,000 on 16-9-1987, Taka 4,31,852 on 1-11-1987, Taka 4,50,000 on 2-11-1987, Taka 1,00,000 on 3-11-1987, Taka 6,800 on 26-12-1989 totaling Taka 59,88,652 and accordingly deducted the said amount from the decreed amount, but the learned trial Judge failed to consider the fact that the said amount was deducted from the claim of the Bank before filing the suit and the same has been reflected in the statement of Accounts (exhibit-16) and as such the impugned judgments so far it relates to deduction as well as pendente lite, interest is liable to be set aside.

8. Mr Razzaque, further that in the facts and circumstances of the case the Artha Rin Adalat ought to have allowed interest pendente lite, that is, from the date of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the judgment and decree. The learned Advocate to fortify his contention has relied on the decisions reported in 2 BLC (AD) 173, 54 DLR 458. AIR 1935 (Patna) 98, AIR 1953 (Born) 445 and AIR 1957 (Cal) 140.

9. Drawing to our attention to the affidavit dated 25-5-2011 Mr Razzaque, finally submits that so far the knowledge of the appellant-Bank, the defendant-respondents did not prefer any appeal against the judgment and decree dated 16-8-1998 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 129 of 1992.

10. No one has entered appearance on behalf of the defendant-respondents to oppose the appeal.

We have heard the learned Advocate for the appellant-Bank and perused the Memorandum of Appeal, impugned judgment and decree dated 16-8-1998, deposition of witnesses, plaint of the Artha Rin Suit No. 130 of 1992, written statement filed by the defendant Nos. 2 and 3, statement of accounts of the plaintiff-Bank and other materials on record. The only material question for consideration in this case is, whether the Artha Rin Adalat committed any illegality in not allowing interest pendente lite, that is, from the date of institution of the suit up to the date of passing the decree.

11. .Now, in order to resolve this dispute, let us see the cited decisions as well as the relevant provisions of law in this regard.

12. In the case of Sonali Bank vs Beg and Beg Jute Incorporated Ltd reported in 2 BLC (AD) 173, wherein our Appellate Division on considering a number of decisions of the Superior Courts of this sub-continent held that the High Court Division acted illegally in not holding that the plaintiff-appellant was entitled to get interest pendente lite, that is, from the date of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the decree.

13. In the case of Surajmal Marwari vs Huro Rai reported in AIR 1935 Patna 98, it was held that Order 34, Rule (2) and (4) deal respectively with a decree in a mortgage suit for foreclosure and for sale, and the words used in the rules seem to me to infer that the question of interest up to the date of the decree is one which is not within the discretion of the Court.

14. In the case of Nilmoni Sarker vs Baidyanath Das Manna reported in AIR 1957 Cal 140, it was held that the Court is bound to decree pendente lite interest, it being left to the discretion of the Court at what rate it is to be allowed. The circumstance of each particular case is to be taken into consideration.

15. In the case of Pubali Bank Ltd vs Md Mamunur Rahman reported in 54 DLR 458, it has been held as follows:

"Since the loan was not denied, since the loan limit of Taka 11 lakh was enjoyed by the defendant No. 1 illegally without proper pledge and since the loan was not repaid, we do not see any reason, not to allow the claim of interest of the Bank for the rest of the period since July 1987 to February, 1988, for the total amount of Taka 16,45,750, we however, would allow simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum pendente lite till realization".

16. In this connection the relevant provisions of law are required to be referred to for having a better view of the dispute in question. Order XXXIV, rule 2 CPC reads as follows:

(1) In suit for foreclosure, if the plaintiff succeeds, the Court pass a preliminary decree-

(a) ordering that an account be taken of what was due to the plaintiff at the date of such decree for-

(i) principal and interest on the mortgage, (ii) the costs of suit, if any, awarded to him, and

(iii) other costs, charges and expenses properly incurred by him up to that date in respect of his mortgage- security, together with interest thereon;

or

(b) 	declaring the amount so due at the date; and

.....................................................................................

17. 	Order XXXIV, rule 11 CPC reads as follows:

In any decree passed in a suit for foreclosure, sale or redemption, where interest is legally recoverable, the Court may order payment of interest to the mortgage as follows, namely-

(a) interest up to the date on or before which payment of the amount found or declared due is under the preliminary decree to be made by the mortgagor or other person redeeming the mortgage-

(i) on the principal amount found or declared due on the mortgage,at the rate payable on the principal, or, where no such rate is fixed, at such rate as the Court deems reasonable,

(ii) on the amount of the costs of the suit awarded to the mortgage, at such rate as the Court deems reasonable from the date of the preliminary decree, and

(iii) on the amount adjudged due to the mortgagee for costs, charges and expenses properly incurred by the mortgagee in respect of the mortgage-security up to the date of the preliminary decree and added to the date of the preliminary decree and added to the mortgage money,at the rate agreed between the parties, or, failing such rate, at the same rate as is payable on the principal, or failing both such rates, at nine percent per annum; and

(b) subsequent interest up to the date of realization or actual payment at such rate as the Court deems reasonable-

(i) on the aggregate of the principal sums specified in clause (a) and of the interest thereon as calculated in accordance with that clause; and

(ii) on the amount adjudged due to the mortgagee in respect of such further costs, charges and expenses as may be payable under rule 10.

18. From a reading of the above quoted provision of Order XXXIV, rule 2 &11 of the Code of Civil Procedure together with the decisions namely the decisions reported in 2 BLC (AD) 173, 54 DLR 458, AIR 1957 Cal 140, AIR 1935 Patna 98 and AIR 1953 Bombay 445, we find a clear view of law as it stands today that the pendente lite interest is in the discretion of the Court which may not grant interest at the contractual rate and reduce it when under the circumstances it is excessive and unfair but cannot refuse it altogether. In any decree passed in a suit foreclosure, sale or redemption, where interest is legally recoverable, the Court cannot refuse to allow any pendente lite interest.

19. On going through the deposition of DW and DW 2, we find nothing in their evidence to suggest that the bank authority in collusion with Mansur Khan, the representative of Nazimuddin, defendant No.2 misappropriated the pledge goods and thereupon, the defendant Gazi Nazimuddin has been made scapegoat. Further, it is found from the evidence of DW 1 and DW 2 that at the time of trial the defendant No.2, Gazi Nazimuddin was not sick but the reasons best known to him as to why he did not turn to depose in the suit. It is also found that admittedly the defendants failed to adjust the loan facility and the Managing Director of the defendant-company due to various reasons failed to run their business.

<u>20. On consideration of the matter vis-a-vis the decision reported in 2 BLC (AD) 173 and Order XXXIV, rule 2 & 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. we are led to hold that in the facts and circumstances of the case the Artha Rin Adalat ought to have allowed interest pendente lite, that is, from the date of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the decree since the suit is a mortgaged suit for recovery of money by sale of the mortgaged property.</u>

21. On an overall consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the legal position, we are of the opinion that the interest of justice will be served if the defendant-respondents are directed to pay interest at the rate of 8% decreetal sum pendente lite, i.e., from the date of institution of the suit till the date of decree.

Accordingly, the appeal succeeds.

22. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree 16-8-1998 (decree signed on 23-8-1998) passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court,Dhaka in Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 so far it relates to interest pendente lite is set-aside.

23. Hence, it is ordered that the defendant-respondents are directed to pay the entire amount in terms of decree along with interest at the rate of 8% on the decreetal sum pendente life, that is, from the date of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the decree.

Let a copy of this judgment along with lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 1172 of 2010
lawyer:
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, instructed by Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners (in both cases) 
Qumrul Haque Siddique, Advocate ----- For Respondent No.16. (in both cases) 
Respondent Nos.1-15 & 17-420 (in both cases) ----- None represented.
parties:
Ruhul Amin and others ----- Petitioners (in C.P No.1172 of 10)
Habibur Rahman and others ----- Petitioners (in C.P. No.1173 of 10)
Vs.
Johara Begum and others ----- Respondents (in both cases)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 21st day of March, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5384 of 2003).
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. These two leave petitions have arisen out of the same judgment and order dated the 21st day of March, 2010 passed by the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5384 of 2003 discharging the Rule.

2. Facts, necessary for disposal of the leave petitions, are as follows:

3. Respondent Nos.1-16 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.274 of 1998 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, First Court, Comilla for partition of the suit land impleading the petitioner of these leave petitions and the order respondents as defendants. The suit was contested by defendant Nos.107, 108 and 109 by filing written statement.

4. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that they became owners of the suit land by was of inheritance from their predecessor, Oli Mohammad and also by purchase. As the plaintiffs were facing difficulties in enjoying the suit property in ejmali, they requested the defendants for petition of the same which they denied raising dispute regarding their title as well as the kabala; hence the suit.

5. The contesting defendants in their written statement took the plea that the suit land was the self acquired property of Boli Mohammad and therefore, the plaintiffs who were the heirs of Oli Mohammad had no title in the suit land and as such, were not entitled to partition of the same, the suit was liable to be dismissed.

6. Both parties adduced evidence, oral and documentary. The learned Subordinate Judge by the judgment and dated 19.11.1992 decreed the suit in part against defendant Nos.1, 4-8, 11, 12, 70-72, 94-100 and 120 on contest and ex-parte against others. The contesting defendants preferred appeal before the District Judge, Comilla against the said judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge being Title Appeal No.22 of 1993. The Appellate Court allowed the appeal and sent the suit back on remand to the trial Court with direction to include the entire land of plot Nos.787 and also to impaled the other co-sharers in the suit.

7. After remand, the suit was transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla and was renumbered as Title Suit No.4 of 1998. The suit was again decreed by the trial Court by judgment and decree dated 28.02.1999 giving saham to the plaintiffs and also to the other defendants as well. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the contesting defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 278 of 1999 before the District Judge, Comilla. The learned Additional District Judge, Fifth Court, Comilla who heard the appeal by the judgment and decree dated 23.09.2003 dismissed the same. Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the defendant-petitioners herein (the numbers of the defendants were not mentioned in the cause title of the revision application) filed Civil Revision No. 5384 of 2003 before the High Court Division. A Single Bench hearing the revision by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule; hence these petitions for leave to appeal by the sets of defendants (number of the defendants has defendants has not been mentioned in the cause title of the leave petitions).

8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned counsel, appearing for the petitioners in both petitions, has submitted that Oli Mohammad was not a co-sharer of the suit land and as such, the suit for partitioning the same by the plaintiffs claiming title through him was not maintainable. He has further submitted that the Courts below completely misinterpreted exhibits-'Uma' and 'Uma(1)' in deciding the issue of res-judicata and the learned Judge of the Single Bench also failed to decide the issue with reference to the said exhibits wherein it was decided that Oli Mohammad was not a co-sharer in the suit land and therefore, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. He has further submitted that Ramjan Ali, son of Oli Mohammad, father of the plaintiffs purchased some land from the heirs of Boli Mohammad vide exhibit-7 before the S.A record and accordingly, the S.A Record was in the names of the plaintiffs as heirs of Ramjan Ali on the basis of exhibit-7 not as the heirs of Oli Mohammad, but the Courts below misread exhibit-7 and without considering the pleading of the defendants decreed the suit giving sham to the plaintiffs as the heirs of Oli Mohammad and the High Court Division also failed to consider this aspect of the case and thus erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and order affirming those of the Appellate Court. Mr. Bhuian has further submitted that the Appellate Court reversed the divisible sham given by the trial Court which was not challenged by the plaintiffs by was of cross objection and as such, the Appellate Court erred in law in reducing the share of Boli Mohammad to the extent of 2.44 acres. He has lastly submitted that the High Court Division, without discussing the contradictory findings of the Courts below as to the co-shareship of Oli Mohammad in the suit land, affirmed those of the Appellate Court and thus, erred in law in discharging the Rule and as such, the impugned and order calls for interference by this Division.

9. Mr. Qumrul Haque Siddique, learned Advocate, entering caveat on behalf of respondent No. 16, has submitted that the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order as the points raised by the defendant-petitioners were found concurrently by the Courts against them and being no merit in the leave petitions, the same be dismissed.

10. From the pleading of the contesting parties as well as the prayer made by the other defendants for saham, the whole controversy in the suit was as to whether the suit property of 3 C.R. khatians being Nos.9, 18 and 63 were the joint property of Boli Mohammad or the self acquired property of Boli Mohammad as claimed by the contesting contesting defendants.

11. From the judgment and decree of the trial Court as well as the Appellate Court, it appears that the doing of maintainability of the suit on the ground that the complicated question of title being involved, the suit for petition was not maintainable, was raised by the contesting defendants and both Court held that the suit was maintainable on the finding that in a suit for partition, question of title can incidentally be gone in to. In holding so, the Courts below relied on two decision of this Division, the cases being Md. Sultan Mia and others-vs-Hajera Bibi and others, 1984 BLD(AD)23 and Sanjib Kumar Bose and another-vs-Syed Shamsuddin Ahmed and another, 33 DLR(AD)347. Mr. Wadud Bhuiyan has not also disputed this proposition of law and hold that in the facts and circumstances of the case, the Court below took the correct decision in finding the suit maintainable.

12. Mr. Wadud Bhuiyan relying on the earlier judgment passed in the Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No.319 of 1939(exhibit-'Uma') as well as Title Suit No.65 of 1959 of the then Munsif, Second Court, Comilla vehemently argued that those judgments, if read carefully, would go to show that plaintiffs failed to prove that they had any interest in the suit land as co-sharers being the heirs of Oli Mohammad and thus, it was proved that suit property was the self acquired property of Boli Mohammad. Therefore, the High Court Division was wrong in not interfering with judgment and decree of the Appellate Court.

13. From the judgment and decree and decree of the trial Court, it appears that the issue of res-judicata was framed in the suit. The trial Court considering the order passed in the pre-emption miscellaneous case (exhibit-'Uma') found that in the order, clear finding was given to effect that without holding local investigation, it was not possible to decide whether the pre-emptoes had title in the case land; the decision given in the pre-emption case shall not act as a res-judicata in a properly constituted suit for title. The trial Court further found that in the pre-emption miscellaneous case, no issue as to the title to the suit land was framed. It further appears that Title Suit No.65 of 1959 was filed in the Court of Munsif, Second Court against the order dated 15.09.1947 passed in Miscellaneous Mutation Case No.422 of 1947 by which Ramjan Ali, predecessor of the plaintiffs, got his name mutated in respect of the part of the suit land. The suit was decreed and the decree was upheld in second appeal. The Trial Court considering the order dated 15.09.1947 passed in the miscellaneous mutation case (exhibit-'Uma-1') found that in the miscellaneous case no issue of title was involved. The trial Court further held that the proceedings of both cases were summary and the suit land involved in the said two proceedings were not same. On such findings and observations, the trial Court came to the finding that the suit was not barred under the principle of res-judicata. The Appellate Court also affirmed the said view of the trial Court. Mr. Bhuiyan could not show before us that in the said two proceedings, title to the suit land of the plaintiffs as the heirs of Oli Mohammad was decided.

14. From the judgment of the courts below it further appears that both Courts below elaborately considered the evidence adduced by the respective party oral and came to the finding that the suit land was acquired both by Boli Mohammad, two full brothers and the plaintiffs being of Oli Mohammad, they were entitled to partition the suit land.

15. From the Appellate Court judgment, it appears that the Appellate Court interfered with judgment and decree of the trial Court so far as it relates to the share of the heirs of Boli Mohammad. The trial Court excluded 2.44 acres of land from the share of the plaintiffs on the view that since 4.88 acres of land from C.R. khatian No. 18 of plot Nos. 233/3, 237 and 220 was sold in Execution Case No. 28 of 1931 pursuant to the decree passed in Rehan Title Suit No.79 of 1993, the said area of land should be excluded from the share of both brothers in equal share on the view that the land was mortgaged by Boli Mohammad on his own behalf and on behalf of his brother, Oli Mohammad. The Appellate Court on consideration of bainanama, exhibit-'kha' came to the clear finding that the execution case was filed against the heirs of Boli Mohammad and auction was held against the heirs of Boli Mohammad only which facts were admitted by the contesting defendants in their written statement. The Appellate Court excluded the entire auction sold from C.R. khatian No.18 from the share of the heirs of Boli Mohammad on the view that since the execution case was filed against the heirs of Boli Mohammad only, the plaintiffs being the heirs of Boli Mohammad could not be saddled with the liability of the auction sale. Mr. Wadud Bhuiyan could not show that the heirs of Oli Mohammad were the judgment debtors in the Rehan suit and that in the execution case in which 4.88 acres of land from C.R. khatian No.18, they were parties. Therefore, we find nothing wrong with the Appellate Court in excluding the entire auction sold 4.88 acres of land from the share of the heirs of Boli Mohammad.

<u>16. The other objection taken by Mr. Bhuiyan that since the plaintiffs did not file any cross objection against the deduction of 2.44 acres of land from their share being half of the auction sold property, the Appellate Court was not justified in interfering with the said finding of the trial Court has got no substance inasmuch as rule 33 of Order XLI of the Code of Civil Procedure has clearly empowered the Appellate Court to interfere with a decree of the trial Court if in view of the pleading of the parties and the evidence on record such decree calls for modification and alteration even the respondent has not preferred an appeal or cross-objection.</u>

17. In view of the discussions made above, we do not see any merit in the petitions. Accordingly, the petitions are dismissed.

End.

lawyer:

parties:
Umme Hani Begum and ors ------ Defendant-Appellants
VS
Ram Gopal Sarker and others ------ Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
Shahidul Islam J: This First Appeal has arisen out of the judgment and decree dated 12-11-1998 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj, in Title Suit No. 344 of 1994 decreeing the suit.

2. The respondent No.2 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 344 of 1994 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj, for declaration of title by way of acquisition of title by adverse possession and also for a further declaration that the registered kabala deed dated 16-4-1969 executed by the defendant Nos. 5-7 in favour of the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-4 to be inoperative and not acted upon contending, inter alia. that the suit land belonged to the defendant Nos. 5-7 who transferred the same by an unregistered deed of gift in 1964 in favour of the plaintiff, who got possession in the suit land through his mother. That deed could not be registered due to legal bar imposed by the Government for getting registered any deed of transfer made by any person belonging to the minority community, but the plaintiff started possessing the suit land continuously and without any interruption from any quarter. The plaintiff's further case is that the CS record, in respect of the suit land was wrongly prepared in the name of the Government and that one Ram Mohan and Chini Bashi managed to get settlement from the Government and thereafter transferred in favour of Hari Das and Anath Bandhu. Chini Bashi transferred in favour of Anath Bandhu and Anath Bandhu died leaving behind the defendant Nos. 5-7 as his heirs. It was their further case that the defendant  Nos. 5-7 were not in Bangladesh in 1969 and the defendant Nos. 1-4 by creating forged deed managed to get their names recorded in the SA and RS record but they were never in possession in the suit land. The plaintiff constructed 18 shops upon the suit land and being in possession was threatened by the defendant Nos. 1-4 in February 1994 with dispossession and, as such, the suit.

3. The defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint and specifically denying the title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. It was their specific case that Government being the owner of the suit land settled the same with Makhan Lal and Chini Bashi who transferred by a registered kabala deed dated 15-4-1969 (Exhibit Ka) in favour of Anath Bandhu and Chini Bashi. Anath Bandhu transferred the suit land in favour of the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-4 by a registered deed dated 16-4-1969 (Exhibit Ka) and that they being in possession the SA and RS records were prepared in their names and they paid rent, constructed a factory, shops upon the suit land and the structures were measuring about 50 feet x 50 feet, 16 feet x 12 feet, and another was measuring 12 feet x 13 feet. The plaintiff was never in possession and with these averments prayed for dismissal of the suit.

4. Upon pleadings of the parties the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj,

framed the following issues:

(i) 	Is the suit maintainable as it stands framed?

(ii) Is the suit barred by limitation?

(iii) Is the suit bad for defect of parties?

(iv) Has the plaintiff acquired any title by adverse possession in the suit land and whether that is existing too?

(v) Is the registered deed No. 5112 executed on 15-4-1969 and registered on 16-4-1969

forged, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff?

(vi) What other reliefs the plaintiff is entitled to?

The plaintiff examined three witnesses of whom the plaintiff himself was examined as PW 1. One Mohammad Ismail was examined as PW 2 and one Mujibur Rahman was examined as PW 3 and the unregistered deed of gift dated 16-8-1964 alleged to have been executed by Makhan Lal and others in favour of plaintiff was marked as Exhibit 1.

6. The defendant examined 4(four) DWs and their documents were exhibited as Exhibits Kaseries, Kha series, Ga, Gha series, Uma series, Cha, Chha, Ja, Jha and Neo.

7. Upon consideration of the evidence on record the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj, decreed the suit by the impugned judgment and decree dated 12-11-1998.

8. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the defendant has preferred this appeal.

9. Mr. Mahbubey Alarn, the learned Advocate for the defendant appellant, took us through the impugned judgment, evidences of both the parties, exhibited documents of both the parties, plaint, written statement and formulated the following points of arguments:

(i) the element of acquisition of title by adverse possession is totally absent in the evidence led by the plaintiff;

(ii) The plaintiff was a minor of five years at the time of his alleged unregistered deed of gift (Exhibit 1). Save and except the said Exhibit 1, there is no other corroborating evidence to show that the plaintiff did ever exercise his act of possession in the suit;

(iii) The defendants produced their title deeds along with biadeeds of their vendor, paid rent and proved their title and possession by .adducing oral and documentary evidence, particularly by paying rent to the Government;

(iv) the learned Joint District Judge, without proper discussions of the evidence on record and being failed to conceive and consider the principle of acquisition of title by adverse possession, has decreed the suit out of misconception of law and fact and the same is not sustainable in law.

10. Mr. A Baset Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondent, on the other hand, supported the judgment and decree of the trial Court and submitted that since 1964 the plaintiff being in continuous and uninterrupted possession on the basis of the unregistered deed of gift has acquired title by adverse possession and the judgment and decree of the Court below are not liable to be interfered with.

11. We have heard the learned Advocates of the respective parties. We have considered their submissions. We have gone through the entire evidences on record very carefully and meticulously.

12. From the case as made out in the plaint as well as in the written statement and from the evidence on record the following issues are framed for deciding the appeal on merit:

(i) Whether the plaintiff could make out a case of acquisition of title by adverse possession as per plaint's case?

(ii) Whether the evidence of PW 1, PW 2 and PW 3 are enough to construe adverse possession in the suit land as against the defendant?

(iii) Whether the Joint District Judge was justified in declaring the sale deed of the

defendant dated 16-4-1969 to be not acted upon?

(iv) Whether the impugned judgment and decree are sustainable in law? Let us discuss and decide all the issues together.

13. Adverse possession means hostile possession which is expressly or impliedly in denial of the title of the true owner. Such possession must be actual and exclusive under a clime of right, adequate in continuity, in publicity and in extent, so as to show that it is adverse to the true owner. Such possession in denial of the title of the true owner must be peaceable, open and continuous. It must be open and hostile enough to be capable of being known to the party interested before a right can be acquired or lost by adverse possession, it must have been such possession by a man without hostile as against the person with the lawful title.

14. In the instant case there is no such ingredient available in the plaint of the plaintiff as well as in the evidence of PW 1-PW 3 to construe adverse possession. In the instant case, the plaintiff has set up a case that on the strength of unregistered deed of gift dated 16-8-1964 he started possessing the suit land through his mother and thereafter continued his such possession till filing of the suit. This sort of possession is termed as lawful possession but not hostile possession. If any person upon entering into possession in the suit land on the basis of a deed and thereafter comes before a Court to get declaration of title by adverse possession in that case he is required to give up his claim on the strength of that deed by which he entered into possession into the suit land and thereafter he is required to set up his claim of hostile and notorious possession against the true owner and further required to prove his said possession for more than the statutory period of limitation.

<u>15. In the instant case, the plaintiff is totally silent about any hostile claim of right as against the defendant Nos. 1-4. The plaintiff did not specifically plead any claim of his acquisition of title by adverse possession. It appears that admittedly the plaintiff was born in the year 1959 meaning thereby he was aged about 5 years only in 1964. Save and except his oral evidence that he started possessing the suit land on the strength of the said unregistered deed of gift dated 16-4-1964 there is no other corroborative evidence by other two PWs in support of his possession in the suit land. The PW 2 and PW 3 simply added that the plaintiff was in possession in the suit land and the defendants did not possess. Save and except this evidence, there is no other assertion of aquisition of title by adverse possession as against the true owner.</u>

<u>16. From the pleadings of the parties it does not appear that the plaintiff ever claimed any hostile title against the defendant Nos. 1-4. In the examination-in-chief, the plaintiff added, that the defendant's predecessor purchased the suit land from the lessee of the government. Admittedly, the suit land was recorded in the name of the Government in CS Khatian and the defendant Nos. 1-4 by producing Exhibits Ka series could be able to prove that the Government's lessee had transferred the suit land in favour of their vendor and by producing Exhibit Gha series the defendants proved their possession in the suit land. The DW2 himself being the defendant No. 2 by adducing positive evidence proved that they established a factory upon the suit land and that there are other structures measuring about 50 feet x 50 feet, 16 feet x 12 feet, 12 feet x 13 feet they have in possession. These evidences have not been denied by the plaintiff nor any reliable evidences were adduced in the trial by the plaintiff to discard the defence case. The Exhibit 1 is an unregistered deed. Admittedly, on 16-8-1964 the plaintiff was a minor but from the deed itself it shows that he was described as a major in the said deed. Under section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 a deed of gift amongst the Hindus is compulsorily registerable. Moreover, the Exhibit 1 was not proved as per law by citing the scribe and attesting witness to prove the said deed as genuine. The vendor of that deed is the vendor of the defendant's predecessor's deed. The defendants deed is a registered deed dated 16-4-1969 which was acted upon as it appears, inasmuch as the SA and RS records were prepared in the name of the defendants and that they paid rent vide Exhibit Ga and Gha series.</u>

17. Those evidences show that the plaintiff being not in possession in the suit land filed the suit.

18. In view of the above discussions, we are constrained to hold that the learned Joint District Judge, without discussing and considering the evidence of the parties, has come to his findings most illegally, arbitrarily and whimsically and those findings are not sustainable in law.

19. In view of our above discussions, we find merit in the appeal.

20. In the result, appeal stands allowed with costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 12- 11-1998 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court Narayanganj, in Title Suit No. 344 of 1994 decreeing the suit is set aside. The suit stands dismissed.

Send down the lower Court's record immediately.

End.

parties:
Iftekhar Uddin Ahmed ----- Petitioner
Vs
Artha Rin Adalat and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Ziant Ara J : In this Rule Nisi, the petitioner has challenged the legality of the proceeding of Money Decree Execution Case No. 42 of 2002 pending, before the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka arising out of Money Suit No. 27 of 1990.

2. Facts necessary for the disposal of the rule, in short, are as follows:

Respondent No. 2 National Credit and Commerce Bank Ltd. Dhaka (shortly, the Bank), as plaintiff on 15-6-1990 instituted Money Suit No. 73 of 1990 before the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka for realization of loan amounting to Taka 20,16,381.90 as stood on 31-3-1990 impleading Messrs Ahmed and Brothers and the petitioner as defendants of the suit. The suit was transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka (the Adalat, in short) and renumbered as Money Suit No. 27 of 1990. The defendant-petitioner did not receive any summon of the suit. Eventually, the suit was decreed ex parte by judgment and decree dated 1-8-1991 (decree signed on 10-8-1991). The judgment-debtors having failed to pay the decretal dues, the Bank filed Money Decree Execution Case No.7 of 1995 before the Adalat in the year 1995 for realization of the decretal dues. The said case was disallowed on 14-5-2001. The order sheet of the execution has been destroyed. The decree-holder-Bank thereafter, filed he second execution case being Money Decree Execution Case No. 42 of 2002 on 5-8-2002 before the Adalat for realization of the decretal dues. The said execution case is pending before the Adalat and in the execution case on an application filed by the decree-hold-er-Bank under section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat, 2003 (the Ain, in brief), the learned Judge of the Adalat issued warrant of arrest against the petitioner. The petitioner came to know about the suit, the execution case, warrant of arrest, etc. from the notice published in the Daily Jugantor dated 24-9-2010 in Money Execution Case No. 42 of 2002. This resulted in this Writ petition.

3. Respondent No.2, the Bank opposed the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the statements made in the Writ petition contending, inter alia that bank filed Money Execution. Case No.7 of 1995 which was dismissed on 14-5-2001 and thereafter, the Bank filed second execution case on 5-8-2002 for recovery of its decretal dues within the period of limitation as per provision of Limitation Act and the Ain. Therefore, the execution proceeding as well as the order for issuing of war- rant of arrest is lawful and the rule is thus, liable to be discharged.

4. The petitioner filed a supplementary affidavit stating that the first execution case was filed on 27-11-1995 before the Adalat for execution of the decree dated 1-8-1991 and therefore, the first execution case was barred by limitation under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. As the first execution case is time barred, all other subsequent application for execution of the said decree is also time barred and, as such, the execution proceeding is liable to be struck down.

5. Mr Mohammad Hedayet Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner invites our attention to the information slip (Annexure-H to the Supplementary Affidavit) and submits that the suit was decreed on 1-8-1991 and the first execution case for execution of the decree was filed on 27-11-1995 and, as such, the first execution case having been filed beyond the period of 3 years as required under Article 182 of the Limitation Act was barred by limitation. He next submits that the first execution case was disallowed on 14-5-2001 and the second execution case was then filed by the decree-holder-Bank on 5-8-2002. He lastly submits that the first execution case being barred by limitation the subsequent Money Decree Execution Case No. 42 of 2002 is also barred by limitation and the entire proceeding of the Money Execution Case is thus, liable to be declared to be without authority.

6. Mr ASM Abdur Razzaque the learned Advocate for the Bank submits that as the record of Money Decree Execution Case No.7 of 1995 has been destroyed, the Bank is unable to ascertain as to whether the first execution case was filed earlier or whether any application for condonation of delay was filed in the first execution case and, as such, it cannot be presumed that the first execution case is barred by limitation and therefore, the rule is liable to be discharged.

7. We have examined the Writ petition, the affidavit-in-opposition, the supplementary affidavit and the connected materials on record.

<u>8. It transpires from the information slip (Annexure-H to the supplementary affidavit) that Money Decree Execution Case No. 7 of 1995 was filed on 27-11-1995 and the said execution case was disallowed on 14-5-2001 as found from the filing Register. It further transpires from the ex parte judgment and decree (Annexure-B and B I to the Writ petition) that Money Suit No. 27 of 1990 was decreed ex parte on 1-8-1991 and decree was drawn up the signed on 10-8-1991. Therefore, it is evident from the materials on record that first execution case was filed beyond the period of 3 years. Thus, the first execution case was barred by limitation in view of the provision of Article 182 of the Limitation Act. As the first execution case was barred by limitation, we are of the view that subsequent Money Decree Execution Case No. 42 of2002 for execution case of the said decree is also barred by limitation.</u>

9. This view of ours is also supported by the decision in case of Manta) Ali Akonda and others vs Kefatullah Mandai being dead his heirs Ira) son A. Hamid and others. reported in 7 MLR (AD) 138 wherein their Lordship of the Appellate Division decided as under:

"We have gone through the available materials particularly the judgment of the executing Court, appellate Court and also of the High Court Division, it appears that the Second Appeal was dismissed on 15-7-1982 and it is well settled that the decree holder may then proceed with the earlier execution proceeding but a separate proceeding initiated which is admittedly barred under Article 182 of the Limitation Act. Before this Court or even before the High Court Division the petitioners failed to produce any paper showing the facts of earlier execution proceeding. It is well settled that the decree may be executed within 12 years from the date of decree and that in the present case from 15-7-1982 on which date the Second Appeal was dismissed but in proceeding with such decree the provision of Article 182 of the Limitation Act is to be followed. The High Court Division found that this provision of law has not been followed and accordingly the proceeding is barred under Limitation Act. Mr Quasem, learned Advocate though tried frantically to convince us that the present case is not barred by limitation but we fail to agree with the submission in view of the fact that the Second Appeal was dismissed on 15-7-1982 and there is non-compliance of the provision of Article 182 of the Limitation Act. On consideration of the available materials we hold that the High Court Division has not committed any illegality and wrong in making the rule absolute."

10. In view of the above, we find merit and force in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and we find no merit in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the respondent- Bank.

11. From the discussions made hereinbefore, it is evident that the proceeding of Money Decree Execution Case No. 42 of 2002 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka being barred by limitation is unlawful.

12. In the result, the rule is made absolute.

13. The proceeding of Money Decree Execution Case No. 42 of 2002 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka is thereby declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

No order as to costs.

Communicate the Judgment to respondent No.1 at once,

End.
