full_judgment:
Sharifuddin Chaklader, J: This rule by the judgment debtor directed against judgment and other dated 3-4-2006 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka dismissing Miscellaneous Appeal No. 90 of 2006 affirming the other dated 7-3-2006 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka rejecting the application filed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of2005.

2. Decree holder Sonali Bank instituted Title Suit No. 21 of 2002 in Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 , Dhaka impleading judgment debtors as defendant No. 1 and 2 and Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation as proforma defendant for realizing loan money of Taka 8,03,568 on selling the mortgage property.

3. Plaintiff in the plaint stated that defendant judgment debtor No.1, Md. Asadullah by mortgaging schedule property with proforma defendant No. 3, took loan at Tk 6,00,000 on 25-4-1984. Later, on 19-7-1986 the judgment debtor applied for giving second mortgage of the self same property with the Sonali Bank, Local Branch to which, defendant No.3 on 31-4-1986 gave sanction. On 5-10-2006 judgment debtor No. 1 through judgment debtor No.2 applied for loan with the Sonali Bank. Sonali Bank on 15-2-1988 sanctioned Tk. 3,00,000 as house building loan. Judgment debtor No.2 on behalf of judgment debtor No.1 received the said money and expended the same for constructing the building. As per sanction letter, defendant No.2 executed the charge document, and as security, mortgaged the scheduled property. The period for repayment of loan was up to 23-4-2003 and installment for payment of loan was from October, 1988 at the rate of Taka 4,650 to be realized from rents and rate of interest was 16%. As security of the loan, defendant No. 2 executed and registered mortgage deed in respect of his owned titled schedule property in favour of the Sonali Bank and executed an irrevocable power of attorney being No. 4604 dated 6-4-1988 and also sworned an affidavit that mortgage property in any manner would not be sold to anyone till payment of loan of the Bank, The defendant did not repay the loan as per terms and condition of the sanctioned letter. Plaintiffs for repayment of the loan requested defendant at first verbally, thereafter by personal connection, later on, by Register Post and lastly, by issuing notice through lawyer but defendant did not pay any heed. Since defendants did not repay the loan, the representative of the Bank personally contacted the defendant verbally and in writing on 29-3-94, 8-7-95, 15-6-96, 13-8-94 and 30-8- 99 by issuing registered letter and having disgusted with the conduct of the defendants, Sonali Bank through his lawyer issued legal notice demanding payment of the loan within 9-1-2001. The loan at 3,00,000 so given to the defendant, stands at Taka 8,03,568 on the date of institution of the suit, filed the suit.

4. Judgment debtors did not appear in the suit. Defendant No.3, Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation appeared and filed written statement. In the written statement this defendant took the plea that suit is no maintainable and further stated that this defendant sanctioned on 18-1-1984 and 25-4-1984, through sanction letter No. D- 16966/875 Taka 4,00,000 with 13% and Taka 2,00,000 with 6% interest, in total, Taka 6,00,000 to defendant No.1 to be repaid in 25 years with monthly installment of Taka 5,571.65 for constructing a house. Defendant No. 1 mortgaged the suit property with this defendant and handover original deed No. 5060 and 6075 dated 6-10-79 with some other papers to this defendant. Defendant No.1 on 19-7-1986 applied to this defendant for second charge with the plaintiff and this defendant by letter dated 31-8-1986 gave approval. Defendant No.1 did not repay monthly installments of this defendant. This defendent on 30-6-99 instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 2000 for realizing Taka 14,30,431.41. In that case plaintiff of the instant suit appeared and contested the suit by filing written statement. This defendant prayed that if there be any decree passed in the instant case and if the schedule property be auctioned, in that case, at first, from the auctioned money all debts of this defendant as first charge would be paid.

5. The learned Joint District Judge on 29-8- 2002 decreed the suit against the proforma defendant on contest and ex-parte against defendant No.1and 2. It has been directed that defendant No. 1 and 2 would pay the money within 1-2-2002 and if they did not pay the said amount, then till realization of the money they would pay 15% interest and also directed that from the auction money, at first the loan of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation would be paid.

6. Decree holder, Sonali Bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 497 of 2003 in Artha Rin Adalat, which was renumbered as Artha Rin Case No. 369 of 2005. The executing Court advertised on 21-3-2004 in daily news paper for auction selling of the decreed property. Auction was held and opposite party No.2 purchased the auctioned property. While auction purchaser went to take possession of the case land through police force on 5-10-2005, petitioners could know about the auction and ex-parte decree through their tenants and filed Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 2005 under section 19(2) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2004 for setting aside the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 221 of 2001. The said case was fixed for maintainability on 7-3-2006. Learned Advocate for petitioner having been fell ill filed application for adjournment of the hearing on the maintainability of Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 2005. Learned Judge took up hearing of the Miscellaneous Case NO. 33 of 2005 on 7-3-2006 and rejected the application filed for adjournment. The learned Judge dismissed Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 2005 on 7-3-2006. Having being aggrieved by order dated 7-3-2006, judgment debtor petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 90 of 2006 before the learned District Judge. In the appeal, present petitioners filed application for not to sell the auctioned land to anybody, Learned Judge dismissed the appeal holding that since judgment debtors did not deposit 50% of the decreetal amount, the appeal is not maintainable. Against this order this rule.

7. Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali along with Mr. Md Nurul Amin, learned Advocates appeared for the judgment debtor petitioners. Md Faruque Hossain, learned Advocated appeared for the opposite party No. 1 Sonali Bank, Mr. Shahed Alam, learned Advocate appeared for House Building Finance Corporation, and Mr. Jamir Uddin Sirker along with Mr. Nowshed Jamir, learned Advocates, appeared for the auction purchaser.

8. Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate with Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Advocate, submits that, petitioners being original owner of the disputed property who having not been informed about institution the original case for realization of money and after having got information about the ex parte decree and auction to maintain their own property rushed to the Court for setting aside the auction, not the decree as they are ready to pay the decreetal amount as such, Court should allow their prayer on taking the decreetal amount, as in that case neither the Sonali Bank nor the Bangladesh House Building Corporation nor the auction purchaser suffer any loss as Bangladesh House Building Corporation and Sonali Bank are not want to grub the property but they will be satisfied if their money be secured which the judgment debtor petitioner are ready to deposit at any moment. The learned Advocates further submits that the auction purchaser just after purchase in auction of the property entered into agreement for selling the suit property with a third party, as such, the auction purchaser purchased the suit property for not to use and live there but to make profit of the same. Learned Advocate next submits that, execution case was filed without complying with the requirement of law as no receipt of acknowledgement due accompanied with the filing of execution case to prove that judgment debtors were notified person. Learned Advocate submits that petitioners challenge the order passed by the trial Court rejecting the application filed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure in appeal but the appeal was dismissed on the ground for nonpayment of 50% of decreetal amount which is an order not supported by law as section 61 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain referred to two options i.e. either to set aside the decree and in that case, deposit of 50% decreetal amount is a must and next, to set aside auction sale maintaining the decree where 50% of the decreetal amount is not required to be paid, learned District Judge totally misread the provision of law in dismissing the appeal of the judgment debtor thereby refuse to place their case. Learned Advocate further submits that in putting the suit property in auction no notice was served upon the petitioners as such, auction was held after practicing fraud upon judgment debtor as well as upon the Court. Learned Advocate further submits that, in holding auction, Court is bound to act as per provisions of section 30 and 33 of Ain, 2003 which having not be complied with the entire proceeding relating to auction of the suit property is liable to be set aside. Learned Advocate relying on the decision of Abdul Jalil vs Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, 41 DLR (AD) 109 submits that on the facts of the instant case this decision is applicable as in that case judgment debtor was allowed to retain the property on payment of decreetal amount giving soletium to the auction purchaser.

9. Mr Md Faruque Hossain, learned Advocate, appearing for the Sonali Bank submits that Sonali Bank is satisfied if the decreetal amount be paid and Mr. Shahed Alam, learned Advocate, appearing for Bangladesh House Building Corporation on the other hand submits that, his client is also satisfied if the loan money of his client be paid.

10. Mr. Jamir Uddin Sirker, learned Advocate, appearing for the auction purchaser, submits that, his client did not do any wrong as he is a bonafide purchaser of the suit property in auction pursuant to a notification published in daily newspaper pursuant to the decree obtained from a competent Court and also pursuant to the order passed in execution case, as such, auction purchase and delivery possession as made together with the judgment passed in original case and execution case should not be disturbed.

11. Mr. Jamir Uddin Sirker with Mr. Nowshed Jamir, Learned Advocates submits that, against the ex-parte decree obtained in original case dated 15-10-2005 judgment debtors filed Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2005, and Writ Petition No. 7705 of 2005 where the judgment debtors did not mooted the question as to service of summons in original suit as such, this question cannot be reopened as on this question Writ Petition is pending. Learned Advocate, on referring to the case of Korea Bangladesh Food Products Limited vs National Bank Limited reported in 13 MLR 253 where it has been held that:-

"The High Court Division observed that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is guided by the principles of the Code of Civil Procedure whereby 50% deposit of the decreetal amount to prefer an appeal is not mandatory. It found that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is a Special enactment. Therefore, the principles of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot override the provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. As there is the mandatory provision to deposit 50% of the decreetal amount to prefer appeal the present appeal is not at all maintainable and practically where is no appeal in the eye of law.

12. It appears from the record that in course of appeal the defendant was negotiating with the bank and the purchaser to sell the auction property and the defendant will pay up the entire decreetal amount at a time to the bank and he will also pay to the auction purchaser the amount together with interest. Thus, the High Court Division showed unwillingness to accept his submission to dispose of this Miscellaneous appeal as the provision for filing the appeal has not been complied with. It further appears from the record that in the absence of 50% of the decreetal amount deposit to prefer this appeal there is no existence of appeal in the eye of law", appellant must deposit 50% of the decreetal amount as such, learned District Judge committed no illegality in dismissing the appeal as it not maintainable. Learned Advocate further submits that the Appellate Division in the aforesaid 13 MLR case held that any appeal filed against any decision of Artha Rin Adalat is required to pay 50% of the decreetal amount. Learned Advocate further submits that, in the case of Sonali Bank vs Artha Rin Adalat, 15 MLR (AD) 20 = 62 DLR (AD) 231, it has been held that the execution proceeding ends with the completion of auction process in respect of mortgaged property, as such, at present when the auction process completed and delivery of auction land has already been given it cannot be re-opened. Learned Advocate further submits that although House Building Finance Corporation order and Artha Rin Adalat Ain are special law giving supremacy of the laws over all other laws prevailing but since Artha Rin Adalat Ain being later and when there is a conflict between two special laws, provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain shall prevail as such the decision reported in 41 DLR (AD) 109 has no manner of application on the facts of the instant case.

13. Let us proceed with our decision.

On the pleadings of the parties following questions calls for determination. At first, whether the ex-parte decree against the judgment debtors petitioners was passed lawfully; next, whether the execution proceeding pursuant to the ex-parte decree was legal; next, when original owner wanted to retain the case property by paying decreetal amount, whether relief can be given on setting aside the auction sale; next, whether auction sale can be set aside when the price of the property as shown in auction was shockingly too law.

14. It is not denied that Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, Act VII of 2003 is a special law and section 3 of the Act give supremacy of the Act over other laws. Chapter 4 deals with filing of case and also procedure of the Court. Section 7 is under Chapter- 4 speaks for service of summons. Section 7 later on amended by Act 39 of 2007 stand as:-

“আপাততঃ বলবৎ অন্য কোন আইনে যাহা কিছু্ই থাকুক না কেন, যদি আদালতের জারীকারক কর্তৃক প্রাপ্তি স্বীকারসহ রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত ডাকযোগে প্রেরণের নিমিত্ত, আরজির সহিত সমন জারীর জন্য সমুদয় তলবানা আদালতে দাখিল করিবেন এবং আদালত অবিলম্বে উহাদের একযোগে জারীর ব্যবস্থা করিবে এবং যদি সমন ইস্যুর ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে জারী হয়ে ফেরত না আসে অথবা তৎপূর্বে্ই বিনা জারীতে ফেরত আসে তাহা হইলে আদালত উহার পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 Order V এর Rule 20 এর বিধান অনুযায়ী সমন জারী করাইবে।”

15. On a reading of this section it appears that after issuing of summons from the Court if it is not served within 15 days or service return not received within 15 days, then on the matter of service of summons Court is to take recourse of procedure of Rule 20 of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure. In original case, which we have brought by special messenger as it relevant for disposal of this rule, order No. 5 dated 4-6-2002, the case was filed on 11-2-2002, runs as-

বাদীপক্ষ তদ্বীর নেননি। ১-৩ নং বিবাদীর সমন জারীকারকের রিপোর্ট মতে রীতিমত জারী অন্তে ফেরত এসেছে। দেখিলাম। সমন জারী সন্তুষ্টজনক। আগামী 2-7-02ইং তারিখে একতরফা শুনানী।

16. We do not understand why the learned Judge proceed so hastily as just before end of 4th month the suit was put into ex parte decree. Facts disclose that petitioner earlier took loan from defendant No. 3 for constructing residential home. The decree was passed against the petitioners ex-parte as they did not appear in the case. Laws says that when after service of summons if anyone did not appear to contest the suit then for fare and natural justice, as pet provision of rule 19 of Order V CPC the process server is required to be examined in support of his declaration and as to service of summons. His depositions stands as evidence of fact as to the service or admitted the service of the summons. On a reading of the judgment and decree passed ex-parte against this judgment debtors we find that learned Judge did not consider whether the summons were served satisfactorily or not. It is to be borne in mind that Ain, 2003 is harsh law giving no chance to a loanee to anything if it is found that he is a defaulting party. In the instant case, as we see, not only the money but also the land together with the building petitioners are loosing by stroke of pen of the learned Judge, as such, when the law is harsh then the learned Judge should be cautious before passing any judgment taking away life and property of an individual as to whether the litigant was aware of the proceeding and whether he was given proper opportunity to place his case. Whether summons were served or not it is the process server who could satisfy the Court as such, before passing an ex parte decree, since the law is harsh, the Court must examine the process server as Court witness. Law demand that before taking everything of a litigant and put him on the road, at least, from the judgment it could gather that before drawing the last blade at least Court is justify that all the required procedure of law have been satisfactorily complied with. When the law is harsh the principle of natural justice will have to follow as an abandoned caution i.e. the Court acted in equity, in honesty and rightly .

17. Next, it is argued that Appellate Court was not justified in dismissing the appeal summarily on the ground that 50% of the decreetal amount was not deposited along with memorandum of appeal.

18. In the case of Md Nur Islam vs Agrani Bank, 1 MLR 373, it has been held that-

"Deposit of 50% decreetal amount in both the cases either in an application for setting aside an ex parte decree or in an appeal is necessary.

19. The Artha Rin Adalat Act specifically provides for only two remedies against an ex parte decree. It is either by an application or by an appeal; but in both the cases deposit of 50% decretal amount is necessary to avoid this deposit, it appears, the petitioner has sought a short-cut by invoking section 151 of the CPC which is not applicable in such a situation.

20. Mr. Jamiruddin Sirker, learned Advocate, empathetically submit that, this law is prevailing over any other law and no sympathy can be drawn to anyone and no mercy can be shown to a party as it is special law and section 3 speaks the provision of this law is prevailing over any other law and this law being harsh law the provision of this law will be construed strictly. The submission of Mr. Sirker is otherwise can be said a pound of flesh as claimed by Shylock in the novel of Merchant of Vannis by William Shakespeare.

21. Generally it appears that if anybody challenge any decree then he will have to pay 50% of the decreetal amount as provided under section 41 of the Act of Ain, 2003 but in the instant case, it appears that, judgment debtor petitioners did not challenge the decree rather they want to maintain the decree but they have challenge the auction proceeding. The appeal is from an order passed on an application filed under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure. When a decree has been passed, ex parte or contested, the judgment debtor can challenge the decree by filing an appeal and as per law he must deposit 50% of the decreetal amount. But, when the judgment debtor challenge the auction sale keeping the decree in tact and want to maintain the decree than he is not required to deposit 50% of the decreetal amount as the judgment debtors are not aggrieved by the decree. Since the judgment debtors did not challenge the decree rather they want to maintain the decree and prayed for setting aside the auction sale so that they can maintain their property, it is our considered view that, 50% of decreetal amount is not required to be filed as required under section 41 of the Act.

22. Next question for consideration as whether the notice as published and auction as held was in accordance with law Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate, on referring to the auction notice published on 21-6-2005, submits that, since notice was not served, provision of section 33 of the Ain, 2003 was required to be followed strictly. Learned Advocate submits auction notice as published was in total violation of section 33 of the Ain, 2003. Section 33 of the Ain, 2003 runs as follows:-

অর্থঋণ আদালত ডিক্রী বা আদেশ জারীর সময় কোন সম্পত্তি বিক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রে বাদীর খরচ বিজ্ঞপ্তি প্রচারের তারিখ হইতে অনূন্য ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের সময় দিয়া সীলমোহরকৃত টেন্ডার আহবান করিবে। উক্ত বিজ্ঞপ্তি কমপক্ষে বহুল প্রচারিত একটি বাংলা জাতীয় দৈনিক পত্রিকায়, তদুপরি ন্যায়বিচারের স্বার্থে প্রয়োজন মনে করিলে স্থানীয় একটি পত্রিকায় যদি থাকে, প্রকাশ করিবে এবং আদালতের নোটিশ বোর্ডে লটকাইয়া ও স্থানীয়ভাবে ঢোল সহরতযোগেও উক্ত বিজ্ঞপ্তি প্রচার করিবে।

23. On a reading of this section it is clear that 15 days notice is required before holding auction. It also appears that notice as to holding of auction is to be affixed in the Notice Board of the Court and also at the locality notified by beat of drums. But nothing on record showing compliance of the provisions of this section.It appears that, auction was held not in accordance with law, as such, we are of the view that sale pursuance to this auction notice was done illegally.

24. Learned Advocate next submits that, auction property was sold shockingly at a very low price at Taka 40,00,000 and referred to the schedule to the execution case. Let us quote the schedule of the property sold.

তপছিল

জেলা-ঢাকার অন্তর্গত গুলশান থানাধীন মৌজা লালসরাই বনানী মডেল টাউন প্লট নং-৩১, সড়ক নং-১৭, ব্লক-ই, জমির পরিমাণ ৪ (চার) কাঠা ১০.৫০ (দশ দশমিক পঞ্চাশ ছটাক) যাহার চৌহুদ্দিঃ-

উত্তরে রাস্তা, দক্ষিণে প্লট নং-৩০, পশ্চিমে প্লট নং-২৯, এই চৌহুদ্দির ভেতরে নির্মিত ইমারাত ও অন্যান্য সরঞ্জামাদী।

It appears that, 4 kathas equivalent of 10.50 decimals of land was sold at Banani Model Town at Taka 40,00,000 itself show that some mischievous hand pressurized in selling of this property as even a 'chhatak' of land at Banani Model Town could not be sold in 2005 at such low price. Learned Advocate on drawing our attention to the fact that auction notice as per provision of law was not affixed in notice board of the Court and that holding of auction was not informed in the locality by beat of drums shows that some under hand tricks have been adopted in selling the property in auction.

25. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that, judgment debtors being the real owners of the property and auction money being at very low they are ready to pay the entire decreetal money in order to maintain their property and relied on the decision of Abdul Jalil vs BHBFC, 41 DLR (AD) 109. In that case, House Building Finance Corporation got decree for realization of Taka 6,83,657.70 and the property was sold in auction. The original owner i.e. petitioner Abdul Jalil filed objection in holding auction upon which the learned District Judge on realising Taka 1,00,000 on the next date on 14-9-1987, by order dated 13-9-1987, postpone the sale subject to payment of balance amount by 10-11-1987. Petitioner Abdul Jalil moved vainly before the High Court in revision and thereafter, move the Appellate Division and while the matter was moved before the Appellate Division the petitioner Abdul Jalil paid the entire decreetal amount. Meanwhile property was allowed to sell in auction and auction was closed as the auction purchaser purchased the auction property at Taka 10,10,000 and odd. The Appellate Division set aside the auction sale on the observation that when the original owner is eager to maintain his property by satisfying the decree, he can do that subject to soletium paid to the auction purchaser.

26. The next point calls for consideration is whether in the same proceeding both the loan of Sonali Bank and House Building Finance Corporation can be realised. Judgment debtor took Taka 3,00,000 from decree holder Sonali Bank on 6- 4-1988 and the last date for repayment of the loan was on 23-4-2003, i.e. for a period of 5 years. The judgment debtor petitioner took loan of Taka 6 lakhs from proforma defendant No.3, Bangladesh House Building Corporation on 25-4-1984 to be repaid within 25 years which would expire on 25-4-2009. But the decree was passed directing the judgment debtor petitioners to pay as:

অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি ৩ নং মোকাবেলা বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে দো-তরফা সূত্রে এবং অন্যান্য বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে একতরফা সূত্রে খরচাসহ ৩১-১-২০০২ ইং তারিখ পর্যন্ত ৮,০৩,৫৬৮ টাকার প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী হইল।

উক্ত ডিক্রীকৃত টাকা আগামী ৩ (তিন) দিনের মধ্যে বিবাদীগণকে বাদী/ব্যাংক বরাবরে পরিশোধ করার জন্য নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হল। অন্যথায় বাদী/ব্যাংক আদালতযোগে তাহার পাওনা টাকা ১-২-২০০২ ইং তারিখ হইতে আদায় না হওয়া পর্যন্ত ১৫% হারে সুদসহ আদায় করিয়া নিতে পারিবে। এবং নিলামে বিক্রিত টাকার মধ্যে প্রথমে ৩ নং মোকাবেলা বিবাদীর দাবীকৃত টাকা পরিশোধিত হইবে। তৎপর বাদী/ব্যাংকের পাওনা টাকা পরিশোধিত হইবে।

27. This decree as we see is not tenable in law as the loan of Sonali Bank was to be paid in 5 years and that of House Building Finance Corporation in 25 years as such, the loan of House Building Finance Corporation cannot and should not be included in the instant suit for repayment.

28. There is another obstacle in executing the decree. In the decree both the loan of Sonali Bank and House Building Finance Corporation have been amalgamated in one decree but as per provision of president's Order 7 of 1973, the loan of House Building Finance Corporation cannot be realised through Artha Rin Adalat constituted under Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 or 2003 as House Building Finance Corporation order itself provides mode of realization of loan under Article 27. In the case of Jahan Ara Akhtar Begum vs BHBFC, 47 DLR 158it has been held that "We are of the view that the cases for realization of loan of the House Building Finance Corporation shall be instituted in the Court of the learned District Judge and the same would be heard and disposed of by the learned District Judge, according to the provision of Article 27 of President's Order 7 of 1978". This judgment was affirmed by the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of BHBFC vs Jahan Ara Akhtar, 49 DLR (AD) 80 where it has been held.

29. Mr. Rafique-ul-Huq lastly argued that the High Court Division was at least wrong in holding that the appellant cannot take recourse to section 5 (1) of the Act for realization of loan and it has to proceed only under article 27. Yes, at some places of the impugned judgment, the impression has been given as above, such as, it has been said.

30. Provisions of section 5(1) of Artha Rin Adalat Act are very clear and, as such, the cases of the House Building Finance Corporation for realization of loan cannot be tried by the Artha Rin Adalat and if it is done, it will be wholly without jurisdiction.

<u>31. The view expressed by the High Court Division overlooks the provision of section 3 of the Act and does not comprehend section 5(1) with the proviso as a whole. In view of the said provisions, the position is that a financial institution may institute a suit in connection with realization of loan in the Artha Rin Adalat under the Act and by reason of the proviso to section 5(1) the special provision or procedure for realization of loan provided in the law by which the financial institution is established will not be affected. The option is with the financial institution either to bring a suit under section 5(1) of the Act or take recourse to the special procedure provided in the relevant law.</u>

32. As far as the present case is concerned the appellant already brought the proceedings under article 27 of President's Order No.7 of 1973. These proceedings cannot be transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat which has jurisdiction to try a suit and not proceedings under article 27. Notwithstanding the promulgation of the Act, the proceedings under article 27 can continue and we understand that this is that the High Court Division has really intended to convey although at places an impression has been given that a financial institution has to follow the special provision or procedure as provided in the relevant law for realization of loan and a suit under the Act for the said purpose will be without jurisdiction. We are, however, inclined to think that the High Court Division expressed itself keeping in view the facts of the present case only and its observations are meant to govern the case in hand and not generally. The appellant's interpretation of section 5(1) read with the proviso is found to be unacceptable."

33. House Building Finance Corporation has its own provisions for realization of loan under Article 27 of President Order 7 of 1972 and jurisdiction has been exclusively given to District Judge as such, for realising its loans only the District Judge has jurisdiction, no other Court, Artha Rin Adalat being a subordinate Court to District Judge has no jurisdiction to entertain any claim of House Building Finance Corporation.

34. As such the decree as passed amalgamating the loan money taken by the judgment debtor from Sonali Bank and House Building Corporation according to us was not passed legally.

35. There is another factor which, according to us, very vital i.e. whether the execution case was filed within prescribed period mentioned in the Ain, 2003.

36. Section 28 sub-section2, 3 and 4 and section 29 Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 are relevant for executing a decree. Section 28 speaks for:-

জারীর জন্য মামলা দাখিলের সময়সীমা৷ The Limitation Act, 1908 and The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 এ ভিন্নতর যে বিধানই থাকুক না কেন, ডিক্রীদার , আদালতযোগে ডিক্রি বা আদেশ কার্যকর করিতে ইচ্ছা করিলে , ডিক্রি বা আদেশ প্রদত্ত হওয়ার অনূর্দ্ধ ১৮০ (একশত আশি) দিবসের মধ্যে , ধারা ২৯ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে , জারীর জন্য আদালতে দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিয়া মামলা করিবে৷

(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর বিধানের ব্যাত্যয়ে , ডিক্রি বা আদেশ প্রদানের পরবর্তী ১৮০(একশত আশি) দিবস অতিবাহিত হইবার পরে জারীর জন্য দায়েরকৃত কোনো মামলা তামাদিতে বারিত হইবে এবং অনুরূপ তামাদিতে বারিত মামলা আদালত কার্যার্থে গ্রহণ না করিয়া সরাসরি খারিজ করিবে৷

(৩)   জারীর জন্য ২য় বা পরবর্তী মামলা,  প্রথম বা পূর্ববর্তী জারীর মামলা খারিজ বা নিষ্পত্তি হওয়ার পরবর্তী এক বৎসর সময় উত্তীর্ন হওয়ার পরে দাখিল করা হইলে,  উক্ত মামলা তামাদিতে বারিত হইবে এবং অনুরূপ তামাদিতে বারিত অনুরূপ মামলা আদালত কার্যার্থে গ্রহণ না করিয়া সরাসরি খারিজ করিবে৷

(৪) জারীর জন্য কোনো নতুন মামলা প্রথম জারীর মামলা দাখিলের পরবর্তী ৬ (ছয়)  বৎসর সময় অতিবাহিত হইবার পরে দাখিল করা হইলে, উক্ত মামলা তামাদিতে বারিত হইবে এবং অনুরূপ তামাদিতে বারিত অনুরূপ মামলা আদালত কার্যার্থে গ্রহণ না করিয়া সরাসরি খারিজ করিবে৷

২৯/ সময়সীমা সম্পর্কিত বিশেষ বিধান৷- আদালত , রায়প্রদানের সময় ডিক্রিকৃত টাকা এককালীন অথবা কিস্তিতে পরিশোধের জন্য কোনো সময়সীমা নির্ধারণ করিয়া থাকিলে , অনুরূপ সময়সীমা অতিক্রান্ত বা অকার্যকর হইবার পর হইতে ২৮(১) এ উল্লিখিত সময়সীমা কার্যকর হইবে৷

<u>37. On a reading of the law it appears that, for filing execution case, 180th day is the penultimate date and if no execution case be filed within this period then as per sub-section 2 the execution case will be dismissed as barred by limitation. Sub-section 3 provides that after dismissal of the execution case under sub-section 2, then as per provision of Sub-section 3, within 1 (one) year thereafter if execution case be not filed then the same will be dismissed. At present Sub-section 4 is not required for consideration. In the instant case in our hand the decree was passed on 29-8-2002 and as per section 28(1) execution case ought to be filed within 28-2-2003 but we find it was filed on 27-10-2003. If we give benefit of taking certified copy, then it appears that application for certified copy was filed on 27-1-2003 i.e. almost after 5 months, i.e. beyond the period for filing application for certified copy, which was obtained on 12-4-2003. Even from 12-4-2003 i.e. date of obtaining certified copy, the execution case was tiled beyond period of limitation as 180th day expired on 11-10-2003 but execution case was filed even thereafter on 21-10-2003 and legally it is more than 14 months from the date of ex-parte decree. As per provision section 28 of Ain, 2003, the Court should dismissed the execution case and as per sub-section 3, from the date of dismissal, decree holder could tile the decree for execution within 1(one) year thereafter. But nothing has so far been done lawfully and it stands the execution case as filed was filed beyond the period of limitation but the learned Judge executed the decree through execution case and the property was sold which is totally in violation of special law. We find the entire proceeding of execution case is barred by limitation and without jurisdiction as such, from the date of filing of the execution case upto selling of the property in auction, entirely was done without jurisdiction, illegally, malafide and arbitrarily with a motive. We find that execution case has filed illegally and no auction could be held on this execution proceeding. We find substance in the rule.</u>

38. In the result, the rule is made absolute. The connected Civil Rule No. 427 (R)/2006 also made absolute.

39. The entire auction proceeding is set aside. Since the decree passed is in existence, the judgment debtors are directed to pay the decreetal amount within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this order.

40. Before parting with the decision and lift our pen, we have considered the case of the opposite party-auction purchaser as he purchased the suit property in auction bonafide at Taka 40.00,000. Auction purchaser will get back the money from the Court with admitted Bank interest from the Bank. We are directing the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Dhaka to refund the money to the auction purchaser with interest within 30 days from the date of receipt of this order.

Sent down the lower Court records.

Communicate this order at once.

End.

full_judgment:
These two Rules in Civil Revision Nos.661 of 2006 and 662 of 2006 were issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 25-1-2006 and 31-1-2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Feni, in Title Appeal Nos.113 and 114 of 2004 allowing the appeals and reversing the judgment and decree dated 20-10-2004 and 27-10-2004 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Parshuram, Feni, in Title Suit Nos. 29 of 2003 and 8 of 2004 heard analogously and disposed of by a single judgment should not be set aside.

2. Since the two Rules were issued and two revisions were tiled out of same judgment let both the Rules be disposed of by this single judgment.

3. The petitioner here as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.63 of 2003 in the Court of Assistant Judge. Feni Sadar, Feni for declaration that the gift deed No.6457 dated 25-11-2001 registered with Feni Sadar Sub-registry Office executed by the defendant No.2 in favour of the defendant No.1 is illegal. collusive, void, inoperative and not binding upon him. The case was subsequently transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, Parshuram, Feni and re-numbered as Title Suit No.8 of 2004.

4. The brief fact of the plaintiff's case is that the plaintiff is an eye consultant (eye specialist) 01" Feni Sadar Hospital at present. The plaintiff after passing MBBS he joined at Kalidah Sub-Centre as Medical Officer and while serving there the father of defendant No.2 requested him to marry his daughter i.e. the defendant No.2, and on being satisfied he gave consent and ultimately the marriage was solemnised in 1988. During their wedlock they got one daughter and one son. The plaintiff appeared at BCS examination of Health Cadre and qualified himself and also subsequently passed FCPS in eye. As an eye specialist he earned good reputation at home and abroad. He went to Saudi Arabia through Government and served there for a long time with the satisfaction of the authority by high paid salary. He did not acquire any foreign decree as alleged by the defendants. The father-in-law of plaintiff Dr. Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury advised him through different letters not to send money to the brothers of Md Jahangir Alam and others because they will misuse his money. Then he advised his son-in-law, if you at all sent money for your future security he can send it to his father-in-law and according to his advice he started sending money to his father-in-law. It may be mentioned here that Dr Md. Jahangir Alam went to Saudi Arabia along with his wife and children and stayed in Saudi Arabia more than one year and came back again and joined at Feni Sadar Hospitalas eye consultant. While he was serving in Feni Sadar Hospital he used to live with his wife and children in a rented house at Mizan Road in Feni town and he also set up an eye clinic there. He brought many gold ornaments for his wife defendant No.2 when they were coming back to Bangladesh. While he was running his practice and clinic business he asked his father-in-law to give account of about Taka 10 (ten) lac which was sent to him from Saudi Arabia. His father-in-law told him that he has invested the money in his business and he would repay the money latter on. The defendant No.2, the wife of Dr. Md Jahangir Alam, was very much annoyed and displeased with him as he asked for his money to his father-in-law. Thereafter the defendant No.2 started pick to up quarrels with her husband on different pleas and she became very much disobedient and unloyaltoher husband. While residing at Mizan Road, Feni Town she used to frequently visit her father's house without seeking any permission from her husband and started a reckless life. Subsequently the relationship between the husband and wife became very bitter and they used to pickup quarrels frequently. That the plaintiff also started giving pressure upon his father-in-law to get back his money As a result the defendant No.2, the wife of Dr. Md Jahangir Alam, without seeking any permission went to her father's house along with her children and stayed some days there and again she came to her husband's house. The defendant No.2 started leading her life according to her sweet will and used to go out from her husband's house frequently to visit her father's house and relations' house. At last finding no other alternative, the plaintiff sent a divorce notice to the defendant No.2 on 4-10-2001 through local Pourashava. After receipt of that notice a Salish was held on 18-11-2001 at old Bar Library building Feni. The Salish was presided over by Dr. Shahidullah who was the then President of the Feni Doctors' Association and in presence of brother of defendant No.2 Manjur Wahab and two advocates of Feni Bar Md Nurul Amin and Md Saidur Rahman and close relation of defendant No.2 Md Zahirul Hoque and both the plaintiff and the defendant Nos. 2 were present in the Salish. After much negotiation and also after looking at the welfare of the children the Salishdar came to a agreement to the effect that Dr.Md Jahangir Alam will withdraw his divorce notice and the 'defendant No.2 Kamrun Nahar will make a gift of 3-1/2 decimal of land in the name of her husband Dr.Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury which was gifted to Kamrun Nahar by her father defendant No.3. Accordingly a Salishnama (Raida) was prepared but since the father-in-law of Dr. Md Jahangir Alam denied that he did not take or receive 10 lac Taka from Saudi Arabia sent by Dr. Md Jahangir Alam as such it was not written in the Salishnama, The Salishnama was signed by all the persons present in the Salish including the plaintiff and the defendant. Thereafter the Salishnama or Raida was authenticated by a Notary Public and it was settled up in the Salish that both plaintiff and defendant will abide by the decision of the Salish. Thereafter Dr Md Jahangir Alam on the same date withdrew his divorce notice and on 29-11-2001 the defendant No.2 Kamrun Nahar executed a gift deed No. 6511 dated 29-11-2001 at Feni Sub-Registry Office in presence of the attesting witnesses No.1 Advocate Md Nurul Amin, Md Saidur Rahman and Manjur Wahab and Kamrun Nahar was identified by her full brother Manjur Wahab. In pursuance of Salishnama and gift deed subsequently Dr. Md Jahangir Alam constructed a three-storied building and set up an eye clinic and chamber under the name and style of Feni Eye Centre in ground floor and first floor and the plaintiff along with his wife and children used to stay on the second floor and they were peacefully and harmoniously living there. Meanwhile after the lapse of about two years while settlement operation was going and the name of Dr Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury was published in the draft khatian or Mat-parcha then a dispute case was lodged before the attestation officer by the defendant No.3 on behalf of defendant No.1 father-in-law and mother-in-law to the plaintiff respectively to the effect that the schedule land was gifted to defendant No.1 the mother of defendant No.2 Kamrun Naharby a registered gift deed No. 6457 dated 25-11-2001 i.e. prior to the gift made by Kamrun Nahar to her husband on 29-11-2001 as such the khatian cannot be prepared in the name of Dr. Md Jahangir Alam. Thereafter Dr. Md Jahangir Alam gave a search in the Sub-Registry Office, Feni to obtain the certified copy of said Gift Deed No.6457 dated 25-11-2001. Meanwhile he received summons along with a copy of the plaint of Title Suit No.52 of 2003 subsequently re-numbered as 29 of 2003 filed by the defendant No.2 Kamrun Nahar.

5. After going through the plaint, the plaintiff came to realise that his wife Kamrun Nahar along with her father and mother only to deceive the plaintiff fraudulently executed the gift deed being No.6511 dated 29-11-2001. As a matter of fact Kamrun Nahar made a gift deed to her mother on 25-11-2001 prior to the gift executed by Kamrun Nahar to her husband on 29-11-2001. It may be mentioned here that Dr. Md Jahangir Alam mutated his name and obtained Kharija Khatian No.910 DCR thereof, he paid the rent in his own name for the suit land and he also submitted the construction plan of his three-storied building before the Feni Municipal Office and also paid municipal taxes in his own name because the holding number was prepared in his name. He also obtained the trade licence from municipal office in his own name for setting up the Feni Eye Centre and electric connection, telephone connection, every thing was made in the name of the plaintiff.

6. Finding no other alternative Dr. Md Jahangir Alam was compelled to institute the instant Suit No.63 of 2003 re-numbered as 8 of 2004 for a declaration to the effect that Gift Deed No.6457 dated 25-11-2001 registered with Feni Sub-Registry Office executed by defendant No.2 in favour of defendant No. 1 was collusive, fraudulent, inoperative, void and not binding upon the plaintiff. Thereafter both the cases were heard analogously by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Parshuram, Feniand disposed of by a single judgment decreeing the suit in favour of plaintiff of Title Suit No.8 of 2004 and dismissed the Title Suit No.29 of 2003 by his judgment and decree dated 20-10-2004 and 27-10-2004.

The brief fact of the Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 which was instituted by the plaintiff Kamrun Nahar against her husband Dr. Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury is that the plaintiff and defendant are the husband and wife and they got married on 11-2-1998 and they have I daughter and one son out of their wedlock. At the time of their marriage her father gifted many valuable goods and articles including ornaments and furnitures to the defendant husband and his father-in-law also gave Taka 5 lac to the defendant for taking higher education from abroad. The defendant is a man of very bad nature who always used to give pressure on her to take money from her father's house and used to torture her both physically and mentally for giving him dowry. Considering the future of the plaintiff her father made a deed of gift in the name of plaintiff on 25-4-2000 measuring 3-1/2 decimal of land situated at Feni town. Her father built up a 3-storied building with a foundation of 5-storied building by spending huge amount of money and she had been living there with her husband and children since 2001. The defendant again created pressure on the plaintiff to transfer the suit land to him in the name of defendant in writing in lieu of dowry and when she refused to do so a notice of Talak was given upon her on 4-10-2001. The plaintiff transferred the suit land measuring 3-1/2 decimal of land to her mother by a gift deed on 25-11-2001 considering her future security and safety in the absence of her husband. After issuance of said Talak notice a Salish was held on 29-11-2001 where it was decided to settle up the dispute and to withdraw Talak notice by the defendant and in pursuance of that decision of Salish the defendant withdrew the notice of Talak by an affidavit and then they started living their conjugal life as husband and wife peacefully.

7. Again the defendant told her to transfer the suit land in the name of the defendant for running his practice as eye specialist and failing of which she would be divorced. In order to maintain conjugal life peacefully and considering the future of the children she executed and registered the gift deed No.6511 dated 29-11-2001 in favour of the defendant. But on the date of execution and registration of deed of gift she had no right and title to transfer the suit land.

But without taking any permission from his first wife plaintiff and the concerned Pourashava, defendant married a girl of Dhaka named Asha and brought in her house on 27-4-2003 and tried to stay there but she prevented them and thereafter defendant shifted his all machineries and equipment of his eye clinic and chamber to a rented house and started living there with his second wife Asha. For that the plaintiff filed CR Case No.75 of 2003 under section 6(5) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1962 in the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Feni against the defendant but the plaintiff could not prove the charge under section 6(5) of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance of 1962 as such the case was dismissed. Subsequently she instituted the Civil Suit being No.29 of 2003 on 5-6-2003 for cancellation of gift deed dated 29-11-2001 under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act to cancel the deed as the deed was forged, collusive, fabricated, null, void and inoperative.

8. The defendant husband Dr. Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint stating, inter alia, what he already stated in the plaint of his Title Suit No.63 of 2003 subsequently re-numbered as 8 of 2004. Both the Title Suit No.29 of 2003 and 8 of 2004 tried by the Senior Assistant Judge, Parshuram, Feni and heard analogously and disposed of by a single judgment dated 20-10-2004.

9. During the course of trial the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Parshuram, Feni after examining the evidence on record and perusing the documents and exhibits produced by both the parties in support of their respective suits and came to his finding that the plaintiff of Title Suit No.8 of 2004 successfully proved the case, on the other hand, the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 Most. Kamrun Nahar miserably failed to prove her case, as such, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Parshuram, Feni decreed the Title Suit No.8 of 2004 in favour of the plaintiff and dismissed the Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 by his judgment and decree dated 2-10-2004 and 27-10-2004 respectively.

10. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court the defendants of Title Suit No.8 of 2004 and the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 preferred 2 appeals before the learned District Judge, Feni which were subsequently heard by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Fenion transfer. Both the appeals were heard analogously and disposed of by one judgment by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Feni after hearing both the appeals and their learned lawyer allowed the appeals and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court by his judgment and decree dated 25-1-2006 and 31-1-2006 respectively.

11. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court Feni the defendant-respondent-petitioner of Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 and plaintiff-respondent petitioner of Title Suit No.8 of 2004 Dr. Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury preferred two revisional applications being Civil Revision Nos. 661 of 2006 and 662 of 2006 under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

12. The learned Counsel Mr. Md Oziullah, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner in Civil Revision No. 661 of 2006 and defendant-respondent-petitioner in Civil Revision No. 662 of 2006 submits that the lower appellate Court is absolutely wrong and erroneous in allowing the appeals and reversing the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial Court, the learned Assistant Judge, Parshuram, Feni on consideration of the evidence on records, documents, exhibits and other connected papers passed in the judgment and decree in favour of the petitioner Dr. Md Jahangir Alam which was absolutely proper and justified. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Parshuram, Feni observed that the plaintiff of Title Suit No.8 of 2004 Dr. Md Jahangir Alam has been able to prove the case that the deed of gift was duly executed and registered in pursuance of terms and conditions of Salish held in Feni Bar Association Building in presence of the plaintiff Dr. Md Jahangir Alam and his wife defendant Most Kamrun Nahar, her brother Manjur Wahab and two Advocates Mr. Md Nurul Amin and Saidul Hoque of Feni Bar Association and all of them were signatories of the Salishnama, According to the decision of the Salish, plaintiff Dr. Md Jahangir Alam withdraw the Talak notice and defendant Most. Kamrun Nahar also executed a deed of gift of31/2decimal of land and the document was duly registered on 29-11-2001 and the possession of the suit land was also duly delivered to the plaintiff. Thereafter plaintiff Dr. Md Jahangir Alam for constructing a three-storied building submitted a plan in the Feni Municipality for approval and deposited the necessary fees in his name and after approval he constructed a three storied building by his own expense. He set up Feni Eye Clinic in the ground floor of that building and set up his chamber in the first floor and started his roaring practice and he along with his wife and children used to live in the 2nd floor of the building. In this way they were living peacefully and harmoniously in their conjugal life in the newly constructed house for about two years. Meanwhile, he has mutated his name by opening a separate khatian and by paying rent and also a new municipal holding number was prepared in his name. Thereafter when a settlement operation was going on an attested khatian was prepared in the name of Dr. Md Jahangir Alam, a dispute case was lodged to the concerned attestation officer by the father-in-law of Dr. Md Jahangir Alam and by father of the defendant No.2 to the effect that the disputed land was gifted to the mother of KamrunNaharon25-11-2001 by a gift deed No. 6457 by Kamrun Nahar as such, the subsequent gift deed executed by Kamrun Nahar, the defendant No.2 on 29-11-2001 with regard to the same suit land has become infructuous. The learned Counsel next submits that meanwhile plaintiff of Title Suit No. 8 of 2004 received summons along with a copy of the plaint of Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 where from Dr. Md Jahangir Alam came to realise about the dishonest and deecptive intention of his wife, father-in-law and mother-in-law and was constrained to file the declaration suit No.8 of2004. The learned trial Court after discussing all the documentary evidence and the oral evidences and after applying his judicial mind and also after proper assessment of the evidence both oral and documentary came to a correct and justified finding that if at all the another gift deed was made by Kamrun Nahar 3 days prior to 29-11-2001 it was dormant or sleeping deed and which was not acted upon and no delivery of possession was made as such, by this sleeping deed no title was passed. The learned Counsel further submits that Kamrun Nahar has got no locus-standi to file the Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 as plaintiff according to her own claim she was no longer the owner of the suit land but her mother Zebun Nahar Chowdhurani was the proper persons to file the suit under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act as such, the suit of Kamrun Nahar as plaintiff is not maintainable. He also submits that under section 92 of the Evidence Act the documentary evidence will prevail upon the oral evidence and draw the attention of the Court to the recital of the gift deed No. 6511 dated 29-11-2001 wherein it has been clearly stated that the suit land was null and vacant land. He further submits that the claim of the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 is barred by waiver and acquiescence because she herself deposed that she had gifted the suit land in 'the name of her mother prior to the gift deed executed in the name of her husband Dr. Md Jahangir Alam. Finally the learned Counsel submits that the learned lower appellate Court without discussing the evidence on record and without perusing the exhibits and documents came to a wrong and fallacious finding being guided by emotion and sentiment and recollecting the poem written by Rabindra Nath Tagore “দুই বিঘা জমি” The lower appellate Court totally ignored the legal aspect of the case that the suit of the plaintiff Most. Kamrun Nahar being Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 is not maintainable according to her own version and deposition. The lower appellate Court in his judgment termed the gift deed executed by Kamrun Naharon 25-11-2001 as security deed or as a shield against her husband. He also submits that in legal proceedings there is no scope or opportunity to do anything which is not permissible by law. The lower appellate Court while allowing the appeals and reversing the judgment of the trial Court is required to reverse the finding of the trial Court with reference to the evidence on record but the lower appellate Court without making such observation and without consideration of the documentary evidence and legal aspect of the case passed a judgment absolutely guided by emotion and sentiment and, as such, liable to be interfered by this Court hence the Rule should be made absolute.

13. On the other hand, the learned Counsel Mr. Abul Kalam Chowdhury with Mr. AT Obaidul Hye, appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 1, submits that the lower appellate Court was absolutely correct and justified in allowing the appeals and reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. In this connection he referred the case which was also cited in the judgment of the lower appellate Court in Title Suit No. 29 of 2003 6 DLR (AD) 97 wherein it has been stated that:

"Initial onus of undue influence is on the person who raises the plea-Initial onus with- out discharge, the burden shifts on the other side to prove the contrary".

14. Next he submits that the lower appellate Court rightly observed that the plaintiff of Title Suit No.8 of 2004 Dr. Md Jahangir Alam creating pressure of giving notice of Talak in a deceitful manner obtained the gift deed from his wife on 29-11-2001. This gift deed in the eye of law has got no value and liable to be cancelled under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned Counsel finally submits that the lower appellate Court after considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also discussing the evidence came to a right and justified finding in allowing the appeals and reversing the judgment and decree which is not liable to be interfered by this Court in revision under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

<u>15. On a meticulous examination of the records, exhibits, documents and the judgment of both the Courts below and also the connected papers it appears that the trial Court discussed the evidence on record and also perused the documents. And exhibits and considered the material evidence and made his observation. It further appears from the judgment of both the Courts below that the lower appellate Court in reversing the judgment of the trial Court did not refer the evidence on record and the contents of the finding of the trial Court with reference to the evidence on record. The decision which was referred by the appellate Court is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. The lower appellate Court totally ignored the legal aspect of the case and being guided by emotion and sentiment passed the judgment of reversal without any cogent and justified reason or ground. The appellate Court while reversing the judgment of the trial Court required to reverse the material finding of the trial Court with reference to the evidence on record. In this connection I like to refer the decision in the case of Mohsena Khatun vs Habib Knitting Mills reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 47 wherein it has been held: "While reversing the judgment of the trial Court the appellate Court is required to reverse the material findings of the trial Court with reference to the evidence on record."</u>

16. In judgment of the trial Court it appears that in its finding the said Court carefully considered the material evidence on record. The learned trial Court did not commit any error of law and also committed no illegality in arriving at his finding because the plaintiff Dr. Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury could be able to prove the case successfully. The lower appellate Court committed an error of law and came to a wrong finding occasioning failure of justice in not considering the documentary evidence, exhibits and other vital documents. The appellate Court being guided by emotion and sentiment passed the judgment without the legal basis. The appellate Court ought to have considered whether the deed of gift was duly executed and registered and acted upon and the validity of the deed of gift and also whether the title was passed by this deed of gift or not. Without determining this vital legal aspect of the case the appellate Court reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court which is liable to be set aside. In this connection I like to rely on the case of Hussain Ahmed Chowdhury vs Md Nurul Amin reported in 47 DLR (AD) 162 wherein it has been held :

"If there is misreading of evidence and non-consideration of some material evidence then it was incumbent on the revisional Court to consider the same and to arrive at a proper finding on the material evidence on record and to finally dispose of the case."

<u>17. Another decision can also be cited in the case of Habibullah vs Sher Ali Khan reported in 57 DLR (AD) 55 wherein it has been stated:</u>

<u>"The High Court Division while exercising its revisional jurisdiction is competent to reverse the judgment of the Courts below when the same has been made either upon misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence causing failure of justice."</u>

<u>18. In view of the facts and legal position of the case I find that the lower appellate Court is absolutely wrong in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, as such, the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court is liable to be set aside.</u>

<u>19. The discussion made above and the facts and circumstances of the case and also the legal position of the case the impugned judgment and decree dated 25-1-2006 and 31-1-2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Feni, in Title Appeal Nos.113 of 2004 and 114 of 2004 allowing the appeals and reversing the judgment and decree dated 20-10-2004 and 27-10-2004 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Parshuram, Feni, in Title Suit Nos. 29 of 2003 decreeing the Title Suit No.8 of 2004 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court is hereby affirmed.</u>

20. In the result these two Rules are made absolute without any order as to the costs.

21. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.

Lower Courts record be sent down at once with a copy of the judgment.

End.

parties:
Gour Netai Sri Sri Modan Mohan Das Bigraha -------- Petitioner
Vs.
Jahanara Islam Chowdhury and others  -------- Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
This Rule was obtained on behalf of the above deity upon making a revision application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure against an order dated 1-6-08 passed by the District Judge at Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 140 of 2008, which dismissed the appeal upon rejection of the application made under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay and affirmed the ex parte decree dated 29-5-86.

2. Case of the petitioner, in short, is that the suit property is 'Debuttor', which belonged to the aforesaid deity. Present petitioner Umananda Saha is a Devotee of the deity by generation. He has been offering 'Puja' every day to the deity.

3. On 22-4-08 the police came to the temple in connection with a case. On enquiry and upon receipt of information from the Court on the very same date, he came to know that on 19- 12-84 one Majharul Islam Chowdhury, predecessor-in-interest of opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 instituted Title Suit No. 405 of 1984, which was dismissed on merit in the absence of the deity by an order dated 12-11-85. Then, said plaintiff made an application under Order XLVII, rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 127 of 1985 for review of said order dated 12-11-85. By an order dated 28-5- 86 the Court allowed said prayer for review and decreed the suit ex parte, behind the back of the deity. He further learnt that said ex parte decree was put into execution in Title Execution Case No. 20 of 1986 and 30-4-86 was fixed for police report.

4. In the circumstances, in order, to protect the property of the deity, he presented aforesaid appeal as next friend of the deity before the District Judge at Dhaka against said ex parte decree dated 29-5-86. As the appeal was out of time by 8007 days, he also made an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 for condonation of the delay.

5. In the said application, he stated that he had no knowledge of the institution of the suit and sub- sequent proceedings arising out of the said ex parte decree until 22-4-08 when the police came to the temple.

6. He asserted that aforesaid plaintiff obtained the ex parte decree by using LTI of a woman, namely, Giribal who was neither owner of the temple property nor Shebayet of the deity. No summons of the suit was ever served upon the deity

7. Upon registration of the appeal and receipt of the application for condonation of delay, the appellate Court issued notice for service upon aforesaid opposite parties. In pursuance thereof, the opposite parties appeared and opposed the admission of the appeal by filing a verified application.

8. In said application, it is stated that their predecessor, Mazharul Islam Chowdhury instituted aforesaid Title Suit No. 405 of 1984 for specific performance of a contract. On 29-5-86 the suit was decreed ex parte. In execution of the decree, he got a sale deed No. 64 dated 6-1-87 executed and registered by the Court in Title Execution Case No. 20 of 1986.

9. It is further stated that one Digendra Sarker claiming to be a member ofthe managing committee of the temple challenged the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 20 of 1993, which was ultimately renumbered as Title Suit No. 217 of 2003. Another Dilip Kumar Roy claiming to be 'Shebayet' of the deity appointed by earlier 'Shebayet' Giribala also instituted Title Suit No. 21 of 1993, which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 216 of 2003 for setting aside the ex parte decree and cancellation of aforesaid deed dated 6-1-87. Digendra Sarker also instituted Title Suit No. 35 of 1993, which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 215 of 2003 against said Dilip Roy challenging the 'Shebayetnama' of Digendra Sarker.

10. He made an application for dismissal of Title Suit Nos. 216 of 2003 and 217 of 2007 on the ground of maintainability and locus standi before the Joint District Judge (Additional Court), who by his order dated 29-2-04 rejected the application. Against the order, he made a revision application under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure being Civil Revision No. 163 of 2004 before the District Judge at Dhaka. Learned District Judge by his order dated 18-8-04 allowed the application and dismissed all the three suits for want of locus standi and cause of action.

11. Against such dismissal, Digendra Sarker and Dilip Roy moved this Division in revision under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure being Civil Revision No. 4554 of 2003 and No. 5133 of 2004 respectively. By an order dated 25-6-06 this Division discharged both the Rules and vacated the order of stay of further proceeding of Title Execution No. 20 of 1986. Against said order Digendra Sarker unsuccessfully made a petition for leave to appeal being CP No. 992 of 2006 before the Appellate Division, which was also dismissed by an order dated 4-2-08. In the aforesaid premises, said opposite parties prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

12. Learned District Judge by the impugned order dismissed the appeal upon purported rejection of the application for condonation of delay.

13. By filing a supplementary affidavit, the petitioner annexed copy of the judgment of the Appellate Division dated 21-6-05 passed in CA No. 283 of 2003 and an order dated 4-2-08 dismissing CP No. 922 of 2006.

14. Opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 opposed the above Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition. Besides what they stated in their objection to the admission of above appeal before the District Judge, it is contended that said decree holder unsuccessfully made an application under Order VII, rules 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaints of Title Suit No. 20 and No. 21 of 1993, which was rejected. Then, on 22-6- 99, he made an application under Order XIV, rules 2 and 5 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for framing an additional issue as to the locus standi of said Digendra Sarker and Dilip Roy. The application was allowed and an issue as to the locus standi of the plaintiffs was framed but remained undecided (?).

15. The decree holder also made an application on 18-4-2000 for a decision of the issue on locus standi before final hearing of the suits, which was rejected by an order 14-9-2000. Then, he made an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the order dated 14-9-2000 and pressed for decision on locus standi first, which was also rejected by an order 3-1-01. He made an application on 15-2-01 for review of said order, which was also rejected. Being aggrieved, the decree holder moved this Division in revision in Civil Revision No. 1670 of 2001. This Division made the Rule absolute and sent the case back to the learned Joint District Judge on remand for final disposal. Whereupon, the learned Joint District Judge found the locus standi of the above plaintiffs, Digendra Sarker and Dilip Roy and dismissed the prayer of the decree holder by his order dated 29-2-04.

16. It is also stated that against the order of the Appellate Division dated 4-2-08 dismissing CP No. 992 of 2006 Digendra Sarker made an application being Review Petition No. 45 of 2008, which was also dismissed on 19-8-08. Dilip Kumar challenged the order of the District Judge dated 18-8-04 before this Division in Civil Revision No. 5133 of 2004, which was discharged on 25-6-06. Then, he filed an application for review of said order and on 20-8-06 obtained a Rule being Civil Rule No. 692 (R) of 2006. The decree holder also made a petition for leave to appeal being CP No. 1488 of 2006, which was ordered to be heard along with above CP No. 992 of 2006 and was ultimately not pressed.

17. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that learned District Judge most illegally dismissed the appeal mainly on the view that the petitioner had no locus standi after dismissal of the suits of said Digendra Sarker and Dilip Roy since the petitioner was never a party in any of the suits and, as such, not bound by the dismissal of said suits.

18. He submitted that learned District Judge fell in serious error in assuming that the petitioner initiated Miscellaneous Case No. 192 of 2008 for setting aside the aforesaid ex parte decree dated 29- 5-86 and most illegally dismissed the appeal for such proceeding.

19. Lastly, he submitted that learned District Judge missed the scope of enquiry in the admission of the appeal upon condonation of the delay and most erroneously dismissed the appeal without consideration of the case of the petitioner at all but on the ground of locus standi etc. on extraneous consideration which resulted in an error occasioning failure of justice.

20. Mr TH Khan, learned Senior Advocate for said opposite parties on the other hand, took me through the record of long protracted litigations they had to face after the decree passed in Title Suit No. 405 of 1984 at the instance of various persons claiming the right to represent the deity.

21. He submitted that after dismissal of the suits of Digendra Sarker and Dilip Roy, the appeal of the petitioner on behalf of the deity was nothing but a device to delay the execution of the decree, and the impugned order therefore, does not call for any interference.

22. He did not hide his frustration by expressing that there must be an end of litigations and all such proceedings were nothing but design to prevent the opposite parties from getting possession of the suit property and enjoying the fruit of long litigations.

23. Only issue that is facing me in the Rule is, whether the learned District Judge was well founded in dismissing the appeal of the petitioner upon purported rejection of the prayer for condonation of delay.

24. In order to dispose of such issue, the facts that are relevant, in brief, are that the petitioner on 24-4-08 presented the aforesaid appeal as next friend of the deity before the District Judge at Dhaka for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 29-5-86. It is his case that he worships the deity for generations and, as such, he has the right to protect the property of the deity as next friend.

25. The appeal was out of time by 8007 days. He accordingly, made a verified application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of the delay. Upon such application, learned District Judge issued notice upon the opposite party Nos. I to 4, descendants of the decree holder, and also granted stay of further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 20 of 1986 under Order XLI, rule 5 of  the Code of Civil Procedure by an order passed on the same date.

26. Said opposite parties on 4-5-08 appeared and filed a verified application for vacating the order of stay dated 24-4-08. They also made an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for dismissal of the appeal. On 1-6-08, all the applications, namely, for condonation of delay, vacating the stay and dismissal of the appeal, were taken up for hearing. By the impugned order the learned District Judge practically dismissed the appeal and affirmed the ex parte decree on the following view:

"In the facts and circumstances of the case, this Title appeal is hopelessly barred by limitation and same can't be admitted and hence refused. The impugned judgment and decree are hereby affirmed."

27. I have closely examined the impugned order. It appears to be of two parts. In the first part, learned District Judge found the petitioner is a third party and had got no locus standi to challenge the -ex parte decree. In order to understand his reasoning, it would be better to reproduce them.

"The record of Title Suit No. 405 of i 984 shows that the appellant filed another Miscellaneous case being No. 192 of 2002 to set aside the ex parte judgment and decree dated 29-5-86 of the said suit. In this appeal same relief is being claimed. The appellant should adopt one forum for setting aside the alleged ex parte decree. It is needless to say that the ex parte decree Was obtained by the respondent as far back as in the year of 1986 and till today they could not enjoy the fruits of the decree this way or that way. The appellant is a third party and, as such, he has got no authority to challenge the ex parte decree. The suit having been decided on the merits up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in favour of the respondents and so this appeal can't be admitted."

28. From the above reasoning, what weighed heavily with the learned District Judge are that the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 192 of 2008 (not 2002); that he is not entitled to adopt both forums, namely, one by appeal and the other section Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that he is third party. But the record does not support the learned District Judge on any of such facts.

29. First, aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 192 of 2008 was brought by one Debashish Mitra under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure and not by the petitioner. So, the entire reasoning on locus standi on this count must be held to be based on no fact but assumption.

<u>30. Second, learned District Judge found that the petitioner was a third party and the appeal at his instance was therefore, held to be not maintainable. Here, he fell in serious error of law, may be, for misunderstanding of the Hindu Law. The petitioner presented the appeal as a next friend of the deity, who was impleaded as defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 405 of 1984 and against whom the ex parte decree was obtained. Under the Hindu Law, any devotee and/or worshipper can represent a deity in any suit by or against her to protect her property. Of course, with permission of the Court under Order XXXII, rules 1 and 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. So, the petitioner did not prefer the appeal as third party. Law in this regard was settled in our jurisdiction in Prodip Kumar Chkraborty vs Jamila Khatun Bibi 51 DLR (AD) 156. The Appellate Division held:</u>

<u>"most of the shebaits have already left the country or have since died. A few who are in this country are dormant and have not been taking any interest in the cause of deity and play its next friend. In the circumstances Prodip Kumar Chakraborty who is admittedly a pujari and a worshipper of the deity and has offered himself to act as next friend of the deity can by no means be precluded from representing the deity as such."</u>

31. Third, the finding of the learned District Judge that the suit having been decided on the merits upto the Appellate Division in favour of the respondents and so, this appeal can't be admitted' is also not based on appreciation of the record. Learned Additional District Judge, Seventh Court, in Civil Revision Case No. 163 of 2004 found that " .... .it is very difficult to ascertain to his real and true representative and so long it is uncertain that they (that is Digendra Sarker and Dilip Roy) have no right and authority to file any suit against any person." Upon such view, he dismissed Title Suit Nos. 215, 216 and 217 of 2003 for want of locus standi by his order dated 18-8-04. Such order was upheld by the Appellate Division in dismissing CP No. 992 of 2006. In Civil Appeal No. 283 of 2003, the original decree holder being unsuccessful in this Division challenged the order dated 10-11-94 of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court and Artha Rin Adalat at Dhaka granting stay of further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 03 of 1993 (after Title Execution No. 20 of 1986 was so renumbered). The Appellate Division allowed the appeal and set aside the orders of the Subordinate Judge and this Division for want of locus standi.

32. So, the decree holder never allowed the merits of the ex parte decree dated 29-5-86 to be judged by any Court at any time. It is the definite case of the petitioner that the decree holder obtained the ex parte decree using the LTI of one Giribala as Shebayet. She was never Shebayet of the deity. It is submitted that no order could be found in the order sheet of said Title Suit No. 405 of 1986 evidencing service of any summons upon the deity or service of any notice of hearing of the aforesaid Review Case No. 127 of 1985 upon the deity after dismissal of the suit for want of proof of execution of the so-called 'Bainapatra' dated 7-10-83.

<u>33. It is admitted that the suit property belonged to the deity. The deity is always a minor. Such deity deserves the same-standard of care and attention from a Court of Law in case of any transfer of its property as a minor does. For this reason, any objection to any transfer of property of a deity even by a worshipper is entertainable by a Court of law in order to find that such transfer was genuine and for the interest and benefit of the deity. In this case, the entire transaction is alleged to be tainted by fraud. No period of delay can defeat fraud, if any practiced, since time does not run against fraud.</u>

34. In the second part of the impugned order, learned District Judge considered the application of the petitioner for condonation of the delay after he found the appeal was not admissible on the aforesaid reasoning. It is the definite case of the petitioner that he came to know on 22-4-08 for the first time of the institution of the suit, the ex parte decree and the execution proceedings only when the police came to the temple. After enquiry and receipt of the information slip, he was sure of the suit and the ex parte decree. In such circumstances of the case, the petitioner was only obliged to explain the delay from the date of his knowledge on 22-4-08 to the date of filing of the suit on 24-4-08.

35. In fact, no objection was filed on behalf of the opposite parties to the application for condonation of the delay and/or the knowledge of the petitioner on 22-4-08. It was the duty of learned District Judge to decide such application on merit.

36. Learned District Judge quoted section 5 of the limitation Act and found every day of delay of 8007 was not explained. He missed the pertinent point here. If the petitioner could satisfy him that he had no knowledge of the ex parte decree before 22- 4-08, then, he was obliged to explain the delay from such date of knowledge to date, of presentation of the appeal and not beyond such period. Only issue would have been before the, District Judge was, whether the petitioner was prevented by any sufficient cause to prefer the appeal.

37. Actually, the learned District Judge appears " to be swayed away by the application of the opposite parties for dismissal of the appeal on the basis of the aforesaid orders of the Appellate Division.

38.
