Faced with such development at the hearing of the Rule, Mr Mohammad Ahasan, learned Advocate for the opposite parties, frankly conceded that in the absence of any written objection to the prayer for condonation of the delay, especially to the case of knowledge of the petitioner, it would be very difficult for them to defend the impugned order refusing admission of the appeal. Accordingly, he prayed for an opportunity for filing an objection to the application for condonation of delay and remand of the case to the District Judge for fresh hearing and disposal of the same on merit.

39. Mr Ruhul Quddus, learned Advocate for the petitioner, opposed such prayer on the apprehension that any remand would give the opposite parties unwanted opportunity to oppose the application for condonation of delay on assertions, about which they had no knowledge. At the same time, he could not avoid his predicament that the petitioner as next friend of the deity presented the appeal without any permission of the Court under Order XXXII, rules 1 and 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He submitted with citations of authorities that such bonafide mistake could be corrected even by this Division.

40. I have considered the prayer for remand of the opposite parties and also that of the petitioner for permission to appeal as next friend. No application was however made by the petitioner before me for permission to appeal on behalf of the deity. I am also not unaware of the dearth of expertise on the Hindu Law in the Bar. Omission to seek the necessary permission on behalf of the petitioner to appeal as next friend was definitely due to the fault, or more precisely, for ignorance of the learned Advocate of the petitioner there. The petitioner cannot be held responsible for such mistake. In this regard, no objection was ever raised by the opposite parties. Nor did the learned District Judge notice such requirement of the law.

41. In the aforesaid circumstances, the impugned order cannot be sustained in law, which no doubt, occasioned failure of justice. There is also no escape from the conclusion I could avoid to arrive at that the prayers of the parties could be well taken care of by the District Judge only. And that can only be availed after remand of the case.

42. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

43. Impugned order dismissing the appeal is hereby set aside and the case is sent back on remand to the learned District Judge. He is accordingly directed to hear afresh and dispose of the matter of admission of the above appeal after consideration of the application for condonation of delay upon receipt of an objection that may be filed by the opposite party Nos. 1 to 4 and also the prayer of petitioner for permission to appeal against the ex parte decree dated 29-5-86 as next friend of the deity that may be made by the petitioner.

44. It must be noted by everyone that whatever I have expressed hereinabove touching the merits of the case including the ex parte decree must be understood to have been expressed for the purpose of the above Rule only and would not be binding upon the District Judge. The learned District judge shall be absolutely free to hear afresh and dispose of the matter, which is sent back to him.

45. Parties are directed to maintain status quo in respect of possession until disposal of the aforesaid matter by the learned District Judge.

Send down the record at once.

End.

lawyer:
Ali Imam Khaled Rahim with Muhammad Ashraf-uz-zaman Khan Advocates ----- Far the Petitioner: Md Mamunur Rashid. Advocate -----For the Respondent No.2. 
Sk Hasan Ali Advocate ----- For the Respondent No, 3.
parties:
Trade Multi Plex and another ------ Petitioners
VS
Artha Rin Adalat and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J : In this application under article 102 of the Constitution the petitioners called in question the legality of the order dated 23-11-2008 passed by the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat and Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Jessore in Misc . Case No. 117 of 2008 (Annexure-E to the Writ Petition) rejecting an application tiled by the petitioners under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.

2. Facts necessary for the disposal of the rule in short, are as follows :

3. Petitioner No. 1 Messrs Trade Multi flex and its proprietors petitioner No. 2 Rashed Mehluz Khan took loan of an amount of Taka 4,80,000 from Janata Bank Ltd., Corporate Branch, MK Road. Jessore (hereinafter referred to as the Bank). The loan was subsequently enhanced by-the Bank from time to time. The petitioners repaid some amount of loan on several dates but from the first part of 2006, the petitioners started facing huge loss in the business due to political unrest and others environmental unavoidable circumstances and therefore, they could not pay the loan. Subsequently, the Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2007 before the Artha Rin Adalat and Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Jessore (shortly, the Adalat) on 27-6-2007 for recovery of Taka 11,59,455. The petitioners did not receive the summons of the suit as result of which they could not appear to contest the suit and the suit was ultimately decreed exparte by judgment and decree dated 2-1-2008. Thereafter, the Bank tiled Artha Jari Case No. 41 of 2008 before the Adalat. The Petitioners came to know about the exparte decree and execution case on 26-10-2008 and instantly filed an application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (shortly, the Ain) on 28-10-2008 praying for setting aside the exparte judgment and decree. The said application was registered as Misc. Case No. 117 of 2008. In the Misc Case the Adalat by order dated 29-10-2008 directing the judgment-debtor-petitioners to deposit 10% of the decretal amount within 15 days. Accordingly, the petitioners deposited the said amount on 10-11-2008 but the learned Judge of the Adalat subsequently by the impugned order dated 23-11-2008 disallowed the Misc. Case on the ground of limitation, where-upon this writ petition has been filed by the petitioners and the rule was obtained.

4. Respondent No. 2, the Bank contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying the materials averments made in the writ petition contending inter alia, that all the defendants of Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2003 reside together in the same house. Defendant No. 5 is the mother of defendants Nos. 2-4 of the Artha Rin Suit. Being satisfied with the services of summons/notices in accordance with law, the learned Judge of the Adalat fixed a date for exparte hearing of the suit on 1-9-2007. Defendant No. 5 (petitioner No. 2's mother) appeared in the suit on 12-9-2007 and prayed for time for submitting written statement which was allowed with cost of Taka 5,000. The petitioners also appeared in the Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2007 and prayed for time to file written statement which was also allowed but the petitioners did not file any written statement on the next dates i.e. 19-9-2007 and 22-10-2007. Thereafter, date was fixed for exparte hearing on 31-10-2007 but again the Adalat allowed chance to the petitioners to file written statement on 31-10-2007 and 13-11-2007 but the petitioners and the defendant No. 5 did not file written statement and therefore, the suit was decreed exparte on 2-1-2008. It is evident from the record that the petitioners were well aware about the Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2003 since 19-9-2003 and so, the learned Judge of the Adalat rejected the Misc. Case in accordance with law. The writ petition is misconceived, not maintainable and thus, the rule is liable to be discharged.

5. Respondent No. 3, i.e. auction-purchaser also contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that this respondent purchased the mortgaged property in auction from the Adalat by registered deed No. 10684/2008. dated 26-11-2008. The possession of the property was also handed over to him and he also mutated his name relating to the said property. The petitioners by suppressing the materials facts have tiled this writ petition and obtained the rule.

6. The petitioners also filed an affidavit-1 reply to the affidavit-in-oppositions contenting, inter alia, that defendant Nos. 1-5 neither received any summons of Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2003 nor they appeared before the Adalat at any time. So the appearance of the petitioners and the defendant No. 5 in the Artha Rin Suit are act of forgery committed by some interested quarters and the petitioners had no knowledge about the exparte judgment and decree and execution case.

7. Mr Ali Imam Khaled Rahim, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the petitioners and defendant No. 5 did not receive any summons of the suit and therefore, they were and able to appear in the suit and contest it which resulted in the exparte judgment and decree and the petitioners had no knowledge about filing of the execution case. He next submits that defendant No.5 the mother of the petitioner No. 2 as well as the petitioners did not appears in the Artha Rin Sit ad if their appearance is shown' in the suit those are acts of forgery committed by interested quarters. He lastly submits that after knowing about the judgment and decree as well as about the execution case the petitioners immediately appeared before the Adalat and filed an application under section 19 of the Ain for restoration of the suit setting aside the ex-parte judgment and decree and the petitioners also deposited 10% of the decretal dues as per order of the Adalat but the learned Judge of the Adalat without deciding the claim of the petitioners on merit on taking evidence rejected the Misc. Case holding illegally that the petitioners were well aware about the filing of the suit long before and the Misc. Case 'was barred. by limitation and therefore, the rule is liable to be made absolute.

8. In reply, Mr. Md Mamunur Rashid, the learned Advocate for the Bank submits that the impugned order was passed by the learned Judge of the Adalat on the basis of materials on record lawfully. He next submits that writ petition is not maintainable against the order passed by the learned Judge of the Adalat on the basis of materials on record lawfully. He next submits that writ petition is not maintainable against the order passed by the learned Judge of the Adalat and therefore, the rule is liable to be discharged.

9. Mr. Alhaj Sk. Hasan Ali, the learned Advocate for the auction-purchaser-respondent also submits that the impugned order passed by the learned Judge of the Adalat is based on the materials on record. He further submits that the instant writ petition is not maintainable in view of the provisions of section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and as such, the rule is liable to be discharged.

10. We have heard the learned Advocates for both sides. Perused the writ petition, affidavits-in- oppositions, affidavit-in-reply and the materials on record.

11. It has been categorically stated in the application tiled by the petitioners under section 19 of the Ain (Annexure-D to the Writ Petition) that the petitioners did not receive any summons/notices as a result of which they could not appears in the suit or in the execution case earlier.

12. Form the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Bank, it appears that the defendant No. 5 moth-er of the petitioner appeared but it has been claimed by the petitioners by filing an affidavit-in-reply that defendant No. 5 or the other defendants never appeared in the suit or in the execution case and their appearance if shown in the suit, are act of forgery by some interested quarters.

13. Be that as it may, the question as to whether the petitioners and defendant No. 5 appeared to contest the suit or no being disputed question of fact cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction without taking evidence. Moreover, the petitioners filed this writ petition against an order dated 23-11-2008 disallowing the Misc Case No. 117 of 2008 filed under section 19 of the Ain. Therefore, the petitioners remedy is before the appellate forum in view of the provision of section 41 of the Ain.

<u>14. Furthermore, it has been decided in an unreported case by judgment dated 17-8-2010 passed in Writ Petition No. 5746 of 2005 (the Oriental Bank Ltd vs Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka and others) by this Division as under:</u>

<u>"Therefore, it transpires that section 41(1) of the Ain provides that if any party to a Manila is aggrieved by an order or decree, he is to prefer an appeal against the said order or decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat within 30 days. Under section 44 of the Ain interlocutory orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot be challenged in appellate and revisional jurisdiction and so, writ petitions are maintainable against interlocutory orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Therefore, it transpires that the orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat which are not interlocutory orders are appellate orders inasmuch as the words' order or decree" it has used in sub-section (1) of section 41 of the Ain. On going through the entire provisions of section 41 of the Ain it does not appears that the word" order" is meant only for the orders passed under section 19(2) of the Ain. Therefore, the order rejecting of execution case being a final order of the Adalat, the petitioner is to file an appeal against said order and the writ petition is not maintainable."</u>

15. The view taken in the said decision is also applicable in the instant case. In view of the above, we find that this writ petition is not maintainable. As it is found that this it petition is not maintainable, we do not like to embark upon the order issues touching the merit thereof.

16. Accordingly, the rule is discharged without any order as in costs.

17. However, the petitioners are at liberty to file an appeal in appropriate forum within 30 days from the date of receipt of judgment.

18. The order of stay granted earlier by the Court stands vacated.

19. Communicate the judgment to respondent No. 1 at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam with Samarendra Nath Biswas Advocates -----For the Petitioners
None Appears ----- For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Saroj Kumar Sarkar and others ------ Petitioners
VS
Monoj Kumar Sarkar ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This application under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure originates out of First Appeal No. 15 of 1988 which also arises from Partition Suit No. 64 of 1986 before this Court and also originates from First Appeal No.15 of 1988 which also arises out of Title Suit No. 96 of 1984 in the Court of Munsif, Manikgonj.

2. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Manikgonj on behalf of Monoj Kumar Sarker alias Moinal Sarker filed Partition Suit No. 64 of 1986 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Manikgonj claiming a share therein stating that Monoj Kumar Sarker, a co-sharer in the suit land, has left for India and his share has become enemy property and the property requires partition.

3. Motish Chandra Sarker and Saroj Kumar Sarker, brothers of Monoj Kumar Sarker, on the other hand, filed Title Suit No. 96 of 1984 in the Court of the Munsif, Manikgonj in respect of the selfsame property. Subsequently the suit was transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, Manikgonj, for analogous hearing with the aforesaid Partition Suit No. 64 of 1986 and the same was renumbered as Title Suit No. 138 of 1985. In that suit plaintiff claimed that their co-sharer, Monoj Kumar Sarker, left for India in the year 1952 and died their in the year 1954 and on his death they have inherited his share.

4. The aforesaid two suits were heard analogously and by the judgment and decree dated 31-8-1987, the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the Suit No. 138 of 1985 filed by the petitioner Saroj Kumar Sarker and others and decreed Partition Suit No. 64 of 1986 filed by the Government on behalf of Monoj Kumar Sarker.

5. Against the judgment and decree in Suit No. 64 of 1986, the defendants of the said suit i.e. the petitioners, have filed an appeal being Title Appeal No. 15 of 1988 before this Court and same is pending for hearing.

6. Against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 138 of 1985, the plaintiff of the said suit i.e. the petitioners, filed an appeal being Title Appeal No. 197 of 1987 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Manikgonj and same is also pending for hearing.

7. The appellants of First Appeal No. 15 of 1988 as petitioners filed an application under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for withdrawing the Title Appeal No. 197 of 1985 pending in the Court of District Judge, Manikgonj and for transferring the same to this Court for analogous hearing with First Appeal No. 15 of 1988.

8. No one appears on behalf of the opposite parties.

9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that Title Suit No. 64 of 1986 and Title Suit No. 138 of 1985 having been heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge, Manikgonj by a single judgment and, as such, the First Appeal No. 15 of 1988 arising out of Title Suit No. 64 of 1986 pending before this Court  and Title Appeal No. 197 of 1987 arising out of Title Suit No. 138 of 1985 now pending before the learned District Judge, Manikgonj require to be heard analogously and for that purpose it is necessary for ends of justice to transfer Title Appeal No. 197 of 1987 from the Court of District Judge, Manikgonj to this Court, so that matter can be heard analogously with First Appeal No. 15 of 1988 pending before this Court. He further submits that if the aforesaid two appeals are heard separately, there may be the possibility of contradictory judgments.

10. In support of his contention he cited the decision in the case of Rosamma Joseph vs PC Sabastian reported in AIR 1996 Kerala 113.

11. The point for determination is, whether Title Appeal No. 197 of 1987 can be withdrawn from the Court of learned District Judge, Manikgonj for transferring the same to this Court for analogous hearing with First Appeal No. 15 of 1988.

12. Now let us see the provision of law in respect of transfer and withdrawal of Suit and appeal which is envisaged in section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure:

"24. (1) on the application of any of the parties and after notice to the parties and after hearing such of them as desire to be heard, or of its own motion without such notice, the High Court Division or the District Court may at any stage.

(a) transfer any suit, appeal or other proceeding pending before it for trial or disposal to any Court subordinate to it an-d competent to try or dispose of the same, or

(b) withdraw any suit, appeal or other proceeding pending in any Court subordinate to it,

and

(i) Try or dispose of the same; or

(ii) transfer the same for trial or disposal to any Court subordinate to it and competent to try

or dispose of the same; or

(iii) retransfer the same for trial or disposal to the Court from which it was withdrawn.

(2) Where any suit or proceeding has been transferred or withdrawn under sub-section

(1), the Court which thereafter tries such suit may, subject to any special directions in the case of any order of transfer, either retry it or proceed from the point at which it was transferred or withdrawn.

(3) For the purpose of this section, Courts of Additional and Assistant Judges shall be deemed to be subordinate to the District Court.

(4) The Court trying any suit transferred or withdrawn under this section from a Court of Small Causes shall, for the purpose of such suit, be deemed to be a Court of Small Causes."

13. This section confers a general power to transfer, withdraw and retransfer suits, appeals or other proceedings at any stage on the application of a party. The power of the High Court and District Judge are concurrent, The Court may also exercise the power suo motu. The section empowers the Court to transfer a suit to itself and to retransfer it to the Court where it was filed after passing an interim order.

14. The High Court Division has power to transfer an appeal to itself suo motu though appeal lies to the District Court. High Court can under section 24 transfer from its file a suit to a District Court.

15. We receive support of the above view in the case of Ayesha vs Daleep A 1961 Raj 186 and in the case of Geyer vs GA 1949 L 34.

16. Where two suits arise from common questions of law and both suits should be tried at same place and by same Judge and where properties and subject matter of two suits are one and same and the common question of law and facts are also same, but there is no bar to try these sorts of cases analogously.

17. Before deciding the question involved ill this case, it is necessary to find out what are the guidelines for exercise of power of transfer and withdrawal of the suit under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure confers general power to transfer and withdraw the suits and proceedings by the High Court and the District Court. The language of section 24 is very wide and there is no restriction in the way of exercising this power by the High Court on suitable cases. It can be exercised by the Court either on the application of any party or of its own motion and at any stage of the suit. It may well be discerned that the provisions contained in section 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure will not stand in the way of exercising the power under section 24. Section 15 of the Code only requires institution of the suit in the Court of the lowest grade competent to try it. It does not preclude transfer of a suit so instituted to a Court of superior grade. In this case the appeal which is pending before the District Judge, Manikgonj, is sought to be tried by the High Court Division. Where there are two suits which raise certain common question of fact and law, having a substantial bearing on the decision of each of the cases, it is obviously desirable that they should be tried at the same place and by the same Judge. The involvement of common question of law and fact is not the only ground authorising the transfer of suits under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is only illustrative and not exhaustive. This is paramountly a matter involving the satisfaction of the Court which exercises the power. What we want to say is that when certain common questions of facts having a substantial bearing on the decision of both the cases, they should be tried together. Even if the facts of the suits sought to be tried together are intertwined with cause of action in each suit, the transfer of suit may not be refused provided the parties and subject matter of the suits are one and the same. When the Court sees that facts intertwined with the different causes of action are separated and suits tried independently would result in conflicting decisions, it can allow the transfer and joint trial.

18. In the instant case, the litigating parties as analysed hereinbefore in both the suits are one and the same and the subject matter involved in both the suits are common having a substantiai bearing on the decisions of both the cases and if these two appeals are not tried analogously there is every possibility of conflicting decisions.

19. In this case the petitioner has filed the application for transfer of the appeal, the respondent has not opposed it by filing any counter-affidavit, and there is no objection at all which presumed that there is no chance of being prejudiced by the other side.

<u>20. In the instant case not only the parties are same or question of law is same both the suits were tried analogously by the learned Subordinate Judge, Manikgonj. Thus it appears to us that all the grounds of withdrawing of the appeal from the Court of District Judge have been mitigated and there is no apprehension of injustice if the appeal is withdrawn and transferred to this Court, rather such transfer will do Justice to the parties. The High Court in such circumstances has unfettered power under .section 24(1) (b) of the Code of Civil Procedure with regard to the transfer and withdrawal of the appeal.</u>

21. In the light of the above discussion, we are of the view that the application under section 24 merits consideration.

<u>22. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the Title Appeal No. 197 of 1987 pending in the Court of the District Judge Manikgonj is withdrawn and transferred to this Court for hearing along with the First Appeal No. 15 of 1988 analogously.</u>

Communicate.

End.

lawyer:
Dr Md Eunus Ali Akond with Fazlul Haque. Advocates ------- For the Petitioners. 
Md Rafiqul Islam (Heru) with Abul Kalam Mainuddin. Advocates ------- For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Alam Taj Begum @ Monowar Begum & others  ------- Petitioners 
Vs.
 Nimai Chandra Roy ------- Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the defendant petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 29-1-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court No.1, Borguna in Title Appeal No.2 of 2001 reversing the judgment and decree dated 15-11-2000 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Borguna Sadar, Borguna in Title Suit No, 115 of 1998 should not be set aside and or pass such other or further order or others as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Short facts of the case are as follows: 
The opposite party No.1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.115/98 before the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Borguna Sadar, Borguna praying for declaration of title stating, inter alia, that the suit land is 6 decimals of land of Plot No.351 which belonged to Rajendra Chandra who died leaving 4 (four) sons namely (l) Suchil, (2) Monindra (3) Sudhir (4) Nimai and one wife; that after death of Rajendra his heirs have been living separately; that at the time of death of Rajendra his son Nimai Chandra Roy was a minor who is the plaintiff of the instant suit and that when the plaintiff has been living separately then his other 3 brothers transferred the 18 decimals of land on 17-2-73 by 4 deeds to the defendant Nos.I-4; that the plaintiff's name was shown in the serial number 4 of the said deed dated 17-2-73 which are illegal, without lawful authority; that the 6 decimals of land showing in the aforesaid deeds and showing the defendant No.5 as guardian of the plaintiff is illegal; that the defendant No.5 is not the legal Guardian of the minor; he was not appointed as guardian by the Court; the plaintiff could not know anything earlier about aforesaid deeds; the plaintiff could know on 12-10-98 about the aforesaid deeds and accordingly, instituted the instant suit. 

3. The defendant Nos.I-4 contested the suit denying all material allegations of the plaint and stating, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable; the suit is barred by Limitation; the suit is bad for defect of parties; that after death of Rajendra, his sons had been living jointly and that on 17-2-73 the plaintiff and defendant Nos.5-7, transferred the 24 decimals of land of Plot No.351 to the defendant Nos.I-4 vide 4 deeds Nos.391/392/393/394 and handed over possession of the suit land; the defend- ant Nos.I-4 had been possessing the said 24 decimals of land; the defendant Nos.I-4 mutated their names vide mutation case Nos.249/73-74, 250/73- 74, 251/73-74, and 252/73-74; that the defendant No.5 Monindra Chandra Roy was appointed guardian of the plaintiff; the plaintiff had knowledge about the aforesaid deeds; the plaintiff's claim is false and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. The suit was heard by the Senior Assistant Judge, Borguna who dismissed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 15-11-2000 and 21-11-2000. against which the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.2/2001 before the District Judge, Borguna and the same appeal was beard by the joint district Judge, 1st Court, Borguna who allowed in appeal vide judgment and decree dated 29-1-2002 and 5-2- 2002 and decreed the suit. 

5. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid appellate judgment and decree, the defendant-petitioners obtained the present Rule. 

6. Dr Md Eunus Ali Akond Advocate along with Mr Fazlul Huque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, placed the revisional application, the impugned judgments and decrees, and the depositions of the PWs and DWs on record and submitted that the learned trial Court on considering the evidence and materials on record having found that the plaintiff could not prove his case and having dismissed the suit, the learned appellate Court on misreading the evidence and materials on record illegally allowed the appeal. The learned Advocate further submitted that the learned appellate Court without considering the facts and circumstances of the case illegally held that the disputed deeds were obtained by the defend- ant petitioners by practicing fraud upon the plaintiff who was minor at the relevant time and illegally held that when fraud is proved the question of limitation does not arise. The learned Advocate further submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the case, Article 44 of the Limitation Act is applicable, but the learned appellate Court illegally held that Article 120 of the Limitation Act is applicable in the present case and accordingly, com- mitted error in law in allowing the appeal. The learned Advocate further submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the present case Article 44 of the Limitation Act is applicable and under the said Article there is no provision for counting the limitation from the alleged knowledge of the plaintiff about the disputed deed and, as such, the learned appellate Court committed gross error in allowing the appeal holding that from the date of knowledge of the plaintiff the suit has been filed within time. 

7. Mr Md Rafiqul Islam (Heru), the learned Advocate along with Mr Abul Kalam Mainuddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party, on the other hand, submitted that the learned appellate Court on considering the evidence of the PWs and DWs on record rightly allowed the appeal and in the absence of any misreading or non consideration of the material evidence on record, the finding of fact as arrived at by the learned appellate Court being final it cannot be interfered with by this Court in revision. The learned Advocate further submitted that having regard to the fact that the mother of the plaintiff being alive at the relevant time none of the other brothers can be the natural guardian of the minor Nimai and in the present case Monindra, one of the three adult brothers of Nimai, having executed and registered the disputed deed on behalf of minor Nimai, the deed is a void one and in the present case Article 120 of the Limitation Act is applicable and the learned appellate Court rightly found that the plaintiffs suit is not barred by limitation. The learned Advocate further submitted that in the deed there is no reference of legal necessity of the minor, no such evidence also has been adduced by the defendant to prove that the disputed transfer was for legal necessity of the minor arid, as such, the learned appellate Court rightly allowed the appeal holding that the disputed deed is a void one. 

8. On perusal, it appears, the learned trial Court held that the plaintiff as PW 1 deposed in the case and his present age is 40 years, his age at the time of execution of the disputed deed dated 17-2- 1973 was 13 years and that the plaintiff attained the majority in -1978 and he filed the present suit in 1998, so according to the learned trial Court, he filed suit after 20 years of his attaining majority and after 2S years of the date of execution and registration of the deed. The learned trial Court held that the plaintiff did not file the suit within three years of his attaining majority and 12 years from the date of the disputed deed and, as such, the suit is barred by limitation. The learned trial Court further found that the defendant No.5, brother of the plaintiff being the karta of the Hindu family, executed and registered the deed on behalf of the minor and, as such the deed is a genuine and valid one and that by the said deed defendant acquired good title in the suit land and that the deed has been acted upon. The learned trial Court further held that the suit as framed is not maintainable without praying for cancellation of the disputed deed under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act. On these findings the learned trial Court dismissed the suit. 

9. On appeal, the learned appellate Court, on the other hand, held that there is no reference in the deed itself and that there is no evidence also to show that the suit land was transferred for legal necessity of the minor and, as such, the deed is void ab initio. The learned appellate Court further found that the defendant No.5 the brother of the minor plaintiff, at the relevant time, had no locus standi or legal authority to transfer the suit land on behalf of the minor. The learned appellate, Court further held that the suit as framed is maintainable without prayer for cancellation of the disputed deed. The learned appellate Court further found that the present suit being a suit for declaration that the disputed deed is a void one Article 120 of the Limitation Act is applicable and held that the suit having been filed within 6 years from the date of his knowledge dated 12-10- 1998 suit is not barred by limitation. The learned appellate Court further found that the plaintiff was able to prove his possession in the suit land. The learned appellate Court further found that the defendants initially having claimed title - in the suit land by the disputed 4 deeds dated 17-2-1973 cannot claim title by adverse possession subsequently as there is a legal bar in claiming title at the same time by two alternative ways. The learned appellate Court then held that the disputed 4 deeds dated 17- 2-1973 are void and the defendants did not acquire any title in the suit land. With these findings the learned appellate Court allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial Court. 

10. On perusal of the judgment passed by the Courts below and pleading of the parties, it appears, admittedly 4 deeds were jointly executed and registered on 17-2-1973 by 4 brothers namely Sudhir Chandra Roy, Sushil Chandra Roy, Monindra Chandra Roy and Nimai Chandra Roy (minor), admittedly by these 4 deeds 24 decimals of land has been transferred out of 35 decimals of land of plot No. 351, admittedly in each of the 4 deeds said 4 brothers including the minor were the executants, so each deed was for 6 decimals of land. Admittedly Nimai was a minor at that time and admittedly Monindra Chandra Roy executed each deed for himself as well as natural guardian of minor Nimai. It appears, in the schedule of the plaint in schedule- Ka reference of said 4 separate deeds have been given. In schedule-Kha 13 separate plots have been mentioned out of which the suit land has been shown to be 6 decimals of land only in plot No. 351 and no boundary of said 6 decimals has been given in the schedule of the plaint. It may be noted that in each of the 4 deeds the area of land has been mentioned as 6 decimals and minor Nimal has been named in each deed, so it cannot be said with certainty, that which 6 decimals of land which is the share of the plaintiff is covered by which deed. Thus, it appears, the specification of the suit land was not proper. Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that the description of the suit land must be specific and if necessary, the specific boundary should be given. The present suit is a suit for declaration of title as well as the 4 deeds are void. So it is a suit for declaration simplicitor in which specification of the suit land is a must. Thus I find that the suit land is vague, unspecified and for this defect also the suit should fail, however, this aspect of the case was not considered by any of the Courts below. 

11. Moreover, in this suit the factum of possession is a very material thing and the learned trial Court held that the plaintiff could not prove his possession in the suit land, but the learned appellate Court held that the plaintiff could prove his possession in the suit land. Admittedly by the said 4 deeds 24 decimals of land have been transferred by 4 brothers including the plaintiff and out of this 24 decimals plaintiffs claim is for 6 decimals. In the schedule of the plaint the plaintiff has shown this 6 decimals in plot No. 351 out of 13 plots. There is no case by the plaintiff that by amicable partition among the brothers the plaintiff got said 6 decimals of land and he is in possession of that 6 decimals of land. The plaintiff in his examination in-chief stated that he is in possession of the suit land. To the query of the Court, plaintiff stated that there is a 'doba' in suit plot No. 351 and that the plaintiff along with his other brothers are the owners of that ditch and the defendants do not use the said ditch and that the defendants land is to the eastern side of that ditch. In cross-examination he could not say how much land he got from his father and he could not say how much land he sold out. He also could not tell how much land he got. He denied the suggestion that at the instance of his brothers he filed the present suit. He further stated that he paid tax including municipal tax for the suit land, but he had not paid tax for the present year. He stated that he cannot produce the rent receipt for the suit land. He stated that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 made a wall in the northen direction in the suit land for their share. He also stated that the defendant Nos. I and 2 made a wall in the southern side of plot No. 351 PW 2 who is the husband of the sister of the plaintiff in his cross- examination stated that he cannot tell how much land the plaintiff possesses in the suit dag. He stated that the defendant Nos. 1-4 have a house in the northern bank of the ditch and that they are in possession by placing a fence. He stated that he does not know how much land of the disputed deed the plaintiff possesses. PW 3 Monindra Chandra Roy stated in his examination in-chief that the plaintiff possesses the suit land, but in cross-examination he stated that he does not know the dag and khatian number of the suit land. The defendant examined 2 DWs including the defendant No.3. It appears, regarding possession of the defendant, they corroborated each other and no material contradiction came out from their cross-examination. 

12. Admittedly the defendants purchased 24 decimals of land by 4 deeds in which plaintiff claims 6 decimals of land. In the schedule of the plaint 6 decimals of land out of plot No. 351 is the suit land. Admittedly, no boundary of the suit land has been given. In the plaint and deposition of the plaintiff nothing has been stated that by amicable partition he got the 6 decimals of land in Plot No. 351. 

13. It appears, the case of the plaintiff is that the defendants possess the rest 18 decimals of land out of24 decimals of land. Plaintiff as PW 1 admitted in his deposition that the defendants are in possession of some portion of suit land by constructing wall. PW 2 stated in his deposition that the defendants Nos. 1 and 2 also are in possession of some portion of the suit land by constructing wall. All the DWs also corroborated each other regarding possession of the defendants in the suit land. Thus from the deposition of the PWs and DWs it is clear that the plaintiff could not prove his exclusive possession in the suit land of which no specific boundary (of said 6 decimals out of 24 decimals) has been given. So, in my opinion, the finding of possession as arrived at by the learned appellate Court is illegal and not sustainable in law. 

14. Regarding limitation the learned trial Court found that the suit is barred by limitation, the learned appellate Court, on the other hand, found that the suit is not barred by limitation. According to the appellate Court, Article 120 is applicable in the case and the suit having been filed within 6 years from the date of knowledge of the deed dated 12-10- 1998 the suit is well within time. 

15. Now let me consider the question of limitation. It appears, the specific case of the plaintiff is that during his minority, his brother Monindra Chandra Roy executed the deed on his behalf as natural guardian and he had no earlier knowledge about the said deed and that on 12-10-1998, he for the first time came to know about the disputed deed and accordingly, filed the suit on 29-11-1998. Article 44 of the Limitation Act provides for setting aside a transfer of property by guardian of the minor which reads as follows: 
"By a ward who has attained majority, to set aside a transfer of property by his guardian, period of limitation is 3 years and the period will run when the ward attains majority." 

16. It appears, in the said article there is no provision for filing a suit from the date of knowledge of such disputed deed. In other words, in order to challenge a transfer of the property of the minor by the guardian, the minor can file a suit within 3 years of his attaining majority. Reference may be given to the case of Sultan Ahmed vs Fazlul Kabir reported in 5 DLR 383. Wherein it has been held that limitation for filing a suit is 3 years from the date when the disability ceases. In the present case in view of article 44 of the Limitation Act, in my opinion, the limitation will be 3 years from the date of attaining majority of the plaintiff. It appears, the plaintiff was aged 13 years when the disputed deed dated 17-2-1973 was executed and, as such, he attained majority in the year 1978-1979 and he could file a suit by 1981 or 1982, but it appears, the present suit was filed on 29-11-1992, after about 10112 years of his attaining majority. So, in my opinion, the suit is barred by limitation. 

17. Since I have found above that suit is bad for want of specification, and that the plaintiff failed to prove his possession in the suit land and that the suit is barred by limitation, in my opinion, the learned appellate Court committed gross error in law in allowing the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree which are liable to be set aside. 

18. In the result; the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court are set aside and those of the trial Court dismissing the suit are affirmed and maintained. 

19. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. 

Send down the LC Records immediately. 

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Md. Kazal Rashid, Advocate ----- For the petitioners 
Mr. Ranjan Kumar Chakrovorty, Advocate ----- For the opposite parties
parties:
Md. Abul Kalam Azad and another ----- Defendant-Appellant-Petitioners
Versus
Khurshid Mia being dead his heirs: A. Majid and others ----- Plaintiff-Respondent Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties No.1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 20.04.2015 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Rajbari, in Miscellaneous Appeal No.05 of 2010 dismissing the appeal affirming the judgment and order dated 01.02.2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1St Court, Rajbari in Miscellaneous Case NO.06 of 2006 arising out of Title Suit No.05 of 1997 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties No.1-3 as plaintiffs instituted the original Partition Suit being No.05 of 1997 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Rajbari against the defendant-petitioners and others. In that suit the plaintiffs for want of getting a separate shaham in respect of the land described in the schedule of the plaint submitted their pleadings and ultimately that suit was decreed by the learned trial Judge on 20.05.1999 and decree was signed on 08.07.1999. After getting the decree the plaintiffs being not satisfied filed a Title Appeal being No.52 of 1999 in the Court of learned District Judge, Rajbari and the learned appellate court allowed the appeal ex-parte and modified the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. Thereafter, the present petitioners filed a Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the 1StCourt of learned Joint District Judge, Rajbari for setting aside the judgment and decree being Miscellaneous Case No.06 of 2006. The learned trial Court after examining the witnesses disallowed the miscellaneous case by his judgment and order dated 01.02.2010. 

3. Being aggrieved the defendant-petitioners preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.05 of 2010 in the Court of learned District Judge, Rajbari which was transmitted to the Court of learned Additional District Judge, Rajbari for hearing and disposal. The learned Additional District Judge, Rajbari hearing the appeal by the impugned judgment and order dated 20.04.2015 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and order passed by the learned trial court. 

4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order the defendant-appellant-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay. 

5. During hearing of this Rule Mr. Md. Kazal Rashid, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Ranjan Kumar Chakrovorty, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties. 

6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original case filed under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and subsequent appeal committed illegality and irregularity resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the petitioners were admittedly defendants to the original partition suit, but there is no service of
summons notice in their names and the plaintiff-opposite party to the Miscellaneous Case being No.06 of 2006 have hopelessly failed to discharge his onus in proving that, there was any service of notice upon the present defendant-petitioners, but neither the lower appellate court nor the trial court arrived at a conclusive decision adverting evidence therein on the service of notice; causing failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that challenging the service of summons under Order V rule 17 and rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure the defendant-petitioner-appellants instituted their miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the petitioners specifically asserted that there was no service of summons notice upon them. The learned Advocate submits that under the ambit of law the onus of proof lies upon the plaintiff to prove that the summons were duly served upon the defendant-petitioners, but they have failed to discharge their onus of proof by any tangible evidence. The learned Advocate in support of his contention referred some decisions of our Apex Court reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162, 16 BLD(AD)4 and 9 MLR(AD)158 and two decisions of this Court reported in 25 DLR 91, and 1990 BLD 151. 

7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel on behalf of the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that neither the trial court nor the lower appellate court during disposal of the original case and its subsequent appeal committed any illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the summons were duly served upon the defendant-petitioners in their own address under Order V rule 17 and 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure and both the courts below being satisfied opined that, in despite of service of notice upon the defendants; suppressing the facts they have filed the original miscellaneous case and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate in support of this submissions referred a decision of our Apex Court reported in 4 MLR (AD) 405. 

8. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates and have gone through the judgment and order passed by the trial court and the appellate court passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 05 of 2010 along with the connected papers. I have also perused the decisions referred to above by the learned counsels for the parties concerned. 

9. Having gone through the papers on records it transpires that the present petitioners who were the defendants to the original Partition Suit being No.05 of 1997 raised a specific plea that, in that suit there was no service of summons notice upon them and for the reason stated, they were in the dark about the original suit and its decree. It was further case of the defendant-petitioners that in the subsequent appeal which was decreed in modified form was also not within the knowledge of them inasmuch as there was no service of summons notice upon them and in collusion with the process-server of the court the summons notices were suppressed by the plaintiffs. 

10. On meticulous consideration over the relevant papers it appears that after the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No.52 of 1999 the original case record was sent back to the trial court. It is obvious to note that the decree was passed in the preliminary form and before its final decree the defendant-petitioners instituted the original Miscellaneous Case No.06 of 2006 under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the service of notice upon them. It is further noticed that the learned trial court bypassing the mandatory provisions of law as incorporated in Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure only on point of limitation disallowed the case. Subsequently; while the matter was placed before the lower appellate court in the form of appeal, the learned appellate court below in slip shod manner without proper appreciation of law as provided in the relevant provisions laid down in Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure decided the merit of the appeal against the appellants therein. 

11. It is a fact that, in the original suit the service of summons was allegedly done under Order V rule 17 and 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure and subsequent to that, the defendants challenging that service of notice; instituted the Miscellaneous Case being No.06 of 2006 before the learned trial court and in that case it was their pleading that in fact there was no service upon them and the serving officer in collusion with the plaintiff served the summons notice after hanging. In the instant nature of case limitation is no doubt immaterial if it is proved that in fact there is no service of summons upon the defendants. The burden of proof in the instant case lies upon the plaintiffs to prove that in fact the service was done and the defendants suppressing the facts of , service of notice upon then raised their plea on non-service of summons. It was 
the incumbent duty upon the learned court below to examine the serving official viz. the process-server; who made a declaration that he served the summons after hanging. In the case laws reported in 36 DLR (AD)248 and 5 BLD(AD)59 examination of the serving officer is mandatory. Besides this; when the process server returns the summons with a declaration that he served the summons by hanging in presence of witness, it cannot justify the recording in the order-sheet as a matter of routine "summons duly served." Rule 19A cannot be raised to take away - the responsibility of the court as provided in Rule 19 of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

12. Apart from this; on the ground of non service of summons the prime consideration before the Court is to satisfy itself as to whether the plaintiff has been able to prove that summons was duly served upon the defendant. Once the defendant denies service of summons upon him the whole onus shifts to the plaintiff who has to prove satisfactorily that summons was in fact duly served. [Ref. Md. Wazed Ali Sardar —vs.- Md. Afsaruddin Sardar and others 16 BLD (AD)4]. 

13. In the instant case; as I have come across from the relevant papers on records that the plaintiff have hopelessly failed to discharge his onus of proof that the summons notice in fact was duly served upon the defendant under Order V rule 17 and 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Neither the concerned process-server nor the witness in presence of whom the alleged service was done, was examined by the learned court below before arrival  at a decision that in fact there was service of summons upon the defendant-petitioners. It is required to be mentioned here that, due to distinguishable character the decision cited by Mr. Ranjan Kumar Chakrovorty is not applicable in this instant case. 

14. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and the discussions referred to above, I am constrained to hold such a view that the learned appellate court below in passing the impugned judgment and order committed gross illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the impugned judgment and order is not sustainable in law. 

15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 20.04.2015 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Rajbari, in Miscellaneous Appeal No.05 of 2010 dismissing the appeal affirming the judgment and order dated 01.02.2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, IS` Court, Rajbari in Miscellaneous Case No.06 of 2006 arising out of the Title Suit No.05 of 1997 is hereby set aside. 

16. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. 

17. Communicate the judgment and order immediately. 

End.

lawyer:
Md Sirajul Huq, Advocate ------ For the Petitioners 
Khair Ezaz Masud with ATM Obaidul Hussain, Advocates ------ For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
AKM Abu Sayed Chowdhury  ------ Petitioners
Vs.
AKM. Abdul Wahed Chowdhury and others  ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of plaintiffs-petitioners calls in question the judgment and decree dated 22-1-2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali in Title Appeal No. 126 of 2000 affirming the judgment and decree dated 14- 5-2000 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Companygonj in Title Suit No. 66 of 1996 decree the suit.

2. The short facts which have given rise to the Rule are as follows: the petitioners as plaintiffs filed Title Suit being No. 66 of 1996 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Companygonj Noakhali against the opposite parties paying for cancellation of decree and not binding upon the plaintiffs; that the case of the plaintiffs is that Sultan Mahmud of village Charkali, PS Companygonj District Noakhali retired from service in 1970 and in 1971 while he fell in financial crisis, he proposed to sell the lands measuring an area 6.54 acres of land described in the schedule of the plaint to his grandsons and son's wife at a consideration of Taka 2500 and accordingly executed a sale deed on 8-5-1971 and delivered the said land to the plaintiffs on 15-8-1996 and that at the time of taking accounts of lands in between the plaintiff No. 1 and defendant No.1, it was disclosed that the defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 115 of 1974 and obtained a decree cancelling the sale deed dated 18-5-1971. It is further stated that on 20-8-1996 the plaintiffs obtaining the certified copy, defmitely came to know that the suit, which was decreed on 9-8-1997, no summons or notice was served upon the plaintiffs i.e. defendants of Title Suit No. 115 of 1974 and that the plaintiffs were not aware of the said decree and the defendants of Title Suit No. 115 of 1974 did not appear by filing power or engaging an advocate which are forged and fraudulent. Hence the plaintiff filled the suit praying for cancellation of the decree which is not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint, stating, inter alia, that the defendants father Sultan Mahmud had been living at Maijdee town and at that time he became ill in the first part of March, 1971; that the plaintiff No. 1 in collusion with his maternal uncle Golam Rabbani showing his father as vendor and by false personification created a forged deed dated 18-5-1971 and that in fact, Sultan Mahmud had no necessity to sell 6.54 acres of land at consideration of Taka 2500. It is further stated that the defendant No.1 came to know about the said kabala from plaintiff No. 1 and his maternal uncle on 17-11-1974, the defendant obtained certified copy on 22-1-1974 and definitely came to know about the said kabala Thereafter the defendant filed the Title Suit No. 45 of 1974, praying for a decree of declaration that the said kabala is not binding upon him. In the said suit, plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 were defendant Nos. 1 and 2. In the said suit the summons were duly served upon the defendant and the defendant contested the suit by filing written statement by engaging a senior Advocate. In the meantime, the uncle of the defendant No. 1 drafted a solenama by late Advocate Sekandar Mia. The defendant No.1 for himself and for his mother signed the solenama and gave deposition in the Court in support of the solenama. The parties have been possessing their respective share as per Shariat, Solenama is genuine and, as such, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed.

4. The plaintiff examined two witnesses and the defendant examined 4 witnesses. The learned Assistant Judge, Companygonj was pleased to decree the suit by his judgment and decree dated 14- 5-2000 against the defendants and the plaintiff preferred Appeal against the judgment and decree dated 15-6-2000 passed by the Assistant Judge, Companyzgonj before the District Judge, Noakhali which was registered as Title Appeal No. 126 of 2000 and on transfer the Appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali who dismissed the Appeal vide his judgment and decree dated 22-1-2007 affirming the judgment and decree dated 14-5-2000 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Companygonj in Title Suit No. 66 of 1996.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 22-1-2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali, the plaintiff petitioner preferred this revisional application before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr Md Sirajul Huque, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that Sultan Mahmud sold 6.54 acres of land described in the schedule of the plaint to his grandson and son's wife at a consideration of Taka 2,500 and accordingly executed a sale deed on 18-5-1971 and delivered the possession of the said land to the plaintiffs on 15-8-1996 that the decree in Title Suit No. 45 of 1974 are also forged and fraudulent. He further submits that the plaintiff's petitioners are entitled to get decree.

7. Mr Khair Ezaz Masud, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that Sultan Mahmud after his retirement fell ill and the plaintiff No.1 collusively created the deed dated 8-5-1971; that Sultan Mahmud had no necessity to sell 6.54 acres of land and that the plaintiffs did not take possession of the land on the basis of deed dated 8-5-1971. He further submits that decree in the suit in Title Suit No. 45 of 1974 is genuine and summons of that suit was duly served upon the defendants in that suit and they contested the suit by filing written statement engaging a lawyer. He further submits that the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court is correct which calls for no interference by this Court.

8. Now the point for the determination is whether the Court below committed any illegality and material irregularity in passing their respective decision which are occasioning any failure of justice.

9. There is no denying of the fact that the suit land originally belonged to Sultan Mahmud of village Charkali, PS Companygonj District Noakhali. The contention of the plaintiffs petitioners is that for financial crisis Sultan Mahmud sold 6.54 acres of land described in schedule of the plaint to his grandson and son's wife at a consideration of Taka 2,500 and accordingly executed a sale deed on 8-5-1971 and delivered possession of the said land on 15-8- 1996 and he has been possessing the suit land. The further contention of the plaintiffs is that sole decree in Title Suit No. 115 of 1974 was forged and fraudulent and the summons of that suit was not served upon the defendants and sole decree of Title Suit No. 115 of 1974 was obtained collusively which need to be cancelled and which is not binding upon the plaintiffs.

10. On the other hand, the case of the defendants is that grandson and son's wife of Sultan Mahmud collusively obtained the deed dated 8-5- 1971 which is forged and fraudulent and possession of the land was not delivered on the basis of that deed. The further contention of the defendants opposite parties is that the defendant as plaintiff filed TS No. 115 of 1974 cancelling sale deed dated 8-5- 1971 and that the Suit was compromised on the basis solenama on 9-8-1997 which is genuine.

11. Both the parties adduced evidence on the trial Court and the trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record it appears that the summons of Title Suit No. 115 of 1974 was served upon the defendant and suit was decreed on the basis of solenama on 9-8-1997. It further appears that the deed dated 8-5-1971 is collusive and the land of the deed in question was not delivered upon the plaintiffs and the sole decree dated 9-8-1997 is genuine.

12. The learned Assistant Judge, Companygonj on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record and as per provision of law legally dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 14-5-2000 and the crafter the plaintiffs petitioners preferred title Appeal No. 126 of 2000 in the Court of District Judge, Noakhali against the decree dated 14-5-2000 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Companygonj and on transfer the Title Appeal No. 126 of 2002 was heard the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali who also considering the facts and circumstances dismissed the Appeal by his judgment and decree dated 22-1-2007.

13. Now let us see how the consistent view as regard the concurrent finding in this respect I may refer the decision in the case Habibur Rahman vs Mobarak Ali reported in 3 MLR (1998)207 = 50 DLR 55 wherein their Lordship held that, when the concurrent finding of fact of the trial Court as well as the Court of Appeal are based on proper appreciation of evidence on record and are not vitiated by the non-reading and misreading of material evidence on record, such findings cannot be interfered within exercise of revisional Jurisdiction, It is a well settled law that unless there is gross misreading and non-consideration of material evidence on record or misconstruction of any document or the finding are perverse and contrary to law or evidence resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, the concurrent finding of fact cannot be interfered with by the revisional Court under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

14. In the present case I did not find any misreading and non-reading in the material evidence or misconstruction of any documentary evidence as such I hold that the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court as well as the lower appellant Court are sustainable in law.

15. The scope of section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is now well settled. Consistent pronouncements by the Highest Court of the country have made it abundantly clear that a Court of revision under section 115(1) of the CPC can interfere with the findings of fact as the final Court of facts only in exceptional circumstances when the findings are shockingly perverse of these are vitiated by non reading and misreading of the materials evidence or misconstruction of any important documents affecting the merit of the suit. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff's petitioners has not been able to find out any such legal infirmity in the impugned judgment which calls for any interference.

16. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, I am of the view that the learned Court of Appeal below on proper consideration of the evidence on record affirmed the judgment passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Companygonj, Noakhali and the findings recorded by the learned Court of Appeal below are well supported by the evidence on record and are based on correct principle of the appreciation of the evidence. I find no illegality in the impugned judgment dated 22-1- 2007 to call for any interference by this Court exercising revisional power.

In the result the revision fails and the Rule is discharged without any Order as to cost.

Sent down the LCR at once.

End.

lawyer:
M Asif Hasan, Advocate------ For the Petitioners. 
Md Jalaluddin, Advocate------ For the Opposite Party Nos. 1(a)-1(c)
parties:
Mokless Uddin Bhiyan  ------ Defendant-Appellant-Petitioner
Vs.
Rabi Chowdhury ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
On an application under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the petitioner the Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 18-2-1999 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 1994 affirming those dated 16-3- 1994 passed by the Assistant Judge, incharge, Singair, Manikganj in Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984 should not be set-aside.

2. The facts for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that opposite party No. 1 as petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984 against the petitioner and others for setting aside the auction sale arising out of Execution Case No.4 of 1975 in pursuance the exparte judgment and decree passed in Money Suit No.4 of 1974. The further case is that he was a Government servant and was posted at Barisal. While he was serving at Barisal without his knowledge and without serving any notice upon him, an ex parte judgment was passed against him on 19-3-1974 and thus Execution case No.4 of 1975 was filed and the present petitioner auction purchased the valuable property of him. The said auction was confirmed on 25-11-1975. The said auction was not in proper, illegal and malafide and the value of the auction money was not proper. The opposite party No.1 came to know the same on 11-078-1976. Hence the case.

3. The case was contested by the present petitioner and the predecessor of the opposite party Nos. 4-13 by filing joint written objection stating interalia that the case of the present opposite party No.1 is false, malafide and barred by limitation. The present opposite party had knowledge about the money suit and decree execution case and auction matter. The auction was never secret and it was sold by open tender. The present opposite party No.1 would not conduct the said Miscellaneous Case and the uncle of the present opposite party No. 1 namely Safiuddin conducted the Miscellaneous Case. The auction purchaser (present petitioner) got the delivery of possession through Court and since then the auction purchaser has been possessing the suit property. The case of the present opposite party No.1 is false and liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj after hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record allowed the said miscellaneous case and setting aside the order of auction dated 25-11-1975 in Money Execution Case No.4 of 1975 by his judgment and order dated 16-3-1994.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order of the trial Court, the present petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 1994 before the District Judge, Manikganj. The said appeal was heard by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Manikganj who after hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record dismissed the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment of the trial Court by his judgment and order dated 18-2-1999.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order of the Courts below, the petitioner filed this revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule.

7. Mr M Asif Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that both the Courts committed error of law resulting in an error of decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the summons was duly served upon the opposite party in Money Execution Case No.4 of 1975 .The learned Advocate further submitted that both Courts below did not consider that the miscellaneous case filed. by the opposite party was barred by limitation since Exhibit-"Kha" proves that the opposite party No. 1 had knowledge about the auction since 2-4-1974 thus they committed error of law. The learned Advocate further submitted that both the Courts erroneously found that there was a irregularity in the auction sale but did not consider that the petitioner got possession over the suit land immediately after the auction sale but the opposite party did not take any initiative at the earliest stage but long after ten years he filed this suit which is absolutely barred by limitation thus both the Courts committed error of law resulting in an error of decision occasioning failure of justice. Thus, he prayed for making the Rule absolute.

8. On the contrary Mr Md lalaluddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 (a)-l(c) submitted that both the Courts concurrently found that the auction which was held by violating the provision of law. The learned Advocate further submitted that both the Courts concurrently found that the notice which was published in a local newspaper but such type of paper has no existence even the present petitioner did not submit the original newspaper thus both the Court concurrently opined that the auction was held by committing fraud upon the Court and since both the Courts found fraud in the auction deed in such a case the limitation is immaterial. The learned Advocate further submitted that concurrent finding of fact cannot be interfered with in revisional .Jurisdiction under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his argument he relying the decisions of the case reported in 32 DLR 168 and 43 DLR (AD) 82. Thus, he prayed for discharging the Rule.

9. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment of the Courts below, papers and documents as available in the records. In the instant case it appears that the Money Suit No. 4 of 1974 was decreed ex parte which was filed for realization of Taka 1,200 thereafter, the petitioner filed Money Execution Case No. 4 of 1975 and accordingly the auction was held and auction was confirmed on 25-11-1975. The opposite party No.1, the petitioner of the Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984 claimed that without any summons and following procedure of law the said auction was held. It appears that the trial Court after discussion of the evidence on record and the procedure of proclamation and the auction of the property found that the same was conducted without following the procedure of law even the ex parte decree which was passed without summons of the petitioner of the Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984. The appellate Court concurred the said finding of facts and both the Courts found that by which substantial injury resulting from the irregularity is proved thus, the Courts below setting aside the auction procedure. It also appears that the trial Court found that the publication of the proclamation in the local Newspaper (Exhibit-"Ka") has no existence in the locality and there is no declaration number, the publisher, the auditor etc and thus clearly opined that which is a fabricated documents. Since both the Courts found that the auction was held by practicing fraud upon the Court so the said concurrent finding of facts cannot be interfered with in revisional application.

<u>10. It is well settle principle that the limitation is immaterial when any order obtained by practicing fraud upon Court. This proposition supported by the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Mashiur Rahman reported in 50 DLR(AD) 205 where in their lordships held.</u>

<u>"It is a cardinal principle of administration of justice that no result of any judicial proceeding should be allowed to receive judicial approval from any Court of law whenever it is obtained by practicing fraud upon the Court; reason being fraud demolishes the very foundation of sanctity of such judicial proceeding. It is also established principle of law that fraud vitiates all judicial proceedings. Thus contravention of the provision of law cannot be a valid ground for allowing an order obtained by fraud to stand."</u>

11. It is settled principle that concurrent finding of fact cannot be interfered with in revisional application when there is no misreading or misappropriation of facts. This proposition supported by the decision of the case of Shambhu Nath Poddar vs Bangladesh Railway reported in 43 DLR (AD) 82 wherein their lordships held -

"A revisional Court acts beyond its jurisdiction in setting-aside concurrent finding of fact, when there is no misreading and mis-appreciation of the evidence on record."

12. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and discussions above I find no merit in the Rule.

13. In the result, the Rule is discharged. However, without any order as to cost. The impugned Judgment and order dated 18-2-1999 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 11 of 1994 affirming those dated 16-3-1994 passed by the Assistant Judge, in-charge, Singair, Manikganj in Miscellaneous Case No. 55 of 1984 are hereby upheld.

14. The order of status quo granted earlier by this Court is hereby recalled and vacated.

Send down the Lower Court's Record at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 23 of 2012.
lawyer:
Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner. 
Khair Azaz Masud, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Head Mistress, Hazrat Shah Ali Girls’ High School, Mirpur, Dhaka -----Petitioner
Vs.
Mohammad Ibrahim and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 11-8-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4596 of 2007).
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This Petition for Leave to Appeal is against the judgment and order dated 11-8-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4596 of 2007 making the Rule absolute and decreeing the suit with a direction upon the defendant opposite parties to appoint the petitioner afresh with effect from the order of dismissal by setting-aside judgment and decree dated 4-6-2007 passed by learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 192 of 2006 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 23-11-2005 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 1st court in Title suit No.313 of 2005 rejecting the plaint.

2. The short facts leading to this petition are that the respondent No.1 as plaintiff filed original suit No. 313 of 2005 praying for a declaration to the effect that the Letter dated 12-6-1999 issued by the defendant No.1 is illegal, improper, unjust and out of jurisdiction and the recommendation Letter dated 26-7-2000 regarding dismissal by the Board is illegal and out of jurisdiction. Hence the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration in the court of Assistant Judge, 1st court, Dhaka.

3. The defendant petitioner filed written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable and the suit is barred by limitation and that the plaintiff petitioner has no cause of action in the plaint and therefore, the plaint is liable to be rejected.

4. The defendant No.1, present petitioner filed an application under Order VII, rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure on 17-10-2005 for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the plaintiff was appointed as assistant teacher on temporary basis and the plaintiff submitted a false certificate in the name of army school and on query, the school authority formed a committee for investigation and upon investigation report and as per the terms of Clause 6 of his appointment, he has been dismissed from service for which the plaint is liable to be rejected.

5. The learned Assistant Judge, 1st court, Dhaka on the application of the defendant No.1 under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, rejected the plaint vide the impugned order dated 23-11-2005 on the ground that there is no cause of action for filing of the suit.

6. The plaintiff-Respondent being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the Judgment and decree dated 23-11-2005 preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 192 of 2006 in the Court of learned District Judge, Dhaka and the said appeal was transferred to the Court of learned Subordinate Judge (Now Joint District Judge) 2nd court, Dhaka who heard the matter and affirmed the judgment and order dated 23-11-2005 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 1st court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.313 of 2005 rejecting the plaint by his judgment and decree dated 4-6-2007.

7. The plaintiff respondent then filed civil Revision No. 4596 of 2007, before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, in which Rule was issued upon the defendant opposite parties of the Revision. The Civil Revision was heard by the learned Judge of High Court Division on 2-8-2011 who by his judgment and order dated 11-8-2011 made the Rule absolute and thereby decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff petitioner(present Respondent No.1) with a direction upon the opposite party to appoint the plaintiff afresh with effect from the date of dismissal on 12-6-1999 upon observation that the dismissal order is absolutely illegal because the opposite party did not follow the provision of law without obtaining prior permission from the arbitration committee.

8. The petitioner and other defendants had no knowledge about the impugned judgment and decree, but suddenly the respondent No. 1 on 9- 12-2011 submitted an application to the petitioner for the implementation of the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Judge of the High Court Division with a photo copy of the judgment and decree. The petitioner then took preparation and arranged required papers within 7 days and then contacted with the learned advocate who applied for certified copy on 18-12-2011 and obtained the same and then within few days preferred the appeal.

9.
