Mrs. Sufia Khatun, the learned Advocate-on-Record on behalf of the defendant petitioner submits that the respondent does not disclose any cause of action and the suit, is not maintainable for which learned Assistant Judge upon application filed by the defendant petitioner rightly allowed the application for rejection of plaint and appellate court also affirmed the said decree, but High court Division upon misconception of law passed the impugned judgment and decree by set- ting-aside the decree of both the learned courts below by the impugned order which is illegal and not sustainable in law.

10. She further submits that the plaintiff respondent No.1 very cunningly practising fraud, got the Rule heard ex-parte and upon misleading submission obtained the impugned decree with a direction for the appointment of the plaintiff which is subject matter of original suit and the High Court Division failed to give attention to the legal aspect of the case and passed the impugned decree which caused serious miscarriage of justice.

11. It is further submitted that High Court Division beyond jurisdiction virtually adjudicated the case which he cannot do before trial and also illegally allowed the prayer of the plaintiff directing the authority to give fresh Appointment and, as, such the impugned decree should be set-aside.

12. Mr. Khair Azaz Masua, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff respondent submits that the plaint discloses the cause of action and that the suit is maintainable. He further submits that judgment and order dated 11-8-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4596 of 2007 making the Rule absolute and decreeing the suit with a direction upon the defendant opposite parties to appoint the petitioner afresh effect from dismissal is legal and the impugned judgment and order does not call for any interference.

<u>13.The pertinent question is whether the learned Judge of High Court Division can finally adjudicate the case without giving chance to adduce evidence when there is a charge of submitting false school certificate against the plaintiff. The answer is in the negative. The suit cannot be finally adjudicated without taking evidence. The learned Judge of the High Court Division acted beyond his jurisdiction and finally adjudicated the case which he cannot do before trial and he also cannot allow the prayer of the plaintiff directly asking authority to give fresh appointment to the plaintiff from the date of dismissal.</u>

14. We find substance in the argument of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner. So, there are sufficient grounds for interference in this case and, as such, the impugned judgment and order dated 11-8-2011 passed by the High Court Division is set-aside.

15. The grounds shown for the condonation of delay being satisfactory are accepted. Hence the delay is condoned.

16. The leave petition is accordingly disposed of.

The matter is remanded to the High court Division for a fresh hearing.

End.

caseno: Appeal from Appellate Order No. 22 of 1971.
lawyer: Abdur Rab ------- For Appellant.
parties:
Munshi Ashadul Huq ------- Appellant, 
Vs. 
Nur Mohammad and ors  ------- Respondent.
full_judgment:
This appeal arises out of an order passed in a Miscellaneous appeal on an application under Order 21 rule 16 of the Code of Civil Procedure in an execution case.

2. The petitioner-respondent No. 1 purchased the suit land from the decree-holder after the decree in the original title suit was passed but before the title appeal was filed. Thereafter the petitioner applied for being added as a respondent in the title appeal and by an order dated 11-2-69 the learned Subordinate Judge allowed the petitioner to be added as respondent No. 2 under Order 22 rule 10 C.P.C. The appeal was partly allowed and the decree-holder respondent was directed to deposit Taka 1400/- to the credit of the appellant and thereafter  the present execution proceeding was started. It may be noted in the connection that the suit out of which the present proceeding arose was for specific performance of a contract for re-conveyance. The petitioner offered to deposit the aforesaid sum of Taka 1400/- which was rejected but subsequently he was allowed by the learned Munsif deposit the same in the name of the original decree-holder. The learned Munsif however found that the petitioner had no locus standi to proceed with the execution case on the ground that he was not an assignee of the decree-holder Against the aforesaid order the petitioner preferred an appeal and the learned District Judge set aside the order or the learned, Munsif and allowed the appeal and directed the execution case to proceed in accordance with the law. Hence, the present appeal at the instance of the opposite party.

3. Mr. Abdur Rab, the learned Advocate appearing, on behalf of the appellant, has ‘submitted' that there being no assignment of the decree; the application wider Order 21 rule. 16 C.P.C. out of which the present appeal arises, was not maintainable at the instance of the petitioner-respondent.

<u>4. From the judgment of the learned District Judge it appears that the suit was decreed on 26-4-68 and the decree-holder transferred his entire interest in the suit land by two Kabalas dented 29-4-68 and 4-5-68. Thereafter; the  opposite party-appellant filed, the title appeal in which the petitioner-respondent was allowed, by the learned Subordinate Judge to be added as a respondent. It is not disputed that the decree-holder transferred his entire interest, the suit property by the two Kabalas to the petitioner-respondent. The learned Advocate has tried to argue that transfer of the suit property does not amount assignment of the decree as content plated under Order 21 rule 16 C.P.C. am afraid I am unable to appreciate the logic of the argument. This transfer by the decree-holder passed to the petitioner the entire rights of the decree holder-vender in, the suit property including all rights under the subsisting deecree for specific performance against the appellant, otherwise the transfer would be meaningless. This transfer by written document namely the kabalas therefore, in my opinion was an assignment of the interest of the decree-holder, in wilting as contemplated under Order 21 rule 16 C.P.C.</u>

<u>5. Apart from this, even assuming for the sake of argument that Order 21 rule 16 C.P.C. is not applicable, in the, instant case, the petitioner would Still be entitled to invoke the aid of section 146 C.P.C. and execute the decree as a person claiming under him, namely, the decree holder since it is not disputed that all rights and interests of the decree-holder-vender in the suit property stood transferred to the petitioner-respondent by the aforesaid Kabalas.</u>

6. In the view that I have taken, I am supported by, the decision of a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court in the case of Ambika Prashad Saxena Vs. Sim Bangladeshi Devi Agarwala reported in A.I.R. 1968 Cal 242.

<u>7. The petitioner-respondent was allowed by the Court to join in the title appeal as respondent under Order 22 rule 10 C.P.C. If the appellant had any objection or grievance against the petitioner being added as a respondent in the title appeal he could have challenged the order since the order was appealable. On query from the court, the learned Advocate admitted that no appeal was filed against the aforesaid order under Order 22 rule 10 C.P.C. on further query from the court, the learned Advocate also admitted that no second appeal was filed against the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court in the title appeal. Having regard to all these facts and circumstances, I am clearly of opinion that the said Order under Order 22 rule 10 C.P.C. having remained unchallenged, the petitioner-respondent was fully entitled to file the application under Order 21 rule 16 C.P.C. and proceed with the execution case and that there was an assignment of the interest of the decree holder as contemplated under the said order of the C.P.C. It was therefore clear from the above discussion that even a person benefit Of the decree not by assignment but by virtue of transfer of property which is the subject matter of the decree, is entitled to execute the decree.</u>

<u>No other ground has been urged by the, learned Advocate. For reasons stated above I find no substance in the appeal which is accordingly summarily dismissed.</u>

The prayer for leave under Clause 15 of the letters patent is refused.

End.

case_source: From the judgment and Order dated 17-7-2001 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3535 of 2000).
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Matin J : This Appeal on Leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 17-7- 2001 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3535 of 2000 making the Rule absolute.

2. The facts, in short, are that the appellant is defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 249 of 1998 which was instituted by the plaintiffs for declaration that the judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional Assistant. Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 51 of 1997 is void and is not binding on the plaintiffs.

3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land measuring about 96 decimals appertaining to CS Khatian 212 and SA Khatian 507 was owned and possessed by the defendant No.1 and his brother Sudhir Chandra now deceased. They transferred the said land by registered deed of sale on 14-5-1969 to the defendant No.2, Parul Bala. On 4-2-1970 Parul Bala transferred the suit land to one Sufia Khatun and delivered possession. The latter got her name recorded in the RS Khatian and possessed the suit land till she transferred it to Shahabuddin on 9-12-1977 and delivered possession. Thereafter, Shahabuddin transferred the land to the plaintiffs who now possessing the same on raising dwelling houses and mutating their names and paying rents.

4. The plaintiffs got a notice from the local Demra Police Station issued on the basis of a complaint dated 7-7-1998 lodged by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and came to learn that the defendants obtained the judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 51 of 1997 in which the aforesaid sale of Parul Bala was held to be void and fraudulent.

5. The defendant appellant contested the suit. His case is that he and his brother acquired the entire suit land of 96 decimals which are nal lands and he has been possessing his 48 decimals of land by cultivating through bargadar. His brother Suddhir died leaving behind defendant No. 2 who acquired life interest over his portion. On 8-8-1995 he heard from Zinnah and others about the aforementioned claim that he and his brother has sold their land to Parul Bala in 1969. Thereupon he obtained certified copies of the deeds and came to know about the fraudulent transfer and instituted Title Suit No. 180 of 1995 which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 51 of 1997 and got the judgment and decree on 24-5-1998 on contest against Parul Bala, the defendant No.2. It was claimed that the petitioner and his brother never executed and registered the deed dated 14-5-1969. The deed was created by forgery.

6. On 30-9-1999 Title Suit No. 249 of 1998 was decreed by the trial Court. On Appeal by the defendant petitioner the Court of Appeal below allowed the Appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The plaintiff thereupon moved the High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction on 17-7-2001 and the rule was ultimately made absolute and the judgment and decree of the appellate Court was set aside and those of the trial Court was restored.

7. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the contesting defendant having taken a plea in the written statement and having proved that he is in possession of the land the learned Single Judge acted illegally in failing to hold that the suit of the plaintiffs is not maintainable without making a further prayer for declaration of title to the suit land.

8. He further submitted that the learned Assistant Judge having arrived at a clear finding in the previous suit that the present petitioner is in possession of the suit land, the present suit for a simple declaration that the judgment and decree passed in TS No. 51 of 1997 is void without making a further prayer for declaration of title and confirmation of possession is not maintainable.

9. Leave was granted to consider the above submissions. Heard Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellants and Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondent Nos. 1-18 And perused the petition and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other papers on record.

10. The learned Counsel appearing for the appellants submits that the learned Assistant Judge arrived at a clear finding in the previous suit No. 51 of 1997 that the present appellant is in possession of the suit land the instant suit for a simple declaration that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 51 of 1997 is void without making a further prayer for declaration of title and confirmation of possession is not maintainable.

11. He further submits that the suit land being owned by the defendant No. 1 and the deceased- husband of the defendant No.2 who had a limited life interest, the Exhibits 5, 7, 8 and 9 series being basic documents of alleged title of the plaintiffs having not been proved in accordance with law, the contesting defendant having taken a plea iii the written statement to the effect that he is in possession of the land and he proved accordingly, the learned Single Judge acted illegally in failing to hold that the suit of the plaintiffs is not maintainable without making a further prayer for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the suit land.

12. He submits that the learned Single judge of the High Court Division is in error of law in holding that the judgment and decree passed on 24-5-1998 in Title Suit No. 51 of 1997, Exhibits-12 and 'Kha' respectively can be declared as void with reference to facts subsequent to Exhibit-4 ignoring the validity of the evidence and facts in the aforesaid suit as stated by the defendant No.1 while obtaining the aforesaid decree holding the Exhibit-4 as void.

13. He lastly submits that the learned Single Judge acted illegally in exercise of his revisional jurisdiction to set aside the finding of facts arrived at by the lower appellate Court in respect of the possession of the suit land misreading the report of the Advocate Commissioner who made a report to the effect that the major portion of the suit land was lying vacant proving the case of the defendant No.1 who is also a recorded tenant in the RS Khatian.

14. The learned Counsel appearing for the respondent submits that the High Court Division arriving in finding that trial Court has correctly declared that the judgment and decree dated 24-5-1998 and 31-5-1998 respectively as obtained by defendant No. 1 in previous Title Suit No. 51 of 1997 was obtained by collusion and practicing fraud in getting cancellation of the sale deed dated 14-5-1969, Exhibit No. 4.

He further submits that the High Court Division found that the finding of the Court of Appeal below on the title and possession and the decision in the Appeal was arrived at on misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record and without application of any judicial mind.

15. It appears from the judgment and decree dated 24th May, 1998 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 51 of 1997 that the Court declared the sale (deed No. 4400) dated 14-5-1969 as a forged one on the basis of the report of the finger print expert, Exhibit- 7 of the suit and it was further held that the defendant who was the plaintiff in the earlier suit was in possession.

16. It further appears that although in the original plaint the plaintiff of the present suit made a prayer for declaration of title but ultimately deleted that prayer by an amendment and allowed the suit to proceed with the only prayer for declaration that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 51 of 1997 is fraudulent one and not binding upon the plaintiff. In the facts and circumstances of the case the Court of Appeal below rightly held that the suit as framed is not maintainable and the High Court Division acted illegally in setting aside the appellate judgment.

17. It further appears that in the earlier Suit No. 51 of 1997 a competent Court relied upon the evidence of finger print expert, Exhibit- 7 of that suit, the Court of Appeal below held as under:-

ইতিপূর্বে ১নং বিবাদী বাদী হইয়া সহকারী জজ আদালতে পারুল বালাকে বিবাদী করিয়া ১৮০/৮৫ নং দেওয়ানী মামলা এবং পরবর্তীতে অতিরিক্ত সহকারী জজ আদালতে ৫৯/৯৫নং দেওয়ানী মামলা নম্বর ভুক্ত হয়। যাহা দোতরফাসূত্রে শুনানী অন্তে বাদী অর্থাৎ বর্তমান মামলার বিবাদীর অনুকূলে ডিক্রী হয়। ঐ মামলাটিতে বিজ্ঞ ননিম্ন আদালতে দোতরফা শুনানী অন্তে ডিক্রী প্রমাণ করিয়া ১৪-৫-৬৯ ইং তারিখে ৪৪০ কবলা দলিল জাল তঞ্চবতা মূলে-সৃজন করা হইয়াছে মর্মে ঘোষণা করেন এবং বিজ্ঞ সহকারী জজ তাহার রায়ে এই মর্মে অভিমত দেন যে,দলিলের টিপ রেজিষ্ট্রার ও আদালতে বাদীর টিপ নিয়া উভয় টিপ পরীক্ষার জন্য সি,আই, ডিতে প্রেরণ করা হয়। হস্ত রেখা রেজিষ্ট্রাওে ভাষানী সরকারের নামের টিপের সাথে আদালতে দেওয়া বাদীর টিপের কোন মিল নাই।” উক্ত ৫১/৯৭নং দেওয়ানী মামলায় বিজ্ঞ সহকারী জজ আলোচনায় উল্লেখ করিয়াছে যে, অত্র মামলার আরজির ক’ তফসিল বর্ণিত ১৯-৫-৬৯ ইং তারিখের দলিল ৪৪০০ জাল, ভ্রমাত্মক, এখতিয়ার বহির্ভুত, তঞ্জতা মূলে তৈরী করা হইয়াছে। সুতরাং, উক্ত দলিল দ্বারা কোনস্বত্ব অজির্ত হইতে পারেনা। নালশী জমিতে বাদী দখল ভোগ রহিয়াছে এই মর্মে প্রমান পাওয়া যায়।

18. Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that comparison of thumb impression has become an exact science and the evidence of the expert of this subject is entitled to considerable weight and the Court of Appeal below rightly held that the sale dead dated 19-1- 5. 1969 deed No. 4400 is a forged one and such finding is passed on a sure foundation namely the report of the finger print expert.

<u>19. Mr Islam has referred to the case of Jaspal Singh, vs State of Punjab, reported in AIR 1979 SC 1708 wherein Indian Supreme Court held that the science of identifying thumb impression is an exact science and does not admit of any mistake or doubt. We endorse the aforesaid view.</u>

20. We find substance in the submission. The Court of Appeal below rightly relied upon the expert's evidence about deed No. 4400 of 1969 and rightly held that the plaintiff did not acquire any right by the alleged purchase from Parul Bala and the purchasers on the basis of Exhibits- 5, 7, 8 or 9 also did not acquire any right by such purchases.

21. In view of the fact that deed dated 14-5- 1969 was rightly held to be a forged one and not binding upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 51 of 1969, Bhashani Mondal, and that the Court of Appeal below rightly held that the plaintiff's possession was not proved, whereas, the defendant Bhashani Mondal's possession was already proved in the earlier Suit No. 51 of 1997 and in the present suit, a sui for declaration simpliciter is not maintain- able.

22. In view of our discussions made above the Appeal is allowed without any order as to cost.

End.

lawyer:
Md. Fazlul Karim and Md. Moinul with Golam Rabbani ------- For the Petitioner.

parties:
Md. Abdul Huq Miah, Advocate  ------- Petitioner
Vs. 
1. Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Dacca, Chairman, Special Tribunal under P.O. No. 13 of 1972. 
2. Md. Shamsuddoula, son of late Haji Abdus Sattar, Ministry of Information, Dacca  ------- Respondents.
case_source: (In the matter of:—An application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh.)
full_judgment:
Ahsanuddin Chowdhury J. - This is a petition under Article 102 of the constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. On this petition the petitioner obtained the present Rule against the judgment and order dated 10-1-73 passed in Tribunal Misc. Appeal No. 3. of 1972 setting aside the order passed on 25-9-72 by the sub-divisional Officer, Sadar (South), Dacca in Misc. Case No. 2 of 1972 of the No- wabpur Union Arbitration Court. P. S. Sutrapur, Dacca constituted under the President's Order No.13 of 1972.

2. The petitioner in his petition has stated that he entered into an agreement of purchase with one Madhusudhan Basak, son of late Kalchand Basak of the premises situated at 28/1 Gopumohan Basak Lane appertaining to plot Not 5461 of holding No. 3, Sheet No. 50 of Dacca Collectorate comprising an area of 0216 acre. But the vendor having failed to execute the deed of transfer within the stipulated time, the petitioner after obtaining permission from the Board of Revenue, filed a suit being title suit No.9 of 1968 against the said Madhusudhan Basak in the 6th Court of the Munsif, Dacca for the specific performance of contract. He obtained a decree on 14-5-68. A copy of the said decree has been annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure "A". Thereafter he put the decree into execution in Title Execution Case No. 25 of 1968. Having got notice of the execution case respondent No. 2 filed a suit, being title suit No. 190 of 1968, in the 6th Court of the Munsif, Dacca for a declaration that the decree obtained by the petitioner in Title Suit No. 9 of 1968 was fraudulent, void not binding on him. The respondent No. 2 also prayed for an injunction restraining the petitioner from proceeding further with his title Execution Case No. 25 of 1968. The Suit ultimately was decreed ex parte on 27-4-70. The petitioner thereafter filed a Misc. Case being No. 125 of 1970 in the 6th Court of the Munsif Dacca for setting aside the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1968. A copy of the said application has been annexed to this petition as Annexure 'B' The said miscellaneous case under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure it till pending for disposal and the papers to that effect has been annexed as 'C' The respondent No. 2, on 29-5-70 filed an application before the Nawabpur Union Arbitration Court stating inter alia, that on the 29th of March, 1971 he left the aforesaid premises and on his return to the city sometime after the liberation, he found the petitioner in the disputed premises on the 26th of December, 1971. He accordingly prayed for restoration of possession of the said premises on evicting the petitioner therefrom. The said application has been annexed to this petition as Annexure 'D.' The petitioner having received a notice of the said application, himself submitted an application to the Arbitration Court disagreeing with the said arbitration proceeding and stating, inter alia, that the respondent No. 2 had no right whatsoever in the house in dispute and that the story of his possession or dispossession therefore was false and baseless. He further prayed before the Arbitration Court to dismiss the case or to send the same to the Thana Magistrate for adjudication with due notice to him. A copy of the said application is annexed to this petition as Annexure 'E' The petitioner has further stated that the respondent No. 2 is a Bihari and has married a Bihari girl and that he collaborated actively with the Pakistan Army by singing songs on Radio Pakistan for Pakistan against the Bangladesh and after the liberation, i.e. independence of Bangladesh, respondent No. 2 was concealing himself as 'Mukti Bahini' was in search of him. The petitioner has also stated that he found one Bhudha Mia staying alone in the house when he visited the house on 1-1-72. The said Bhudha Mia stated to him that the respondent No. 2 Was hiding somewhere in the city and asked him to look after his house, but he was feeling helpless and wanted to leave the house on the petitioner taking over possession of the same. As such, the petitioner got into possession of the house at the request of Bhudha Mia on 1-1-72. Thereafter he undertook the repair works of the house and spent about Tk. 5000/- to make the house habitable and since then it is his possession. The further statement of the petitioner is that on 14-7-72 he filed a petition to the Sub-Divisional Officer to transfer the case to him from the Arbitration Court whereupon the Sub-Divisional Magistrate called for the records. A copy of the entire proceeding of the Arbitration case has been annexed as Annexure "F" The Sub-Divisional Magistrate having received the records asked Mr. M. Roy, Magistrate, 1st Class for enquiry and report regarding the house in question. After obtaining the report of the Magistrate, the Sub-Divisional Officer approved the proposal made in the report, but he directed to serve a notice on the petitioner to show cause. This order of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate was challenged by the respondent No. 2 in appeal before the Tribunal. A true copy of the memorandum- of appeal has been annexed as Annexure "G" The Tribunal having heard both the parties, passed its judgment on 10-1-73, setting aside the order passed by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate and directing that the respondent No. 2 should be allowed to take over possession of the house in dispute on evicting the petitioner therefrom within seven days from the date of order. A true copy of the said, judgment and order is annexed to this petition and marked as Annexure "I" which has been challenged before this Court under its 'writ' jurisdiction.

2A. The Respondent No. 2 in his affidavit-in-opposite has controverted, whatever adverse statements have been made against him by the petitioner. He has further stated in his affidavit-in-opposition that one Kalidash Basak and Madhusudhan Basak were the C.S. recorded tenants in the holding in question in equal shares. The said tenants having failed to pay their land revenue for the holding in question, it was put to auction sale and his wife Mrs. Afroz Jahan, purchased the same on 25-4-63. A true copy of the certificate of sale has been annexed as Annexure "A" to this affidavit-in-opposition. This respondent thereafter purchased the said holding by a kabala dated 11-12-64 from his wife Mrs. Afioz Jahan. He is a Government servant and took house building loan of Tk. 5,808/- from the Government keeping holding in question in mortgage to the Government and constructed two pucca room and one katcha room thereon. He took electricity and water connections in the holding in question and his name was mutated in the Government Tahsil Office and also in the Municipal Office. Since then he has been paying, land revenue, municipal taxes and other rates, electricity bills, water bills etc. of the said holding. He was constantly living in the holding in question with the members of his family since 1963 till 29th March, 1971 when be had to leave his residence for fear of his life and also of the members of his family, as the locality was overwhelmingly inhabited by the Biharis and other local miscreants. He did not know anything of the fraudulent decree passed in Title Suit No: 9 of 1968 at the instance of the petitioner. But he came to know of it when the execution thereof was started. Then he filed title Suit No. 190 in of 1968 in the 6th Court of the Munsif Dacca for a declaration of his title and for confirmation of his possession and for a permanent injunction retraining the petitioner from proceeding further with the title Execution Case No. 25 of 1968. He also prayed for further declaration that the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 9 of 1968 was fraudulent, illegal void and not binding on the respondent. The petitioner appeared in Title Suit No. 190 of 1968 and filed a written statement but ultimately the suit was allowed to be decreed ex-parte. A copy of the decree in Title suit No. 190 of 1968 has been annexed as Annexure to this affidavit-in-opposition. The petitioner had not title whatsoever and he had no possession at any time till he illegally trespassed into the house on the 26th December, 1971. The attempt of the respondent No. 2 to get back possession of the house amicably having failed, he filed an application before the Nawabpur Union Arbitration Court on the 29th May, 1972. The said Court sent the record to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate with its findings and the Sub-Divisional Magistrate in his turn also had an enquiry made through Mr. M. Roy, Magistrate, 1st Class regarding the actual possession of the house in question. The enquiring Magistrate submitted his report to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate recommending restoration of possession of the house to the respondent No. 2 by evicting the petitioner therefrom, if necessary, with police force. But the Sub-Divisional Magistrate committed an illegality by directing a notice to be served on the petitioner to show cause, though virtually he proved of the report of the enquiring Magistrate. The respondent No. 2 thereafter moved an application to the Tribunal which having set aside the order of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, directed that the possession of the house in question should be restored to the respondent No. 2 who is an evacuee according to the President's Order No. 13 of 1972.

3. Respondent No. 2 has emphatically denied petitioner's, statements that he (Respondent No. 2) is a Bihari, that his wife is also a Bihari and that he collaborated with the Pakistan Army. He was asserted that he and his wife are Bangalis. He himself hails from the District of Hoogly in West Bengal and his wife comes from the district of Faridpur in Bangladesh. He himself came to this place in 1950, got a job under the Government as a singer (now Kanthashilpi) in the then Public Relations Department (now Ministry of Information of Bangladesh) under Poet Jasimuddin and late Abbasuddin Ahmed who were in charge of Song Publicity Section and selected this respondent for this job. The respondent is now singer on Radio, TV and in public meetings of Bengali folk songs and had his training under poet Jasimuddin and late Abbasuddin Ahmed. He never concealed himself for fear of his life from 'Mukti Bahini'. Rather, after the liberation he immediately joined his office and has been rendering his humble best in the service of the nation as a singer. Sometimes he sings folk songs in public meetings, undertakes official tours with Ministers and sometimes with the Prime Minister himself. Thus the respondent No.2 controverts what has been stated against him by the petitioner.

In the affidavit-in-reply filed by the petitioner nothing particularly has been said as against what have been stated by the respondent No. 2 in his affidavit-in-opposition.

The point involved in this case is as to whether the Tribunal has acted in excess of its jurisdiction and thereby acted without jurisdiction, and mala fide in not following the procedure prescribed in President's Order No.13 of 1972 (hereinafter referred to as P.O. 13/72).

4. From what has been stated above, it is obvious that a dispute over the title of this property has been going between the parties. The petitioner claims his title to the property in pursuance of a contract for sale on the basis of which he obtained a decree which was subsequently set aside as a fraudulent one at the instance of the respondent No. 2 who claim his title to this property by virtue of his purchase from his wife who acquired her title to this property in a revenue sale The decree obtained by respondent No. 1 Title Suit No. 190/68 in respect of this property still stands. So, prima facie, the title of the property vests in respondent No. 2.

5. Now, the case, of respondent No. 2 is that he was living in this holding since 1963 till 29th of March, 1.971 when he had to leave his hearth and home on account of the country wide disturbance due to liberation struggle. That area was overwhelmingly inhabited by the Biharis and other local miscreants. He had close attachment to the Awami League Party and, as such, his life was not secure at that place due to the presence of the Bihari population there. He had, therefore, to leave his house with his family for the sake of their life. This state of things has not been controverted by the petitioner. We are, therefore, to see whether respondent No. 2 is an evacuee within the definition as contained in clause (c) of Article 2 of P. O. 13/72. Clause (c) Article 2 of P. O. 13/72. reads as follows:-

"Evacuee" means a person ordinarily resident in Bangladesh, who, on account of the country wide' disturbances, on or after the 25th day of March, 1971 and before the 16th day of December, 1971 left his ordinary place of residence for any place within Bangladesh or left Bangladesh for any other country and includes the legal heirs of such person."

6. The case of respondent No. 2 is that he moved from place to place to Bangladesh but he could not go to his place of residence for the reasons stated above. The circumstances described by Respondent No. 2 and asserted by him in his affidavit-in-opposition clearly go to show that he was an evacuee within the definition of clause (c), Article 2 of P. O. 13/72, as quoted above.

<u>7. The character of the respondent No. 2 being an evacuee has, however, been challenged by the petitioner and his learned Advocate has also argued on that point. Whether the respondent No. 2 is an evacuee or not is a question of fact. The Arbitration Court in its findings has clearly stated that respondent No. 2 was an evacuee, i.e., he was in his residence till 29th of March, 1971 and thereafter he left it, and these findings are made on local enquiries and based on evidence as Well. The petitioner contents that the Arbitration Court had no right to make such findings as he informed the Arbitration Court about his disagreement to the proceedings before it. Clause (5.) to Article 7 of P. O: 13/72 empowers the Arbitration Court to send its findings under clause (3) along with the record of the case to the Thana Magistrate having jurisdiction for such order as he deems fit where the parties have not agreed to arbitration. In this particular case, the petitioner did not agree to arbitration. Court was not debarred, in any way, from sending its findings under clause (5) to Article 7 of the said Order. The petitioner has not only disagreed to the arbitration to be made by the Arbitration Court but also submitted an application to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate stating that not only the Arbitration Court but the Thana Magistrate too had no power to, arbitrate between him and the respondent No. 2. He was of the view that a case under Order 9, rule 13, being pending in a Civil Court, this matter cannot be the subject matter of Arbitration under P.O. 13/72 (Vide Annexure "E" to the affidavit-in-opposition) and thereafter he did not appear before the Arbitration Court as well as the Thana Magistrate though the record from the, Arbitration Court was called for by the Thana Magistrate at his instance. Whatever opinion the petitioner might have with regard to the maintainability of the case before the Arbitration Court and for that matter before the Thana Magistrate, those authorities were not bound by the opinion of the petitioner. They were of the view that they had the power to dispose of the Respondent's application in accordance with law, even though the petitioner challenged their jurisdiction on the ground that a case in respect of the property was pending in the Civil Court between the parties. The Petitioner was obviously under a wrong conception regarding the applicable of the provisions of the P. O. -13/72 because the fact that a case is pending in a Civil Court regarding this property is no bar to an application by an evacuee under P.O. 13 of 1972, provided the applicant is an evacuee as defined in Clause (c) of Article 2 of the Order. A reference to article 11 clauses (1) and (4) will show that the petitioner was under a misconception of law. Because the decision made under the provisions of the Order will not debar any aggrieved party to seek remedy in a competent Civil Court. Mr. Moinul Huq contends that one may come for relief under P. O. 13/72 provided one is an evacuee within the meaning of Clause (c) of Article 2. In the present case, he contends, the applicant i.e., the respondent No. 2 does not fall within the ambit of the definition of an evacuee. In this connection he refers to the report of the enquiring officer. It appears from the report that the respondent No. 2 had possession in the property before the trouble period i.e., before the specified date which means the 25th day of March, 1971. It is true that the report contains an expression that the respondent had possession in the property before the trouble period. This does not mean that he had no possession after the specified date and that he did not leave the property namely the house in question after the specified date. The report if read as a whole clearly gives that impression and for that reason the Enquiry Officer made a proposal for respondent No. 2 on evicting the petitioner therefrom if necessary with police force. It appears also from the findings of the Arbitration Court that the respondent No. 2 had possession till 29th of March, 71. This is also the clear case of the Respondent No. 2. Furthermore para 13 of the petitioner's petition shows that he got possession from one Budhah who told him that he was looking after the house on behalf of respondent No. 2 who was hiding somewhere in the city. The Tribunal also has found that the respondent No. 2 was in occupation of the holding in question even after the specified date i.e. after 25th of March, 1971 and that the petitioner is in unauthorized occupation of the house. Mr. Moinul Huq, however, contends that the petitioner cannot be evicted as an unauthorized occupant as he did not enter into the possession of the house during the period from 25th of March to 16th of December, 1971. We are unable to accept the contention of Mr. Moinul Huq because P.O. 13/72 does not protect an unauthorized occupant who entered into possession after 16th or December 1971. The only condition to be fulfilled for eviction of an unauthorized occupant is that the person applying for restoration of possession of the property must be an evacuee within the meaning of Clause (c) of Article 2 of the order. Respondent No. 2 has been found to be an evacuee.</u>

<u>8. The next question is whether the order of the Thana Magistrate was appealable. Mr. Moinul Huq contends that appeal lies to the Tribunal against a final order passed by the Thana Magistrate. No appeal has been provided against any interlocutory order. The Thana Magistrate, having passed no final order, the appeal did not lie against his order. Mr. Mustafa Kamal representing respondent No. 2 has argued that the Thana Magistrate's order must be construed as an final order by which he approved the proposal of the Enquiry Magistrate. We have noticed what proposal the report contains. The report having been approved the Thana Magistrate had to pass the order for restoration of possession to the respondent No. 2 on evicting the petitioner and he had no power, to make an order for service of a show cause upon the parties. In this respect Mr. Mustafa Kamal points out that clause (3) to Article 7 of the Order contains two mutually exclusive procedures to be followed by the Thana Magistrate, one preceding the word "or" and the other following it. When the Thana Magistrate adopts the procedure preceding the word "or" and acts on the result thereof, his function so far as enquiries are concerned is over and he is to pass the final order either allowing the prayer of the applicant or rejecting it. He cannot follow the two mutually, exclusive procedure simultaneously. In this case the findings of the Arbitration Court, the report of the Enquiring Magistrate Mr. M. Roy, and the entire record were before the Thana Magistrate and being satisfied, he approved the proposal of the Enquiring Magistrate. So, it was not open to him to notify the parties further. Mr. Moinul Huq on the other hand, contends that if this interpretation is accepted then it will lead to some absurdities, i.e., the whole of the findings, other evidence on record and the result of further enquiry if made in the case cannot be looked into by the Thana Magistrate and the case is to be disposed of only after hearing both the parties himself. We do not think there is any absurdity in it. Because the Thana Magistrate is one of the authorities named in the said Order. The Thana Magistrate is quite competent to dispose of the matter after hearing both the parties himself, even without looking into what has already come on the record. The word "hearing" has got a wide connotation. The Thana Magistrate himself can take evidence, examine documents as may appear material to him and dispose of the case accordingly. So in the instant case the Thana Magistrate having approved the proposal contained in the report of the Enquiring Officer and having had sufficient materials in support thereof ought to have passed the order in clear terms either allowing the prayer of the applicant. Respondent No. 2 or rejecting it. However the approval of the proposal contained in the report amounted to final order allowing the prayer of the applicant. Notice in these circumstances is not contemplated in the President's Order. The learned Tribunal has, in our opinion rightly found that the learned Thana Magistrate acted illegally when he directed further show cause notice after he had approved the proposal for restoration of the property to respondent No. 2 by evicting the petitioner there from. It may also be mentioned here that the Tribunal is the ultimate authority under P. O. 13/72. An appeal lies to the Tribunal both against an order allowing the petition of the applicant or rejecting it and the order passed by the Tribunal in appeal is final. The Tribunal considered the whole case in presence of both the parties and if was satisfied from the findings of the Arbitration Court, the result of the enquiry and the materials on record that the respondent No. 2 was in possession of this property even after the specified date, i.e., 25th of March, 1971 but he had to, leave that place under compelling circumstances, and that the petitioner who had no possession at any point of time, took advantage of the situation and entered into the property in question behind the back of respondent No. 2. We think that it has been rightly stated in the affidavit-in-opposition by the respondent No. 2 that what the petitioner could not do by legal process, he had sought to do it in complete usurpation of the same in a period of crisis. The petitioner is thus an unauthorized occupant.</u>

<u>9. Mr. Moinul Huq has taken objections to the order passed by the learned Tribunal He contends that the Tribunal has no power to restore a person to possession. Its power lies only in passing an order either allowing the appeal or dismissing the same. We are unable to agree with him on this point because the Tribunal being the ultimate authority is to pass a speaking order in case the prayer of the applicant is allowed. The operative portion of the order of the Tribunal runs as follows:-</u>

<u>Ordered</u>

<u>“that the Misc. Appeal be allowed on contest. The petitioner be allowed to take over possession of the property in question being restored to him and the O. P. be evicted on expiry of 7 days from the date of order with the help of police, if the possession is not delivered amicably within the above grace period of 7 days.”</u>

<u>The Tribunal's order that the petitioner should be allowed to take over possession of the property in question is a direction as to how affect shall be given to its order. Clause (8) of Article 7 provides that the Thana Magistrate in the case of an order passed by the Tribunal for restoration of possession under clause (7) of the same Order shall cause the possession of the property concerned to be delivered to the applicant by evicting the unauthorized occupant therefrom and may, for this purpose, cause to be used such force as may be necessary. So the Tribunal's order directing restoration of possession to the applicant namely respondent No. 2 is not violative of any provision of P. O. 13/72. It is in-consonance with clause 8 of Article 7 of P.O. 13/72. We do not, therefore, find any illegality to have been committed by the Tribunal in allowing the appeal of the respondent No. 2 and passing the order for restoration of possession in accordance with law. In this view of the matter the Tribunal has not acted without lawful authority. The order of the Tribunal does not, therefore, warrant any interference by this Court.</u>

10. Lastly, Moinul Huq has urged that the application of respondent No. 2 under P. O. 13/72 is not maintainable on the ground that no rules have been framed as yet by the Government. Article 15 of the Order provides that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make Rules to carry into effect the provision of this order. Admittedly Rules have not been framed by the Govt. nevertheless it is to be considered whether, due to non-framing of rules the operation of P. O. 13/72 will be kept in abeyance. Mr. Moinul Huq contends that it should be. In this connection he refers to us certain decisions, particularly the decision in the case of M. Noman Vs. Dacca Improvement Trust and others reported in 16 D.L.R. (Dacca) 537. M. Noman was the Chief Engineer under the Dacca Improvement Trust. He was placed under suspension and a departmental proceeding was also drawn against him for some allegations against him. A Division Bench of the Dacca High Court found that no rules having been framed under the Town Improvement Act, 1953 by the Govt. the action taken against him was not maintainable. Section 102 of the Town Improvement Act provides that the Provincial Govt. may make Rules not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act, in particular, the Provincial Government may make rules for all or any of the following matters, (e) the conditions on which the employees of the Board or of the Tribunal may be appointed, reduced, suspended, discharged, removed, dismissed or otherwise punished." It was found that the provisions of section 102 of the Town Improvement Act empowering the Provincial Government to make Disciplinary Rules in respect of the D.I.T. employees, though apparently permissible are really mandatory. Furthermore section 34 of the Act provides that the power of appointing and punishing shall be subject to any Rules for the time being in force". It was then held, "What follows then is no rule, no power one presupposing the other". "There being no rule, the proceedings started against M. Noman were held to be bad in law and of no legal effect. It is to be noted here that the case of Noman, is a case between the Master and a Servant and the conditions of the service were involved in that case. Hence much stress was put on the rules to be framed as otherwise the servants are left at the mercy of the Master. But because of non-framing of rules under the Town Improvement Act there is no scope to say that the Act did not come into force. The entire administration of the D.I.T. is being carried on under the provisions of the Act. Only in respect of a particular matter, namely, the question of dismissal of an employee of the D.I.T., the necessity of the rules to be framed as provided under some sections of the Act was noticed by the Court. But in the case under our consideration it is difficult to say that due to non-framing of rules the operation of the order should remain suspended. Here again Mr. Moinul Huq contends that if this Court differs from the view taken in Noman's case then this court has got to refer it to a Full Bench for decision on this point as has been done in first Appeal No. 503 of 1968 by another Division Bench of this Court. He refers to an unreported decision of this Court in F. A. 503 of 1968 (The district Council of Comilla Vs. Mr. M. Khalilur Rahman). It was an appeal, by the Govt. against the order of the trial Court setting aside an order of dismissal of a public servant. In that appeal, the case of M. Noman was cited, the Bench presided over by the learned Chief Justice, doubted the correctness of the decision made in Noman's case. Hence a reference to the Full Bench has been made with respect to the said case. We do not, however, feel that, we should also do it in the facts of the instant case. P. O. 13/72 is both a substantive and a procedural law. Furthermore it is a legislation enacted for the purpose of giving protection to the sufferers in respect of their property during the liberation period. This legislation has been given a life only for a specified period. It will remain in force only upto the 25th day of March, 1973. Taking all the provisions of P.O. No. 13/72 into consideration we think nothing has been left to be done by way of framing rules under the Order. Article 15 of the Order regarding the framing of rules is only an enabling provision. The Government may or may not make any rules but for want of rules the operation of this emergency legislation cannot remain suspended. This is not also the intention of the maker of this law. Clause 3 of Article 1 of the P. O. 13/72 provides that this order shall come into force at once. This order was published in the Bangladesh Gazette Extraordinary on 18th of February, 1972. It came into force on and from 18th of February, 1972. The operation of this Order is not at all dependent on the framing of Rules. We, therefore, find no substance in the contention raised by Mr. Moinul Huq.

In view of the findings made above, the Rule is discharged and the order of stay is vacated. We, however, direct that the parties do bear their own costs in this Rule.

K.M. Subhan J.- I agree.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 10th day of January 2010 and the 3rd day of February 2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ petition Nos. 2535 of 2008 and 5889 of 2008.)
full_judgment:
Md A Wahhab Miah J: Although these two leave petitions have been filed against the separate judgments and orders passed by the High Court Division in two separate writ petitions, the parties being the same and the facts giving rise to these petitions being overlapped, they have been heard together and are disposed of by this common judgment.

Civil Petition No.648 of 2010:-

2. Facts giving rise to this leave petition are that respondent No.2, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Bank), filed Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997 in the Court of the then Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna under the provisions of the President's Order No.129 of 1972 for realization of outstanding loan to the tune of Taka 2,06,27,235 from the petitioners. Eventually, the said miscellaneous case was converted into Artha Rin Suit No.43 of 2003 on payment of court fees. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 10-11-2003. Execution Case No.190 of 2004 was levied by the decree-holder-Bank for realization of decretal amount. On an application filed by judgment-debtor No. 2 on 16-2-2006 under section 49(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003(the Ain, 2003), the Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna (hereinafter referred to as the Adalat) by order of the same date (16-2-2006) allowed the judgment-debtors to pay the decretal amount in 4(four) installments, the date of last installment being 25-1-2007, on the condition that in default of payment of any installment, the entire decretal amount shall be payable and in that case, the execution case shall proceed. By the same order, the application filed by the decree-holder-Bank under section 33(4) of the Ain, 2003 was kept with the record. The execution case was disposed of accordingly. As the judgment-debtors failed to pay the decretal amount pursuant to the order dated 16- 2-2006, the Adalat on the application of the decree- holder by order dated 7-10-2007 issued warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors with the direction to keep judgment-debtor Nos.2-4 in jail till the realization of the decretal amount, but for a maximum period of 6(six) months. On 10-2-2008, the judgment-debtors filed an application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 for withdrawing the application filed on 16-2-2006 and also for setting-aside the order passed on the said date on the plea that no such application was filed by them; such application might have been filed falsely by the Bank just to harass and prejudice the judgment-debtors. The Adalat by order dated 19-2-2008 rejected the said application. The petitioners challenged the said three orders (date of the orders are 16-2-2006, 7-10- 2007 and 19-2-2008) before the High Court Division by filing Writ Petition No.2535 of 2008.

3. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that Rule was issued calling upon the respondents, namely, the decree-holder-Bank and the Adalat to show cause as to why the order of war- rant of arrest issued under section 34( 1) of the Ain, 2003 passed by the Adalat on 7-10-2007 in the execution case without compliance of the provisions laid down in section 34(9) of the Ain, 2003 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

4. The decree-holder-Bank contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition supporting the order dated 7-10-2007 passed by the Adalat issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioners and further stating that the order dated 16-2-2006 was passed by the Adalat on the basis of application filed by the petitioners, but they failed to comply with the said order. As the petitioners failed to pay the installments pursuant to the order dated 16-2-2006, the Adalat rightly passed the order dated 7-10-2007 on the application filed by the decree-holder-Bank; whether the petitioners filed the application on 16-2- 1996 or not is a disputed question of fact which cannot be decided in a writ petition.

5. The main contention of the pensioners before the High Court Division was that without complying the provision of section 34(9) of the Ain, 2003, the Adalat was not justified in issuing the war- rant of arrest against them. A Division Bench of the High Court Division discharged the Rule by the judgment and order dated 10-1-2010; hence this petition for leave to appeal.

Civil Petition No.434 of 2011;-

6. Facts giving rise to this leave petition are as follows:-

Respondent No.2, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Bank) on 23-11- 1997 filed Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna (hereinafter referred to as the Adalat) against the petitioners under the provisions of President's Order No.129 of 1972 for realization of its outstanding loan amounting to Taka 2,06,37,235/-. The said miscellaneous case was allowed ex-parte by order dated 7-5-2000. Challenging the ex-parte order, the petitioners filed Writ Petition No.3646 of 2000 before the High Court Division and a Rule was issued in that writ petition. Rule in the said writ petition was made absolute declaring the ex-parte order allowing the miscellaneous case to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Thereafter, on 26-11-2002, the Bank filed an application under section 151 read with Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) before the Adalat for amendment of the petition of Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997. The application was rejected on 25-3-2003 as no one appeared when the application was taken up for hearing. Then, on 10-4-2003, the Bank filed another application under section 151 read with Order VI, rule 17 of the Code for amendment of the petition of Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997 and the Adalat allowed the prayer on the same date vide order No.47. By that order, the Adalat directed to register the miscellaneous case as Artha Rin suit and fixed 28-4-2003 for depositing court fees and necessary requisites. Order No.48 dated 28-4-2003 shows that the Bank deposited the court fees of Taka 40;250 on that date and 8- 6-2003 was fixed for-filing necessary requisites. Eventually, by order- No.59 dated 10-11-2003, the Adalat decreed the Artha Rin suit ex-parte. Against the ex-parte decree; the petitioners moved up to this Division, but failed. The petitioners filed the instant writ petition (Writ Petition No.5889 of 2008) challenging the 3 (three) orders: (i) dated 10-4-2003 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997 (ii) orders dated 28-4-2003 and 10-11-2003 passed in Artha Rin Suit No.43 of 2003 on the ground of discovery of an "application dated 05-4-2003 filed by the respondent No.2" claiming those orders to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

7. From the writ petition, it appears that the petitioners challenged the said 3(three) orders on the contention that since the miscellaneous case filed under the provisions of President's Order No.129 of 1972 ultimately stood dismissed by the judgment and order of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.3646 of 2003 on the ground that the Sub-ordinate Judge or the Artha Rin Adalat had no jurisdiction to try any case under President's Order No. 129 of 1972, the conversion of the said miscellaneous case into an Artha Rin suit by the impugned orders was illegal and, as such, the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 43 of 2003 on 10-11-2003 was illegal and without jurisdiction. The Rule was issued as per terms of the prayer.

8. It further appears that though there were two petitioners in the writ petition, a supplementary affidavit was filed on behalf of petitioner No.1 only reiterating the stand taken in the writ petition and mentioning the relevant provisions of the two laws, namely: the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and the Ain, 2003 and the number of the leave petition being No.1856 of 2007 filed before this Division against the order passed in Writ Petition No.9624 of 2007 summarily rejecting the same.

9. The respondent-Bank contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition supporting the impugned orders. The main contention raised in the affidavit-in-opposition was that the ex-parte decree passed in the Artha Rin suit having been maintained up to this Division, there was no scope of challenging the same again by filing new writ petition on the ground of "discovery of an application dated 05-4- 2003 filed by the respondent No.2."

10. A Division Bench (not the same Bench which heard and disposed of Writ Petition No. 2535 of2008) by the judgment and order dated 3-2-2011 discharged the Rule with cost; hence this leave petition.

11. Mr. SN Goswami, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners in both leave petitions, has submitted that the respective impugned judgment and order was passed by the respective writ Bench on misconception of the provisions of sections 6(2), 8, 33, 34(9) and 57 of the Ain, 2003 and also on misconception of the facts of the case and as such, those are liable to be interfered with by this Division by giving leave.

12. From the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.2535 of 2008 giving rise to Leave Petition No.648 of 2010, it appears that the High Court Division discharged the Rule on two grounds: first being that the writ petition was not maintainable. In holding so, the learned Judges took notice of the fact that the petitioners denied about the filing of application under section 49(1) of the Ain, 2003 before the Adalat which was absolutely question of fact and such question of fact could not be decided in writ jurisdiction. For this proposition, the High Court Division relied on a decision of this Division in the case of Abdul Hamid Khan vs Mia Nurul lslam 42 DLR(AD) 49; second ground being that the provision of section 34(9) of the Ain, 2003. "does not invite any auction sale rather it invites an issuance of the process of auction sale by the court concerned which is found in the proceeding because the step of publication of notice under section 33(4) has been taken which means that process under section 33 have been already complied with."

13. Let us see whether the learned Judges were correct in taking the said views.

14. So far as the first ground is concerned, it appears that in para-7 of the writ petition, the petitioners stated that:-

"7. That it is stated that to use the name of the petitioner's decree holder bank filed the application dated on 16-2-2006 and obtained the Order and also beyond the knowledge of the petitioner's decree holder bank obtained the Order dated on 16-2-2006 and 7-10-2007 frequently(sic). "

In the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Bank despite no specific reply being given to the statements made in the said paragraph, in other paragraphs thereof it was stated that the petitioner himself filed the application dated 16-2-2006. Thus, the filing of an application by petitioner No.2 on 16-2- 2006 became a disputed question of fact and the same could not be thrashed out without taking evidence, so the High Court Division was perfectly correct in taking the said view.

15. Now, second ground: Section 33 of the Ain, 2003 has dealt with auction sale (নিলাম বিক্রয়). In section 33, there are 9(nine) sub-sections. Sub-sections (1)-(4) of the section have dealt with the procedure of auction sale of a property in execution of a decree. Sub-section (5) has dealt with the power of the executing Court to give the decree-holder the right to possess and enjoy the property to be sold in auction and also to authorize the decree-holder to sell such property and issuance of certificate to the decree-holder to the above effect in case the property cannot be sold under sub-sections (1), (2), (3) and (4) of the section. Section 7 has dealt with the power of the executing Court to give certificate of ownership to the decree-holder-Bank in case it applies for such ownership in the circumstances as contemplated therein. Sub-section (8) has stipulated that no tax and registration fee would be necessary in case a certificate is given under sub-section (7) and sub- section (9) thereof has stipulated as to how the execution case shall be disposed of in case the right to possess and enjoy the property and the certificate of ownership is given under sub-sections (5) and (7) of the section. Sub-section (6) has dealt with how the excess money if fetched more than the decretal amount in selling the property in auction shall be adjusted and how the decretal amount shall be realized from the judgment-debtor(s) in case the property is sold at a price less than the decretal amount.

16. Section 34 of the Ain, 2003, has dealt with civil detention. Sub-section (l) thereof has empowered the Adalat to issue a warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtor(s) for detaining him in civil jail for a maximum period of 6(six) months if he/it fails to make payment of the decretal amount subject to sub-section (12) of the section of the Ain, 2003. Sub-section (12) of section 34 of the Ain, 2003 reads as follows:-

(১২) এই আইনের অধীনে কোন ডিক্রী বা আদেশ বাস্তবায়নের উদ্দেশ্যে পরিচালিত জারী মামলায় সংখ্যা একাধিক হইলেও, কোন একজন দায়িককে গ্রেফতার করিয়া পরিপূর্ণ মেয়াদের জন্য একবার দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক রাখা হইলে, তাহাকে পূনর্বার গ্রেফতার করা ও দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করা যাইবে না।

17. In the facts of the present case sub-section (12) is not relevant. It is sub-section (9) which is relevant, the sub-section reads as follows:-

(৯) এই ধারার অধীনে আদালত কোন দায়িককে দেওয়ানী কারাগারে আটক করার আদেশ প্রদান করিবে না, যদি না তৎপূর্বে অন্ততঃ একটি নিলাম বিক্রয় কার্যক্রম অনুষ্ঠিত হইয়া থাকে এবং উহার দ্বারা ডিক্রীদারের প্রাপ্য পরিপূর্ণভাবে আদায় হইয়া থাকে।

<u>18. A reading of section 34(9) of the Ain, 2003 shows that the Adalat shall not pass any order of civil detention until process of holding of auction sale of the property of the judgment-debtor(s) has been resorted to at least once. In sub-section (I) of section 34 of the Ain, 2003, it has been provided that power under this sub-section can be exercised subject to sub-section (12) of the section; a reading of sub-section (9) of the section also shows that power under sub-section (1) thereof cannot be exercised unless the conditions as stipulated therein are fulfilled. So it is necessary to see whether before issuing the warrant of arrest under sub-section (1) of section 34 vide the impugned order dated 7-10- 2007, there was compliance of sub-section (9) of section 34.</u>

19. Order sheets of the execution case have been annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Bank. On perusal of the order sheets, it appears that the Adalat by order No.15 dated 14-11-2005 allowed the prayer of the decree-holder to publish the notice of the auction in two newspapers: one in the 'Daily Naya Diganta' and the other in the local daily newspaper' Janabarta' fixing the next date on 13-1-2006 for filing the copy of the newspaper and objection if any. On 13-1-2006 in place of two newspapers one paper, i.e. the national daily newspaper 'Daily Naya Diganta' was filed by the decree- holder, but Nilam Istehar was not returned and no auction bid was also submitted and the next date for auction sale was fixed on 25-1-2006 and also for the return of 'Nilam Istehar' and for filing the daily local newspaper' Janabarta.' The order dated 25-1- 2006 reads as follows:-

অদ্য পুনঃ নিলাম ও জনবার্তা পত্রিকা দাখিলের জন্য ইস্তেহার ফেরতের জন্য দিন ধার্য্য আছে। নিলাম ডাকে কেহ অংশ গ্রহণ করে নাই। জনবার্তা পত্রিকার কপি দাখিল করে নাই।আগামী ইং ১৬-২-২০০৬ তারিখ পুনঃ নিলাম এবং পত্রিকায় কপি দাখিল। ইস্তেহার ইস্যু করা হোক। ধার্য্য তারিখ নিলাম না হইলে ৩৩(৪) অথবা ৩৩(৭) ধারার তদ্বীয়।

20. From the order dated 25-1-2006, it is clear that steps were taken to sell the property of the judgment-debtors in open auction, but the auction could not be held on the date and then the next date was fixed on 16-2-2006 for holding the auction in default to take steps under sub-sections (4) and (7) of section 33. So there was clear compliance of the condition as stipulated in sub-section (9) of section 34. In addition to this on 16-2-2006, i.e. the date fixed for holding re-auction sale, filing of Nilam Istehar and newspaper in default to take step under section 33(4) or 33(7), judgment-debtor No.2 filed an application under section 49(1) of the Ain, 2003 to allow the judgment-debtors to pay the decretal amount in 4(four) installments in a year and-accordingly, the Adalat allowed the prayer fixing the last date for paying the installment on 25-1-2007, but they failed to pay the decretal amount. Thereafter, the Bank filed an application for issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioners and the prayer was allowed.

21. In view of the above, we find no illegality with ground No.2 as quoted hereinbefore on which Rule in Writ Petition No.2533 of 2008 was discharged.

<u>22. From the impugned judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 5889 of2008 giving rise to Leave Petition No. 434 of 2011, it appears that the Rule was discharged on the ground of maintainability of the writ petition. In finding the writ petition not maintainable, the learned Judges considered that the orders impugned in the writ petition were earlier challenged in Writ Petition No.9624 of 2007 which was summarily rejected on the finding that there was no illegality in the orders; challenging the summary rejection of the writ petition, the petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1856 of 2007 before this Division and the leave petition was dismissed and thus, the order passed in Writ Petition No.9624 of 2007 was upheld. When the orders challenged in the instant writ petition (Writ Petition No.5889 of 2008) were found legal up to this Division, those could not be challenged afresh on the plea of discovery of "an application dated 5- 4-2003 filed by the respondent No.2." If such practice is allowed, there will be no end of litigation and the other side(s) shall be subjected to the unnecessary harassment particularly, when the matter arises out of a decree passed in an Artha Rin suit. In the context, the High Court Division took the correct view in finding the writ petition not maintainable. Therefore, we find no ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No.5889 of 2008.</u>

In view of the above, both leave petitions are dismissed.

End.
